READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Ezekiel 5:2-4
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:2-4 Ezekiel's hair (usually a sign of religious devotion, cf. Numbers 6; Judges 16-17; 2 Sam. 10:4-5) was to be shaved, divided, and disposed of in specific ways.

  1. one-third burned at the center of the city (i.e. the model of Jerusalem of chapter 4) when Jerusalem falls, Ezek. 5:2
  2. one-third cut with the sword all around the city (i.e. the model of Jerusalem of chapter 4), Ezek. 5:2
  3. one-third scattered to the wind, Ezek. 5:2 (i.e. the scattering of exiles)
  4. a few hairs were tied into Ezekiel's robe, Ezek. 5:3
  5. a few hairs put in a fire, which will spread to all Judah, Ezek. 5:4 (fire is often used in Ezekiel as a judgment of God, cf. Ezek. 5:2,4; 10:2,6-7; 15:4-7; 16:41; 19:12,14; 20:47-48; 21:31-32; 23:25,47; 24:10,12; 30:8,14,16; 39:6

The symbolic act seems to mean that one-third of the inhabitants of Jerusalem will be killed by the sword, one-third will be killed by famine and one-third will be scattered among the nations (cf. Ezek. 5:2).

In Ezek. 5:3 the concept of remnant appears, which occurs throughout the OT in God's dealing with His rebellious covenant people (cf. 2 Kgs. 25:22; Isa. 6:13; 10:22; Jer. 23:3; Ezek. 5:3; 6:8-10; 11:13; Zech. 13:8, 9).

SPECIAL TOPIC: FIRE

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE REMNANT, three senses

entries.title: Ezekiel 5:5
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:5 This verse affirms the purposeful plan of God to place His people where they must depend on His care and protection. They were not a large, powerful people (cf. Deut. 7:7), but their land was at the crossroads of the major Near Eastern powers of Babylon, Assyria, Anatolia, and Egypt.

God wanted to use His people planted in such a prominent place to educate and draw the surrounding peoples (i.e. "the nations) to Himself (cf. Deut. 4:6-8, see The Prophecy of Ezekiel by Feinberg, p. 37). Because of Israel's disobedience, all they (i.e. the nations) saw was the judgment of God (cf. Ezek. 5:7-9; 36:22-36).

▣ "at the center of the nations" When this phrase is seen in light of

  1. Ezek. 38:12
  2. the use of the imagery of "navel" in Near Eastern religion (cf. NIDOTTE, vol. 2, pp. 333-334)

it becomes a significant theological statement. YHWH's people were the revelatory epicenter of the world. His eternal, universal, redemptive plan involved them. Their continuing covenant unfaithfulness was a major barrier to revealing His faithful character, which will be expressed in the "New Covenant," which is not based on human performance (cf. Jer. 31:31-34; Ezek. 36:22-36).

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

entries.title: Ezekiel 5:6-7 "statutes. . .ordinances"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:6-7 "statutes. . .ordinances" See Ezek. 5:6, 7 .

SPECIAL TOPIC: TERMS FOR GOD'S REVELATION

5:7
NASB  "you have more turmoil"
NKJV  "your have multiplied disobedience more"
NRSV  "you are more turbulent"
TEV  "you have caused more trouble"
NJB  "your disorders are worse"
JPSOA  "you have outdone"
REB  "you have been more insubordinate"
NET  "you are more arrogant"

This NOUN form appears only here in the OT (BDB 243, KB 632, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT). Its basic meaning may be

  1. to rebel
  2. to raze
  3. to be turbulent
  4. Some scholars assert that it comes from a different root meaning "to disdain" or "to be weak."
▣
NASB  "you have not walked. . .nor observed" (twice)
LXX, NKJV, Peshitta  "have not walked in. . .nor kept"
NRSV  "not followed. . .or kept"
TEV  "by not obeying. . .or keeping"
NJB  "you do not keep. . .or respect"
REB  "have not conformed. . .have not kept"
JPSOA  "you have not obeyed. . .or followed"

The MT has the negative (לא) twice, but the RSV leaves out the negatives. The UBS Text Project, p. 10, gives the MT a "B" rating. The only English translation that removes the two "nots" is the RSV, which follows some Hebrew and Syriac manauscripts.

Because of the last phrase of this verse, Ezek. 5:6, and 16:27, this phrase must mean that Judah sinned worse than the surrounding nations! Her idolatries reached new heights!

entries.title: Ezekiel 5:8 "I, even I"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:8 "I, even I" This is very emphatic! YHWH will act against Israel to maintain the truthfulness of His own revelation. The covenant God acts against the covenant people!

God wanted to reach all nations through Israel. She was the means, not the goal!

▣ "I will execute judgment among you in the sight of the nations" It must be remembered that Israel was called to be "a kingdom of priests" (cf. Exod. 19:5,6). She will be a testimony, either positively or negatively (cf. Ezek. 5:15; Ezek. 36:23-36).

entries.title: Ezekiel 5:9
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 5:9 God will execute judgment against His own covenant people more severely than other judgments because Israel knew Him, knew His will and yet violated them (cf. Luke 12:48; Rom. 9:4-5)!

entries.title: Ezekiel 5:10 "the fathers will eat their sons"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:10 "the fathers will eat their sons" This is one of the horrors of siege warfare. It was foretold in Lev. 26:29 and Deut. 28:53. The cannibalism is predicted in Jer. 19:9 and fulfilled in Lam. 2:20 and 4:10. Flavius Josephus also tells us of the same horrendous acts occurring in the siege of Jerusalem by Titus in A.D. 70.

▣ "scatter all your remnant to every wind" The concept of remnant was alluded to in Ezek. 5:3.

This VERB (BDB 279, KB 280, Piel PERFECT with waw) refers literally to winnowing grain (i.e. separating the husk and grain), but it is often used as imagery of judgment (i.e. exile, cf. Deut. 30:15-16; 31:15-16; Ezek. 20:23). God's very own people become the "husk"!

Notice it is YHWH, not the nations, who scatters His people (cf. Ezek. 5:10,12; 6:8; 12:14-15; 20:23; 22:15; 36:19). It was not the power of the gods of the nations or their military, but the righteous judgment of YHWH that scatters His people for breaking the covenant (cf. Leviticus 26; Deuteronomy 28).

SPECIAL TOPIC: REMNANT (three senses)

entries.title: Ezekiel 5:11 "So as I live declares the Lord God"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:11 "So as I live declares the Lord God" This is an oath used fourteen times in Ezekiel. It is a play on the word YHWH (i.e. a form of the VERB "to be"), which means "the only-living, ever-living God." God is true to His word (i.e. Isa. 55:9-11)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

▣ "because you have defiled My sanctuary" This is described in detail in chapter 8 (cf. Ezek. 9:7; 23:38; 43:6-9).

▣ "abominations" See SPECIAL TOPIC: ABOMINATION

NASB  "I will also withdraw"
NKJV  "I will also diminish you"
NRSV, TEV  "I will cut you down"
NJB, LXX  "I too shall reject you"
JPSOA  "I in turn will shear [you] away"
REB  "I in turn shall destroy you"
Peshitta  "I will scatter away"

This refers to

  1. Ezekiel's vision of the glory of YHWH and His Spirit leaving the temple in Jerusalem and moving east to be with the exiles (cf. chapters 8-11)
  2. YHWH shearing Israel (cf. Ezek. 5:1; same VERB, BDB 175, KB 203, used of "shaving" in Isa. 15:2; Jer. 48:37)

There is some question about what this VERB (BDB 175, KB 203, Qal IMPERFECT) means. The basic meaning is to

  1. diminish (cf. Exod. 5:8,19; Deut. 4:2; Jer. 26:2)
  2. restrain (cf. Job 15:4,8; Niphal Num. 9:7)
  3. withdraw (cf. Job. 36:7; Niphal Num. 36:3,4)
  4. cut down (see NRSV, TEV, JPSOA, relating back to the shaving of Ezek. 5:1-2)

The results of YHWH abandoning His own temple is a complete rejection of the inhabitants of Jerusalem as His people. Notice He will

  1. have no pity, BDB 299, KB 298, Qal IMPERFECT, cf. Ezek. 7:9; 8:18; 9:5,10
  2. not spare, BDB 328, KB 328, Qal IMPERFECT, cf. Ezek. 7:9; 8:18; 9:5,10

Instead of the promise of great numbers of Israelites (i.e. stars, sand, dust; see full note at Gen. 13:16), YHWH will extensively reduce their numbers until only a remnant is left (cf. Ezek. 5:3).

▣ "My eye" This is an anthropomorphic way of referring to God's personal attention to His covenant people.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PROBLEMS AND LIMITATIONS OF HUMAN LANGUAGE

entries.title: Ezekiel 5:13
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:13 Notice all the "My's" in this verse! They denote YHWH's personal righteous character.

  1. My anger (BDB 60)
  2. My wrath (BDB 404)
  3. My zeal (or "jealousy," BDB 888; see SPECIAL TOPIC: JEALOUSY, ZEAL)
  4. My wrath (BDB 404)
NASB, REB  "I shall be appeased"
NKJV  "I will be avenged"
NRSV  "satisfy myself"
TEV  "until I am satisfied"
NJB  "I have sated my fury"
LXX  "when I spend my anger"
JPSOA  "when I vent all My fury"
Peshitta  "I will be comforted"

The VERB (BDB 636, KB 688, Hithpael PERFECT with waw) in this stem can have several meanings.

  1. "be sorry" or "have compassion," cf. Deut. 32:36 (which does not fit this context)
  2. "rue" or "repent," cf. Num. 23:19 (which does not fit this context)
  3. "comfort oneself," cf. Gen. 37:35; Ps. 119:52 (which could fit)
  4. "ease oneself by taking vengeance," cf. Gen. 27:42 (by planning evil); also this same connotation is expressed in the Niphal stem (cf. Isa. 1:24). This does fit the context best!

God's anger will cease after His judgment (cf. Ezek. 16:42; 21:17; 24:13). His purpose is an obedient people, not a settled wrath! His acts of judgment are meant to restore, not totally annihilate!

Also note that it is not the people's repentance, but YHWH's mercy that limits and concludes judgment!

▣ "in My zeal" This NOUN (BDB 888) is translated "ardor," "zeal," and "jealousy." Therefore, it could be understood as

  1. YHWH jealous for His word
  2. YHWH jealous for His covenant people.

Judah had violated YHWH's covenant and YHWH's love!

SPECIAL TOPIC: JEALOUSY, ZEAL

entries.title: Ezekiel 5:14-15
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:14-15 This reflects Deut. 28:37. Moses told the people of Israel that if they kept the Mosaic Covenant they would be blessed, but if they broke it they would be cursed (cf. Lev. 26).

Notice the list of things YHWH will do to His disobedient covenant people.

  1. "I will make you a desolation," Ezek. 5:14 (BDB 352, a place of waste and ruin)
  2. "a reproach among the nations," Ezek. 5:14 (BDB 357, a shame, disgrace, scorn, cf. Ezek. 5:15)
  3. "a reviling," Ezek. 5:15 (BDB 154, this FEMININE NOUN form is found only here and means a taunt or someone as the object of blasphemous words)
  4. "a warning," Ezek. 5:15 (BDB 416, "chastening" or "chastisement of God")
  5. "an object of horror," Ezek. 5:15 (BDB 1031, "appalling object," horror," cf. Deut. 28:37; Jer. 25:9,11,18,38)

Notice how God describes His coming judgments (i.e. Ezek. 5:15)

  1. in anger (BDB 60, cf. Ezek. 5:13)
  2. in wrath (BDB 404, cf. Ezek. 5:13[twice])
  3. in raging rebukes (BDB 407 CONSTRUCT 404, cf. Ezek. 25:17)

YHWH acts against disobedient Judah as a witness to the nations of His righteous character (i.e. Ezek. 5:14-15; 36:22-38). It has always been YHWH's plan to reveal Himself through Israel (cf. Gen. 12:3; Exod. 19:5-6; see SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN). He wanted it to be in blessing, but if necessary, He will witness in judgment!

SPECIAL TOPIC: HORROR, REPROACH, CURSE

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

5:15
NASB, NKJV  "it"
NRSV, TEV, NJB, REB, JPSOA, LXX, Peshitta, Targums, Vulgate, DSS  "you"

The MT has "it shall be" (BDB 224, KB 243, Qal PERFECT with waw, FEMININE SINGULAR), which refers to Jerusalem. Here, the city stands for God's people, set by Him among the nations as a witness (cf. v. 5). Even the exiles were used by YHWH to spread His name among the nations.

The UBS Text Project, p. 11, gives "you" a "C" rating.

entries.title: Ezekiel 5:16
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:16 The MT, at the beginning of v. 16, has "against them," both "them" and "you," but the verse implies has "you," which fits the context better. The UBS Text Project, p. 11, thinks "them" is original (i.e. "B" rating).

▣ "and break the staff of bread" The term "staff" (BDB 641), following its usages with Moses' staff (i.e. God's power in the hands of Moses), may be an idiom for a divine supply. Therefore, in this context it is parallel to famine. This phrase is used several times (cf. Lev. 26:26; Ps. 105:16; Ezek. 4:16; 5:16; 14:13).

entries.title: Ezekiel 5:16-17
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:16-17 These verses continue the items of destruction mentioned in Leviticus 26 and Deuteronomy 28. YHWH is true to His word (cf. Ezek. 5:17c).

Note the litany of judgments.

  1. the deadly arrows of famine, Ezek. 5:16,17; Deut. 28:20-26
  2. wild beasts, Ezek. 5:17 (cf. Lev. 26:22; Deut. 32:24)
  3. plague, Ezek. 5:17 (cf. Lev. 26:21)
  4. bloodshed, Ezek. 5:17
  5. sword, Ezek. 5:17

These were meant to turn His people back to Him in repentance and faith (cf. Deuteronomy 28; 30:1-10).

entries.title: Ezekiel 5:17 "they will bereave you of children"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:17 "they will bereave you of children" The wild beasts will kill the children of the disobedient Jerusalemites. Notice, like David's first child with Bathsheba, the children pay the price for their parent's sin (cf. Deut. 5:9). However, please note Deut. 5:10 and 7:9. His love reaches to "a thousand generations"! Judgment is God's strange work (cf. Isa. 28:21; Lam. 3:33).

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

  1. What does the scroll of chapter 2 represent? Why was it sweet as honey in his mouth, chapter 3, Ezek. 5:3?
  2. Why did God send a prophet to His people whom He knew would not listen?
  3. What do the symbolic acts of chapters 4 and 5 represent?
  4. What is the major message that Ezekiel is trying to convey to the exiles in Babylon?

entries.title: Ezekiel 6:1
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 6:1 These prophecies and symbolic actions were not from Ezekiel, but from YHWH. Ezekiel is but a mouthpiece for God (cf. Ezek. 1:3; 3:16; 7:1).

The Sins of Israel

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Ezekiel 6:2 "Son of man"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:2 "Son of man" This is a Hebrew idiom for "human person." See full note at Ezek. 2:1.

Ezekiel is instructed to

  1. "set his face towards the mountain," BDB 962, KB 1321, Qal IMPERATIVE (a standard phrase of judgment oracles, cf. Ezek. 13:17; 20:46; 21:2; 25:2; 29:2; 35:2; 38:2)
  2. "prophesy against them," BDB 612, KB 659, Niphal IMPERATIVE

SPECIAL TOPIC: SON OF MAN

▣ "the mountains" This had a multiple connotations.

  1. the most permanent physical feature
  2. part of God's promised land in Judah and Samaria
  3. a place of refuge
  4. places of fertility worship (cf. Ezek. 6:13)

In context #4 fits best. The mountains are personified and commanded to hear the word of the Lord (here, Adon, cf. Ezek. 6:2,11; 5:5,7,8,11; 7:2,5).

SPECIAL TOPIC: Lord (adon and kuiros)

entries.title: Ezekiel 6:3 "listen to the word of the Lord God"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:3 "listen to the word of the Lord God" The VERB (BDB 1033, KB 1570, Qal IMPERATIVE ) is often used in a legal sense of testimony in a trial. Judah is responsible for the words they hear! The prophets often used a court scene as a literary mechanism to communicate their message of covenant negation (i.e. divorce case).

SPECIAL TOPIC: LISTEN/HEAR (shema)

▣ "the Lord God" This is literally Adon YHWH.

SPECIAL TOPIC: LORD (adon and kurios)

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

▣ "I Myself" This is reminiscent of Ezek. 5:13. It is God Himself who acts through the human instrumentality of Neo-Babylon (as He did Assyria, cf. Isa. 10:5). Later, God will call and use Cyrus II (i.e. Persia, cf. Isa. 44:28; 45:1) to return the exiles to Palestine. History is in YHWH's hands, for His purposes!

▣ "your high places" This man-made, raised altar (the one at Megiddo was 6' tall by 24' x 30') was used for the worship of the Canaanite fertility gods (i.e. Ba'al and Asherah, cf. Ezek. 6:13).

YHWH hates the false worship of non-existent gods (see Roland deVaux, Ancient Israel, vol. 2, pp. 284-288).

SPECIAL TOPIC: FERTILITY WORSHIP of the ANE

SPECIAL TOPIC: IDOLATRY

entries.title: Ezekiel 6:4 "incense altars"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:4 "incense altars" This term (BDB 329) is uncertain. Here are the possibilities from Canaanite sites (cf. 2 Kgs. 16:4)

  1. incense altar
  2. sun-pillar (cf. 2 Chr. 34:4 in ASV)
  3. sanctuary of a foreign god (NIDOTTE, vol. 2, p. 903)

The best option is #1 (cf. R. K. Harrison, Introduction to the Old Testament, p. 365, footnote 23).

▣ "idols" This term (BDB 165) is uncertain in etymology. It is used often in Ezekiel to refer to Canaanite idols. Verses 4 and 6 have a series of six Niphal PERFECTS. YHWH's judgment on pagan worship sites and worshipers in Israel is shockingly graphic!

SPECIAL TOPIC: CONSEQUENCES OF IDOLATRY

entries.title: Ezekiel 6:4-7
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 6:4-7 These verses describe the result of the Neo-Babylonian mercenary army invading and destroying all the cities, worship sites, and idols of Judah. The locals may have fled to their worship sites to be saved by their gods. But. their idols could not deliver them and they were slain and unburied all about the temples and worship sites. Their idols and raised platforms were also destroyed.

entries.title: Ezekiel 6:6 "altars"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:6 "altars" Apparently these man-made worship platforms contained several items.

  1. raised stone (massebah, BDB 663) representing Ba'al, the male fertility god
  2. carved or live tree representing Asherah (BDB 81), the female goddess
  3. incense altar (cf. Lev. 26:30; 2 Chr. 14:3; 34:4,7; Isa. 27:9)

entries.title: Ezekiel 6:7 "you will know that I am the Lord"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:7 "you will know that I am the Lord" This is a recurrent phrase in Ezekiel which denotes the personal judgment of YHWH (i.e. Ezek. 6:10,13,14 and over 50 more times in the book of Ezekiel).

The phrase first appears as a repeated refrain in Exodus (cf. Exod. 6:7; 7:5; 16:6; 29:46). YHWH acts on His covenant people's behalf so they will know (BDB 393,KB 390, in personal intimacy) Him, but in Ezekiel they will know Him in covenant justice. He will act according to His word!

SPECIAL TOPIC: KNOW

▣ YHWH will pollute idolatrous worship sites (cf. Lev. 26:30) by

  1. their physical destruction (cf. Ezek. 6:6)
  2. unburied bodies in their locale (cf. Ezek. 6:7)
  3. dead bodies in their locale (cf. Ezek. 6:13)

entries.title: Ezekiel 6:8 "I shall leave a remnant"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 6:8 "I shall leave a remnant" See note and Special Topic: The Remnant, Three Senses.

entries.title: Ezekiel 6:9
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:9 There is hope! A remnant will repent by remembering and returning to YHWH (cf. Deut. 30:1-6).

  1. "will remember Me"
  2. how I (i.e. YHWH) have been hurt by their adulterous hearts which turned away from Me
  3. by their eyes, which played the harlot after their idols
  4. they will loathe themselves in their own sight (cf. Ezek. 16:61,63; 20:43; 36:31)

Notice the personal element of idolatrous sin. YHWH also felt a personal rejection. Sin is a personal violation of the grace of God! Biblical faith is a love relationship.

▣ "their abominations" See SPECIAL TOPIC: ABOMINATION (OT)

entries.title: Ezekiel 6:10
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 6:10 Judgment is an act of love. Mankind's only permanent hope is a personal faith relationship with the one true God. The best way to view divine discipline is in the analogy of a human parent (cf. Heb. 12:5-13).

entries.title: Ezekiel 6:11
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:11 There are three symbolic acts of recognition

  1. "clap your hands," BDB 645, KB 697, Hiphil IMPERATIVE
  2. "stamp your feet," BDB 955, KB 1291, Qal IMPERATIVE (usually #1 and 2 refer to rejoicing, cf. Ezek. 25:6)
  3. "say, 'Alas,'" BDB 55, KB 65, Qal IMPERATIVE (cf. Ezek. 9:4, a sign of repentance)

It is difficult to be certain what these three taken together mean. They seem to be a recognition of the appropriateness of YHWH's judgment, but also the tragedy of it.

James M. Freeeman, Manners and Customs of the Bible, notes five different meanings to clapping of the hands (p. 305).

  1. sign of contempt, Job 27:33; Lam. 2:15
  2. sign of anger, Num. 24:10; Ezek. 21:14,17; 22:13
  3. sign of sorrow, Ezek. 6:11
  4. sign of triumph, Ezek. 25:6; Nah. 3:19
  5. sign of a pledge, Gen. 14:22 (if "lift the hand" is related to "clap the hands"); Prov. 11:21 and possibly Ezek. 21:14,17

For a good brief discussion see IVP Biblical Background Commentary (OT), p. 694.

entries.title: Ezekiel 6:12 "He who is far off"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:12 "He who is far off" This phrasing ("those far off. . .those near. . .") is often used in a positive sense (i.e. Ps. 145:18; Isa. 55:6), but here it is just the opposite. Everyone will experience the judgment of YHWH.

▣ "plague. . .sword. . .famine" These are the three triads of YHWH's judgment (cf. Ezek. 14:12; 24:10; 27:8,13; 29:17,18). Ezekiel 14:21 adds the Levitical and Deuteronomic curse of "wild beasts" (cf. Lev. 26:22; Deut. 32:24).

entries.title: Ezekiel 6:13 "Then you will know that I am the Lord"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:13 "Then you will know that I am the Lord" The phrase is used in both a negative and positive sense, both of which relate to the disobedience or obedience to YHWH's revealed will (i.e. word).

  1. negative, Ezek. 6:13; 7:27; 11:10; 12:16
  2. positive, Ezek. 34:27,30; 37:13,14,28

In Jeremiah it is related to Israel's witness to the surrounding nations (cf. Jer. 22:8-9). This is reaffirmed in Ezek. 37:28.

SPECIAL TOPIC: KNOW

▣ "on every high hill, on all the tops of the mountains, under every green tree, and under every leafy oak" These were the physical locations of Canaanite fertility altars (cf. Ezek. 20:28; Deut. 12:2; 1 Kgs. 14:23; 2 Kgs. 16:4; 17:10; 2 Chr. 28:4; Isa. 57:5; Jer. 2:20; 3:6,13; 17:2; Hosea 4:13).

▣ "the places where they offered soothing aroma to all their idols" The phrase "soothing aroma" (BDB 629) was an idiom for an acceptable animal sacrifice (cf. Gen. 8:21; Exod. 29:18,25,41; Lev. 1:9,13,17). As the smoke of the sacrifice rose up, it symbolically left this physical realm and ascended to God. Ezekiel takes this sacrificial idiom and turns it on its head (another idiom) and uses it of pagan sacrifices offered by Jerusalemites and Judeans (cf. Ezek. 6:13; 16:19; 20:28).

SPECIAL TOPIC: A SOOTHING AROMA

entries.title: Ezekiel 6:36 "because of the blood of your sons which you gave to idols"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:36 "because of the blood of your sons which you gave to idols" This refers to the worship of Molech.

SPECIAL TOPIC: BLOOD

SPECIAL TOPIC: MOLECH

entries.title: Ezekiel 6:14 "I shall stretch out My hand"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:14 "I shall stretch out My hand" This phrase is characteristic of the book of Ezekiel (cf. Ezek. 14:9,13; 16:27; 25:7; 35:3), but is also found in Jeremiah (cf. Jer. 6:12; 15:6). It denotes YHWH's action.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PROBLEMS AND LIMITATIONS OF HUMAN LANGUAGE

NASB, NKJV, JPSOA, Peshitta, Vulgate  "Diblah"
NRSV, TEV, NJB, REB  "Riblah"
LXX  "Deblatha"

Diblah was a city in the Negev, but "Riblah" (cf. 2 Kgs. 23:33; 25:6), is in northern Israel (cf. Num. 34:11). The whole point of the phrase, which probably should be "the wilderness to Riblah" (see UBS Text Project note on p. 14) is to denote the whole Promised Land from south to north. This would be similar to the phrase "from Dan to Beersheba."

Copyright © 2014 Bible Lessons International

entries.title: Ezekiel 7:1 "the word of the Lord came to me saying"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 7:1 "the word of the Lord came to me saying" As "Lord" (adon) was so common in chapters 5-6, here, YHWH, cf. vv. 1,2,4,5,9,19,27. This seems to be literary variety without theological significance (cf. v. 2).

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Ezekiel 7:2 "son of man"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:2 "son of man" See note at Ezek. 2:1

SPECIAL TOPIC: SON OF MAN

▣ "the land (adamah, BDB 9) of Israel" This is parallel to

  1. "the four corners of the land" (erets, BDB 75, Ezek. 7:2; see SPECIAL TOPIC: LAND, COUNTRY, EARTH)
  2. "the mountain of Israel," in Ezek. 6:2
  3. "the wilderness of Diblah/Riblah" of Ezek. 6:14.

This phrase is found only in Ezekiel (17 times, cf. NIDOTTE, vol. 1, p. 271). It seems to have the theological emphasis of the Promised Land given by YHWH to His covenant people (cf. Deut. 7:13; 11:9,21; 28:11; 30:20). This special gift, they are about to lose! As God took the Canaanites out of the land because of their evil (cf. Gen. 15:16), so too, if Israel takes on their ways (i.e. idolatry), He will remove them from the land.

▣ "an end" The time of judgment has come! This word (BDB 893) is used in Ezek. 7:2 (twice), Ezek. 7:3, Ezek. 7:6 (twice). It is also used in the sense of "climax" in Ezek. 21:25,29; 29:13; 35:5. God is in control of time and history. His patience and longsuffering are often misunderstood and abused, but there is a limit!

▣ "the four corners of the land" The word "four" is often associated with the whole earth (i.e. four directions of the compass, four winds, four corners, cf. Isa. 11:12). Here it is a play on "end." The end of time is coming to the very ends (corners) of the Promised Land.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SYMBOLIC NUMBERS IN SCRIPTURE, #2

entries.title: Ezekiel 7:3 "I shall judge you according to your ways"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:3 "I shall judge you according to your ways" This truth is repeated in Ezek. 7:8,9; 18:30; 24:19; 33:20; 36:19; 39:24. Another way to put this recurrent truth is "we reap what we sow" (cf. Job 34:11; Ps. 28:4; 62:12; Prov. 24:12; Eccl. 12:14; Jer. 17:10; 32:19; Matt. 16:27; 25:31-46; Rom. 2:6; 14:12; 1 Cor. 3:8; 2 Cor. 5:10; Gal. 6:7-10; 2 Tim. 4:14; 1 Pet. 1:17; Rev. 2:23; 20:12; 22:12).

▣ "abominations" This term (BDB 1072) is used in Ezek. 7:3, 4, 9, 20. It is used forty-three times in Ezekiel, mostly in chapters 7,8,16.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ABOMINATION (OT)

entries.title: Ezekiel 7:3-4
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 7:3-4 Verses 3-4 are repeated exactly in Ezek. 7:8-9. They form a refrain. In many ways this chapter is a lament (cf. The Prophecy of Ezekiel, by Feinberg, p. 44).

entries.title: Ezekiel 7:4 "For My eye will have no pity on you"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:4 "For My eye will have no pity on you" See note at Ezek. 5:11. This is repeated in Ezek. 7:9; 8:18; 9:5,10; 24:14. It is a shocking reversal of YHWH's normal character (cf. Exod. 34:6) and acts!

▣ "then you will know that I am the Lord" See note at Ezek. 6:7. A slightly different form is in Ezek. 7:9. This chapter is like a tapestry of themes woven together to form recurrent patterns of truth.

7:5
NASB, NJB  "a unique disaster"
NKJV, JPSOA  "a singular disaster"
NRSV, Targums  "disaster after disaster"
TEV  "one disaster after another"
REB  "disasters are coming, one after another"
NET  "a one-of-a-kind disaster"

The word "unique" is literally the Hebrew word "one" (BDB 29). Translating it "unique" shows that there is theological significance to the phrase "one God" (i.e. a unique, one-of-a-kind God). Monotheism is the stark uniqueness of the OT in its Ancient Near Eastern setting!

The footnote of the Rotherham's Emphasized Bible, p. 790, mentions that the word "one" is similar to the word "after."

  1. one ‒ BDB 25, אחד
  2. after ‒ BDB 29, אחר

The Aramaic Targums translate it "Disaster after disaster."

SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM

entries.title: Ezekiel 7:6 "It has awakened"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:6 "It has awakened" The end is personified. It awakens to the activity of judgment (cf. "the sword" of Zech. 13:7).

The VERB (BDB 884, KB 1098, Hiphil PERFECT) is also used in Hab. 2:19 in sarcasm of lifeless idols. However, YHWH is not a lifeless idol; He acts!

Notice the repetition of immediate and appointed time (BDB 773) markers in Ezek. 7:6-12.

  1. the end is coming, Ezek. 7:6
  2. the end has come, Ezek. 7:6
  3. it has come, Ezek. 7:6
  4. your doom has come to you, Ezek. 7:7
  5. the time has come, Ezek. 7:7
  6. the day is near, Ezek. 7:7
  7. I will shortly pour out My wrath on you, Ezek. 7:8
  8. Behold the day! Behold, it is coming, Ezek. 7:10
  9. the time has come, Ezek. 7:12
  10. the day has arrived, Ezek. 7:12

The VERB "come" (BDB 97, KB 112, Qal PERFECT) is used eight times in these verses! This theme of immediacy is repeated in Ezek. 12:23-25,28. Number 6 is a key eschatological phrase in Amos 5:18-20; Joel; and Zephaniah.

7:7
NASB, NKJV, NRS, NJB, REB  "doom has come"
TEV  "the end is coming"
KJV  "the morning is come"
JPSOA  "the cycle has come"
LXX  "the time is come"
Peshitta  "the dawn. . .is come"

The term (BDB 862, KB 1048, #2) is also used in Ezek. 7:10. It usually means "crown" or "diadem" (cf. Isa. 28:5). Its meaning in Ezekiel 7:7,10 is uncertain.

  1. The KJV takes it from an Aramaic root "morning."
  2. Most English translations take it from an Arabic root, "doom" or "fate."

▣ "tumult" This (BDB 223, KB 552) refers to the panic (originally a divinely given military technique used against Israel's enemies, cf. Exod. 15:16; 23:27; Deut. 7:23, but also a warning to Israel that if she was disobedient to the covenant, it would happen to her military, cf. Deut. 28:20) caused by YHWH's coming in judgment (cf. Zech. 14:13). The judgment referred to is the Neo-Babylonian invasion.

This is not what YHWH desired. He wanted "joyful shouting on the mountains," but His covenant people forced Him to act in judgment because of their idolatry!

SPECIAL TOPIC: MAGIC

NASB  "joyful shouting"
NKJV, REB  "rejoicing"
NRSV  "reveling"
TEV  "celebrations"
NJB, JPSOA  "joy"

This term (BDB 212, KB 238) is found only here in the OT. Many assume it is from the root, "loud noise" (BDB 212), possibly "thunder," which in this context would refer to the sounds of the idolatrous harvest festivals (cf. Isa. 16:9c; Jer. 48:33).

entries.title: Ezekiel 7:8 "I will pour out My wrath on you"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:8 "I will pour out My wrath on you" This VERB (BDB 1049, KB 1629, Qal IMPERFECT) is used several times in Ezekiel (cf. Ezek. 9:8; 14:19; 20:8,13,21; 22:31; 30:15; 36:18). It could have several origins.

  1. In Ezek. 5:2 it is imagery for "pour out" (BDB 937, KB 1237, Hiphil IMPERFECT), translated "unsheathe a sword." It may refer to the military conquest of the Neo-Babylonian military.
  2. The concept also has a sacrificial connotation of
    1. "pour out" a libation (i.e. Gen. 35:14)
    2. "pour out" the life blood at the base of the altar of sacrifice (cf. Exod. 29:12; Lev. 8:15; 9:9)
  3. "pour out" (same root), used of idolatry in Ezek. 16:15; 23:8
  4. the opposite of the "pouring out" of the Spirit in Joel 2:28-29 (eschatological)

That which was meant to be imagery for worship and blessing has become imagery for judgment and destruction!

▣ "according to your ways" See note at Ezek. 7:3.

entries.title: Ezekiel 7:9 "I, the Lord, do the smiting"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:9 "I, the Lord, do the smiting" Normally in the Ancient Near East the defeat of one nation by another was viewed as the superiority of one national deity above another. YHWH wants it clearly understood that He uses Neo-Babylon (as He did Assyria, cf. Isa. 10:5) for His purposes. Israel's defeat is due to their covenant infidelity and idolatries, not His impotence!

John Taylor has a great statement about this phrase in Ezekiel, Tyndale OT Commentary:

"To hearers and readers who were used to names of God like 'Jehovah-jereh' and 'Jehovah-nissi' (Gen. 22:14; Ex. 17:15), it must have come home with tremendous force to have Him described as 'Jehovah-makkeh'! The Lord who had provided and protected was about to strike" (p. 93).

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D. #5

entries.title: Ezekiel 7:10-11
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:10-11 Notice the imagery of spring (i.e. budding, Israel's evil has burst into flower).

  1. "The rod has budded" (note this is where "doom" of Ezek. 7:7 can be understood as "diadem")
  2. "Arrogance has blossomed"
  3. Violence has grown into a rod of wickedness

Judah thought her unique position as YHWH's covenant people and the presence of the temple would protect her, even without obedience and faith! But this false sense of assurance (i.e. #2, arrogance) was about to be clearly rejected! I fear evangelicalism has this same false sense of security. Conservative theology must issue in Christlikeness, not self-righteousness and judgmentalism. Justification must issue in sanctification. An initial profession must issue in daily obedience and perseverance (cf. Luke 6:46; Eph. 2:8-10; James 2:14-26). The covenantal method of being accepted by God has changed from a human-performance basis (OT) to a God-performance basis (NT), but the goal of a righteous people for the purpose of fellowship with God has not. It is affected by Genesis 3. Now God wants a righteous people to help those who do not yet know Him to come to Him. The goal has always been Christlikeness! Be careful not to confuse the changing method and the unchanging goal! Also be careful of a proof-texted assurance connected solely to an initial prayer or rite!

SPECIAL TOPIC: ASSURANCE

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHRISTIAN ASSURANCE

SPECIAL TOPIC: APOSTASY

▣
NASB, NKJV, NRSV, LXX  "the rod has budded"
RSV, REB  "injustice buds"
NJB  "the sceptre has blossomed"
TEV  "violance is flourishing"
Peshitta, NET  "the staff blossomed"

The MT has "your diadem has blossomed." The NOUN "the rod" is very similar to "injustice."

  1. the rod ‒ המטה (BDB 862)
  2. injustice ‒ המטה

Only vowels are different. The UBS Text Project, p. 16, gives "the rod" an "A" rating.

Another word for "rod" (BDB 641) appears in v. 11.

entries.title: Ezekiel 7:11
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:11 Because of her sin, Jerusalem and Judah will fall.

  1. her people
  2. her wealth
  3. her eminence

Total destruction and shame!

▣
NASB  "nor anything eminent"
NKJV  "nor shall there be wailing for them"
NRSV  "no pre-eminence among them"
TEV  "or their glory"
NJB    —omit—
REB  "nothing but turmoil in them"
JPOSA  "nothing comes of them"
Peshitta  "none of them shall remain"

The meaning of "eminent" (BDB 627, KB 675) is uncertain. The form is found only here.

  1. BDB lists "eminence" and "distinction"
  2. Feinberg suggests "lamentation" or "wailing" (p. 45, i.e. no one left alive to bury or mourn the dead, cf. Ezek. 6:4-5).
  3. KB suggests an Arabic root meaning "to be raised" or "to be high."

The UBS Text Project, p. 17, suggests two possible ways to understand this term.

  1. no beauty in them
  2. no rest for them

entries.title: Ezekiel 7:12 "Let not the buyer rejoice nor the seller mourn"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:12 "Let not the buyer rejoice nor the seller mourn" These VERBS are translated as JUSSIVES.

  1. "rejoice" BDB 970, KB 1333, Qal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVEsense
  2. "mourn" BDB 5, KB 6, Hithpael IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense

Verses 12-13 are a literary way of prophesying that all segments of society (i.e. rich and poor) will be judged by YHWH.

▣ "multitude" This root (BDB 242) basically means "a great noise" (cf. Ezek. 7:11,12,13,14) and can refer to

  1. tumult and confusion (cf. 1 Sam. 14:19; 2 Sam. 18:29; Ps. 65:7; Isa. 17:12)
  2. a large crowd (cf. Ezek. 7:11-14; 29:19; 30:11,15; 31:2,18; 32:12 [twice],16,18,20,24,25,26,31,32; Isa. 13:4)
  3. abundance of wealth (cf. 1 Chr. 29:16; Ps. 37:16; Eccl. 5:10; Isa. 60:5)

In this context it refers to all of Judah (there is no distinction between righteous and wicked). They all are wicked"!

entries.title: Ezekiel 7:13
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:13 This is a difficult verse to translate as the variety in the ancient versions shows. Some think that Ezek. 7:12-13 refer to the selling of property in relation to "the Year of Jubilee" (cf. Lev. 25:13-16).

SPECIAL TOPIC: FEASTS OF ISRAEL, II. C.

entries.title: Ezekiel 7:14 "They have blown the trumpet"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:14 "They have blown the trumpet" Military preparations will fail because of the fear of the soldiers (cf. Ezek. 7:17).

SPECIAL TOPIC: HORNS USED BY ISRAEL

entries.title: Ezekiel 7:15
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:15 Here are the three main enemies that YHWH arrayed against His people:

  1. the sword ‒ the Neo-Babylonian army
  2. the plague ‒ sickness within the walled cities under siege
  3. famine ‒ no food within the walled cities under siege

These three are the recurrent threat of divine judgment (cf. Lev. 26:25-26; 2 Chr. 20:9; Jer. 14:12; 21:7,9; 24:10; 27:8,13; 29:17,18; 32:24,36; 34:17; 38:2; 42:17,22; 44:13; Ezek. 5:12; 6:11,12; 7:15; 12:16).

entries.title: Ezekiel 7:16
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 7:16 Even those few who escape to the mountains will be helpless and sorrowful (i.e. like doves, cf. Isa. 38:14; 59:11). Most who try to escape by fleeing the walled cities into the supposed safety of the countryside will also die (cf. Ezek. 7:15; 33:27). There is no safety!

entries.title: Ezekiel 7:17
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:17 All resistance will be ineffective because of the paralyzing fear striking the cities' defenders (cf. Ezek. 21:7; 22:14; Isa. 13:7).

▣ "all hands" See SPECIAL TOPIC: HAND

▣ "knees will become like water" This is literally, "knees shall run with water" (NASB margin). It possibly refers to fear causing urination (NET).

entries.title: Ezekiel 7:18
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:18 This is a series of mourning rites.

  1. gird with sackcloth (cf. Ezek. 27:31; Isa. 22:12; Amos 8:10)
  2. pull out or shave (cf. Ezek. 5:1) their hair (cf. Ezek. 27:31; 29:18; Amos 8:10)

SPECIAL TOPIC: GRIEVING RITES

▣ "shame will be on all faces" This was a common idiom for guilt associated with sin (cf. Jer. 51:51; Obad. 1:10; Micah 7:10). It can be expressed in several ways (see Interpreter's Dictionary of the Bible, pp. 305-306).

entries.title: Ezekiel 7:19 "abhorrent thing"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:19 "abhorrent thing" This term (BDB 622, KB 673 II, cf. Ezek. 7:20) is used of unclean or impure things or acts.

  1. menstrual period, cf. Ezek. 18:6; 22:10; 36:17; Lev. 12:2; 15:19-30; 18:19; 20:18
  2. having sex with a brother's wife, Lev. 20:21
  3. contact with a corpse (note 6:4-5), Num. 19:9,13,20,21; 31:23
  4. idolatry, cf. Ezek. 7:19,20; Ezra 9:11; Lam. 1:17

▣ "their silver and gold shall not be able to deliver them" This has two possible meanings.

  1. Neo-Babylon will not take ransom to spare them (cf. Zeph. 1:18)
  2. their personal idols of gold and silver cannot deliver them; they are thrown out into the streets

Neither can their wealth or their gods get them food because of the siege!

▣ "an occasion of stumbling" The original meaning of the VERB for "faith" was a stable stance. The opposite was slipping in the miry clay or stumbling in the way. Therefore, "stumbling" (BDB 506) is the contrasting concept from faith.

This phrase is literally "for the stumbling block of their iniquity" and is used only in Ezekiel, but often (cf. Ezek. 14:3,4,7; 18:30; 44:12). The prophet must have coined the phrase. Wealth is not always a blessing!

SPECIAL TOPIC: WEALTH

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PATH, THE WAY

7:20
NASB  "His ornaments"
NKJV  "his ornaments"
NRSV, Peshitta  "their beautiful ornaments"
TEV  "once they were proud of their beautiful
  jewels"
NJB  "they used to pride themselves on the
  beauty of their jewelry"
REB  "their beautiful jewelry"
JPSOA  "their beautiful ornaments"
LXX  "choice ornaments"

The context (i.e. Ezek. 7:20-22) seems to imply the temple's treasures, but it must be noted "His" is not in the text and the ornaments may refer to

  1. personal jewelry (BDB 725, cf. Exod. 33:4-6) of Ezek. 7:19
  2. their idols (i.e. BDB 1055, "detestable things")

If so, then "the secret place" of Ezek. 7:22 refers to Jerusalem (cf. NIDOTTE, vol. 2, p. 1074, while in vol. 3, p. 686, a different word study author asserts it is the temple).

entries.title: Ezekiel 7:19-22
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:19-22 These verses describe Israel's gods.

  1. money and commerce
  2. gold and silver idols (cf. Zeph. 1:18)
  3. YHWH's temple and its wealth have become a boast of pride (cf. Jer. 7), not sanctity and faith

Neo-Babylon will take Israel's collected wealth, individually and corporately.

entries.title: Ezekiel 7:21 "foreigners"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:21 "foreigners" This VERB, "be a stranger," BDB 266, KB 267, Qal PARTICIPLE, is used of invading enemies (cf. Ezek. 7:21; 11:9; 16:32; 28:7,10; 30:12; 31:12).

They are characterized as "the wicked of the earth." Neo-Babylon followed the military practices of the Assyrians. Both were merciless, vicious people. In Ezek. 7:24 they are called "the worst of the nations."

entries.title: Ezekiel 7:22 "I will also turn my face from them"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:22 "I will also turn my face from them" The "face" of God was an idiom for His personal presence and care for His covenant people (cf. Ezek. 39:23-24,29; Isa. 59:2). Judah's protection, peace, and prosperity depended on Him. When He left, hope left!

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANTHROPOMORPHIC LANGUAGE USED TO DESCRIBE GOD

entries.title: Ezekiel 7:23 "Make a chain"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:23 "Make a chain" The VERB (BDB 793, KB 889) is a Qal IMPERATIVE. The term "chain" (BDB 958) can be understood in two ways.

  1. sarcasm related to decorating idols with gold or silver chains (cf. Isa. 40:19)
  2. related to fetters to drag the people into exile (cf. Jer. 27:2)

▣ The violent foreigners came because of the idolatry of Israel.

  1. The land is full of bloody crimes
  2. The city is full of violence.

We reap what we sow (see note at Ezek. 7:3).

SPECIAL TOPIC: CONSEQUENCES OF IDOLATRY

entries.title: Ezekiel 7:24 "the worst of the nations"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:24 "the worst of the nations" This refers to the mercenary armies of Neo-Babylon (cf. Ezek. 21:31; 28:7; Jer. 6:22-23).

▣ "and they will possess their houses" This is one of the warnings for covenant violation in Lev. 26:32. What YHWH did to the Canaanites for their sin, He will now do to His covenant people (cf. Gen. 5:12-21)! God is no respecter of persons.

entries.title: Ezekiel 7:25 "anguish"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:25 "anguish" This term (BDB 891) appears only here as a NOUN. The VERB appears only in Isa. 38:12, where it is translated "rolled up," but may refer to a cloth being "cut off" from the loom (cf. NIDOTTE, vol. 3, p. 953).

▣ Many of the prophets (i.e. false) of Israel relied on YHWH's earlier promises to Israel, forgetting they were conditional promises/covenants. The benefits of the covenant are only available to the faithful, obedient follower. The consequences of disobedience are severe (cf. Leviticus 26; Deuteronomy 28). These false proclaimers, in YHWH's name, preached a covenant protection and peace, but there was "no peace" (cf. Ezek. 13:10,16; Isa. 48:22; 57:21).

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

entries.title: Ezekiel 7:26-27
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:26-27 The leaders of the people (cf. Jer.18:18; Micah 3:11) will be totally helpless.

  1. religious leaders
    1. prophets
    2. priests
  2. civil leaders
    1. elders
    2. king
    3. princes
    4. the people of the land (see SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PEOPLE OF THE LAND)
  3. military (i.e. "the hands of the people of the land will tremble," cf. Ezek. 7:14,17)

They are the very ones who have caused and allowed the covenant disobedience to start and continue!

▣ "people of the land" See SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PEOPLE OF THE LAND

Copyright © 2014 Bible Lessons International

entries.title: Ezekiel 8:1 "It came about in the sixth year, on the fifth day of the sixth month"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:1 "It came about in the sixth year, on the fifth day of the sixth month" This day relates to the exile of the Davidic seed (Jehoiachin) from Jerusalem to Babylon (cf. Ezek. 1:2). Ezekiel uses this dating reference throughout his book (cf. Ezek. 1:2; 8:1; 20:1; 24:1; 26:1; 29:1,17; 30:20; 31:1; 32:1,17; 33:21; 40:1). This same dating reference is also seen in 2 Kgs. 25:27; Jer. 52:31.

▣ "with the elders of Judah sitting before him" This shows that the symbolic physical positions of Ezek. 4:4-8 did not last all day and all night.

The "elders" were local tribal or clan leaders. This meant they were the civil leadership of towns, villages, and communities. They dealt with individual Israelites on a local level. Here they are the tribal leaders from Judea who have been exiled by Nebuchadnezzar II to an exilic community by the canal Chebar. The fact that the elders would come and consult with Ezekiel shows his reputation (i.e. "sitting before me"). What a contrast between the elders of Judah, who would seek God's counsel from Ezekiel, and the elders of the House of Israel, who are committing idolatry in the temple and at home in Ezek. 8:7-13.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ELDER, I. B.

▣ "the hand of the Lord God fell on me there" Notice the anthropomorphic language. Apparently YHWH's revelations came at different times and at different places. The exact nature and mechanism of divine inspiration is uncertain, but the reality is certain (cf. Ezek. 1:3; 3:14,22; 33:22; 37:1; 1 Kgs. 18:46; 2 Kgs. 3:15; Isa. 8:11; Jer. 15:17; 2 Tim. 3:14-16). God has revealed Himself and His will to certain human instruments and through them to generations of believers.

SPECIAL TOPIC: GOD DESCRIBED AS HUMAN

SPECIAL TOPIC: INSPIRATION

SPECIAL TOPIC: WAYS OF REVELATION

entries.title: Ezekiel Contextual Insights
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
EZEKIEL 8

PARAGRAPH DIVISIONS OF MODERN TRANSLATIONS

NASB NKJV NRSV TEV NJB
Vision of Abominations in Jerusalem Abominations in the Temple Temple Visions
(8:1-10:25)		 Ezekiel's Second Vision
(8:1-10:22)		 A Vision of the Sins of Israel
The Vision of Idolatry Idolatry in Jerusalem
8:1-4 8:1-4 8:1-4 8:1-3 8:1
8:2-6
8:4-5
8:5-6 8:5-12 8:5-6
8:6
8:7-13 8:7-13 8:7-12 8:7-13
8:13-14 8:13-14
8:14-15 8:14-15 8:14-15
8:15-16 8:15-16
8:16-18 8:16-18 8:16-18
8:17-18 8:17-18

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS TO CHAPTERS 8-11

  1. Ezekiel chapters 8-11 are one literary unit (cf. Ezek. 8:1 and 11:24).

  2. This section occurs fourteen months after Ezekiel's original vision of YHWH by the River Chebar; compare Ezek. 1:1-3 with 8:1 (August-September 592 B.C.).

  3. This is a literary unit which encompasses a vision of the abominations that were occurring in the temple in Jerusalem. Commentators have been divided on whether this was
    1. simply a vision ("brought me in the visions of God," Ezek. 8:3; also especially Ezek. 11:24)
    2. that he was physically transported to Jerusalem ("lifted me up between earth and heaven," Ezek. 8:3)

      The details of both the temple and the people involved are very specific.

  4. Much of this flagrant idolatry can be attributed to the influence of King Manasseh (cf. 2 Kings 21), also notice King Josiah's reform in 2 Kings 23.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Ezekiel 8:2
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:2 Although this appearance (BDB 909) is very similar to the description of anthropomorphic deity in Ezek. 1:26, 27, this verse seems to describe angelic agency (typical of apocalyptic literature; see SPECIAL TOPIC: APOCALYPTIC LITERATURE).

The MT has "a form that had the appearance of fire." The term "fire" (BDB 77) is repeated later in the verse. The Septuagint translates a similar Hebrew word "man" (BDB 35). The UBS Text Project, p. 21, suggests that the MT had "fire" but that the LXX is a more ancient form.

  1. man ‒ איש
  2. fire ‒ אש

▣ "fire" See note at Ezek. 1:27 and SPECIAL TOPIC: FIRE.

▣ "brightness, like the appearance of glowing metal" See note at Ezek. 1:4,27.

entries.title: Ezekiel 8:3 "He. . .the Spirit"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:3 "He. . .the Spirit" The angelic being is parallel or equated with "a spirit" (no ARTICLE in Hebrew text, cf. Ezek. 3:12; 11:1). Often the Spirit (BDB 924) represents YHWH's presence, in this case an angelic being, transports the prophet (cf. 1 Kgs. 18:12; 2 Kgs. 2:16; Ezek. 3:12,14; 8:3; 11:24; 37:1; possibly Acts 8:26-27,39). See notes at Ezek. 2:2

I do not think that there are two spiritual beings involved in this transport of the prophet.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SPIRIT IN THE BIBLE

▣ "lifted" The VERB (BDB 669, KB 724) is used in

  1. v. 3 ‒ Qal IMPERFECT, Ezekiel is lifted, cf. Ezek. 3:12,14; 11:1,24; 43:5
  2. v. 5 ‒ Qal IMPERATIVE, Ezekiel is commanded to lift his eyes
  3. v. 5 ‒ Qal IMPERFECT, he lifts his eyes

▣ "in the visions of God" "Visions" (BDB 909) is a means of receiving divine revelation (cf. Gen. 46:2; Num. 12:6; 1 Sam. 3:15; Dan. 10:16; Ezek. 1:1; 8:3; 40:2). Whether this involved

  1. sight (cf. Ezek. 8:2,4,5,6,7,10,11)
  2. hearing (cf. Ezek. 8:5,6,8,9,12)
  3. mental images (cf. Ezek. 8:3,4,7)

is not always clear. See note at the beginning of the chapter, C.

SPECIAL TOPIC: WAYS OF REVELATION

▣ "to the entrance to the north gate of the inner court" This gate is called the Altar Gate in Ezek. 8:4. We learn from Lev. 1:11 that this was the place of sacrifice. It was known as the royal entrance because it faced the palace of the king.

▣ "the idol of jealousy" There has been much discussion as to the exact nature of this idol or image (BDB 702). Idolatry caused a powerful reaction from YHWH (cf. Exod. 20:3-4)! Jealousy (BDB 888) is a word of deep passion. It is obvious that the idol had a prominent place at the entrance to the temple of YHWH (cf. Ezek. 8:3,5; Jer. 7:30; 32:34).

  1. Some have supposed that because of 2 Kings 21:3,7; 23:6 that it was the carved image of Ashtoreth, the Canaanite female fertility goddess. If so, this reflected Canaanite idolatry.
  2. Others supposed it was a statue of a temple guardian (i.e. lion, sphinx), if so, then Babylonian idolatry.

SPECIAL TOPIC: CONSEQUENCES OF IDOLATRY

SPECIAL TOPIC: JEALOUSY, ZEAL

entries.title: Ezekiel 8:4
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 8:4 The portable throne chariot of God that Ezekiel saw in Babylon (cf. Ezek. 1:26-28) was also present in the temple.

entries.title: Ezekiel 8:5 "He said to me. . ."
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:5 "He said to me. . ." Who is speaking? There are several subjects involved in this context.

  1. the Lord God fell on Ezekiel, v. 1
  2. the spiritual being described in v. 2 and lifted Ezekiel up, v. 2
  3. a spirit is also involved in the transportation of Ezekiel to the temple, v. 3
  4. the glory of the God of Israel was in the temple, v. 4; 9:3 (related to Ezekiel 1); also mentioned in 9:3
  5. the "He" of v. 5 identifies Himself as the owner of the temple (i.e. YHWH) in v. 5. This same representation of Deity speaks and leads Ezekiel in 8:7-13,14-15,16-18, and continues in chapter 9
  6. personsified executioners are summoned in 9:1,5,7
  7. "a certain man clother in linen" in 9:2,4,11

▣ "Son of man" See note at Ezek. 2:1.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SON OF MAN

NASB  "that I would be far from My sanctuary"
NKJV  "to make Me go far away from My sanctuary"
NRSV, JPSOA  "to drive Me far from My sanctuary"
TEV  "drawing me farther and farther away from my
  holy place"
NJB  "to drive Me out of my sanctuary"

The VERBAL (BDB 934, KB 1221, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT) expresses the reason for YHWH's departure (cf. Ezek. 11:22-23) from the temple, which He promised never to leave (cf. 2 Sam. 7:13,16, but Jeremiah saw this event, cf. Jer. 33:17,21). The Mosaic Covenant was unconditional on God's part but conditional on Israel's part (see SPECIAL TOPIC: CONVENANT).

Both the LXX and Peshitta translate this phrase in such a way as to refer to Israel being addressed. The MT supports that it is YHWH who is driven away.

entries.title: Ezekiel 8:6 "the great abomination"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 8:6 "the great abomination" See SPECIAL TOPIC: ABOMINATION (OT)

entries.title: Ezekiel 8:7 "the entrance of the court"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:7 "the entrance of the court" This refers to the outer court of Solomon's temple.

▣ "a hole in the wall" This implies that this particular idolatry was done in secret by the leaders of the people.

entries.title: Ezekiel 8:8 "now dig through the wall"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:8 "now dig through the wall" This VERB (BDB 369, KB 365) is used twice.

  1. Qal IMPERATIVE
  2. Qal IMPERFECT with waw

It is uncertain how "the hole" of Ezek. 8:7 is related to the new hole of Ezek. 8:8, dug by Ezekiel. The first may have been a secret entrance for the idolaters (cf. Ezek. 8:11-12) and the second an access hole for Ezekiel to view the abominations occurring there (cf. Ezek. 8:10-13).

entries.title: Ezekiel 8:9 "Go in and see"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:9 "Go in and see" These are both Qal IMPERATIVES.

  1. BDB 97, KB 112, cf. Ezek. 8:10
  2. BDB 906, KB 1157, cf. Ezek. 8:11

entries.title: Ezekiel 8:10 "every form of creeping things and beasts and detestable things"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:10 "every form of creeping things and beasts and detestable things" This may relate to the worship of animals as reflected in Egyptian idolatry (cf. Exodus 32, a golden calf, later copied at the temples in Bethel and Dan). For Israel, they were to make no image of these unclean (cf. Leviticus 11; Deuteronomy 14) animals (cf. Deut. 4:18). These prohibitions were to isolate Israel from Canaanite worship. Much of the Levitical legislation is for this purpose.

▣ "were carved on the wall all around" The VERB (BDB 348, KB 347, Pual PARTICIPLE) means "to carve" (cf. 1 Kgs. 6:35 or "scratch" cf. Ezek. 4:1). In Ezek. 23:14 it may refer to wall painting.

entries.title: Ezekiel 8:11 "seventy elders of the house of Israel"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:11 "seventy elders of the house of Israel" "The house of Israel" parallels "the house of Judah." It also shows the number 70 (cf. Exod. 24:1; Num. 11:16,25) of the elders (cf. Ezek. 7:26) involved in this idolatry. This would symbolize all of Israel's leadership. Seventy is a round number denoting fullness.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SYMBOLIC NUMBERS IN SCRIPTURE, #7

▣ "Jaazaniah the son of Shapan" This shows the radical influence of idolatry when one of the well known leaders was involved in it (cf. Ezek. 11:1). Shapan is a name related to the court leaders of Josiah (cf. 2 Kings 22; 2 Chr. 34; Jeremiah 36), but the connection is uncertain. Possibly his name is meant to convey that the political leadership at the highest levels was involved.

entries.title: Ezekiel 8:11 "each man with his censer in his hand, and the fragrance of the cloud of incense rising"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:11 "each man with his censer in his hand, and the fragrance of the cloud of incense rising" They were all personally involved in the idolatrous rituals.

NASB, NRSV  "fragrance of the cloud of incense rising"
NKJV  "a thick cloud of incense went up"
TEV  "smoke was rising from the incense"
NJB, REB  "rose a fragrant cloud of incense"
Peshitta  "the smoke of the cloud of incense went up"
LXX  "the vapor of the incense was ascending"

The Hebrew term "fragrance" (BDB 801 II) is found only here in the OT. The same consonants mean

  1. pray
  2. worshiper
  3. abundant
  4. a place name in Josh. 15:42. BDB suggests "odor" (NET), but also possibly "smoke" (which is a symbol of prayer rising to God)

entries.title: Ezekiel 8:12 "each man in a room with its carved images"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:12 "each man in a room with its carved images" Not only were these leaders participating in cultic idolatry in the temple, but they had made local or individual shrines in their own homes (or alcoves of the temple). It is uncertain if this represents corporate worship or individual worship or both.

▣ "they say" There is a series of excuses and words found in the book of Ezekiel (cf. Ezek. 8:12; 9:9; 11:3, 15; 12:22, 27; 18:2,25; 33:10, 24, 30; 35:12; 37:11). This is similar to Paul's use of diatribe in Romans.

▣ "'The Lord does not see us; the Lord has forsaken the land'" These comments cast aspersions on YHWH's knowledge and His covenant promises! They were repudiating the character of YHWH (cf. Gen. 3:1-7)! These men had reacted theologically to the deportations of artisans and leaders from Jerusalem by Nebuchadnezzar II in 596 B.C.

entries.title: Ezekiel 8:13 "yet you will see still greater abominations which they are committing"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:13 "yet you will see still greater abominations which they are committing" This becomes a repeated refrain (cf. Ezek. 8:15).

SPECIAL TOPIC: ABOMINATION (OT)

entries.title: Ezekiel 8:14 "women were sitting there weeping for Tammuz"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 8:14 "women were sitting there weeping for Tammuz" See a good, brief article in James M. Freeman, Manners and Customs of the Bible, pp. 299-300. This reflects the Babylonian idolatry of the Sumerian agricultural god who died and rose every year. Obviously he became the fertility god of the Babylonians. He is known in Babylon as Dumuzi, Consort of Ishtar (cf. Isa. 17:10,11). He is known in Greece as Adonis, which is very similar to the Egyptian Osiris. This was the male lover of Aphrodite who was killed by wild boars and sent to the underworld each year for six months. The women wept to identify with Aphrodite, who wept at the loss of her lover during the winter. August to September (cf. Ezek. 8:1) would have started this cycle. Possibly the worship of Babylonian gods shows that it had already conquered Israel spiritually!

entries.title: Ezekiel 8:16 "the inner court"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:16 "the inner court" This is described in 1 Kgs. 6:36. It was also known as "the Court of the Priests" in 2 Chr. 4:9. It would be the court just before the inner shrine (i.e. holy place and holy of holies).

▣ "twenty-five men" There may be some purposeful symbolism related to the identity of these different groups.

  1. The 70 elders and the son of Shapan seem to represent the civil leadership.
  2. The women seem to represent the general public.
  3. The twenty-five men may represent priests (i.e. the High Priest and the priests from David's day; the LXX has "twenty").

If so, then all segments of Israeli society were actively involved in idolatry at the temple (the place YHWH symbolically dwelt).

▣ "with their backs to the temple of the Lord and their faces to the east. . .toward the sun" The last mentioned Canaanite idolatry was the worship of the sun (i.e. Deut. 4:19; 17:3; 2 Kgs. 23:5,11; Jer. 8:2). The worship of the sun is also illustrated by the names of cities:

  1. Beth Shemesh" ["house of the sun," cf. Josh. 15:10; 21:16; Jdg. 1:33]
  2. En-shemesh" ["fountain of the sun," cf. Josh. 15:7; 18:17]
  3. Mount Heres" ["mount of the sun," cf. Jdg. 1:35])

It is ironic symbolism that as they faced the sun they turned their back on the Lord. This sun worship was rampant all over the Ancient Near East, but particularly in Egypt, Canaan, Babylon, and later in Persia (cf. 2 Kgs. 23:11). It is also related to the later winged sun disk of Zoroastrianism.

entries.title: Ezekiel 8:17 "provoked Me repeatedly"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:17 "provoked Me repeatedly" The VERB (BDB 494, KB 491, Hiphil INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT) is regularly used of provoking YHWH to anger by committing idolatry (cf. Deut. 4:25; 9:18; 31:29; 32:16; 1 Kgs. 14:9,15; 16:7,33; 22:54; 2 Kgs. 17:11,17; 21:6; 23:19; Jer. 25:6,7; 32:30; 44:8; Ezek. 16:25).

▣ "for behold they are putting the twig to their nose" There have been several theories concerning this phrase:

  1. we have found this (i.e. a flowered stem held to the nose) as an act of sun worship in Assyrian bas reliefs (ANEP 281, which fits this context best)
  2. the early rabbis and later Kimchi and Rashi say it relates to God's nose and thus the stench of idolatry that rose to Him (JPSOA footnote "c" states "their" is a euphemism for "My")
  3. it is a sign of contempt and mockery of God (i.e. LXX, Strabo [historian], cf. NIDOTTE, vol. 1, p. 1118)

entries.title: Ezekiel 8:18
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:18 See full exegetical note at Ezek. 7:4. Also note this is repeated in 9:10.

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

9:1
NASB, NKJV, NRSV  "Draw near"
TEV  "come here"
NJB  "are approaching"
REB  "here they come"
JPSOA  "Approach"
Peshitta  "Come near"

This is translated as an IMPERATIVE, but the VERB (BDB 897, KB 1132) is a Qal PERFECT, which denotes that the executioners have drawn near and abide!

NASB  "O executioners of the city"
NKJV  "those who have charge over the city"
NRSV  "you executioners of the city"
TEV  "you men who are going to punish"
NJB  "The scourges of the city"
REB  "those appointed to punish the city"
JPSOA  "you men in charge of the city"
Peshitta  "O you avengers of the city"

Chapter 9 personifies the judgment that is mentioned in Ezek. 8:18. These executioners (BDB 824) are angelic beings (cf. The Death Angel of Egypt, Exodus 12 and Dan. 4:13, 17, 23). It is interesting that the "watchers" of Daniel (cf. Dan. 4:13,17,23) may serve as temple guardians. If so, they would have been distressed at an idol guardian erected at the temple entrance!

It is also interesting that the basic meaning of this FEMININE NOUN (BDB 824) is "visitation." It can mean for blessing, but usually it is for punishment (cf. Isa. 10:3; Jer. 8:12; 10:15; 49:8; 50:31; Hosea 9:7; Micah 7:4).

SPECIAL TOPIC: DEATH ANGEL

NASB, NRSV, Peshitta  "destroying weapon"
NKJV  "deadly weapon"
TEV  "weapons"
NJB, REB, JPSOA  "weapons of destruction"
LXX  "instruments of annihilation"

This (BDB 479 CONSTRUCT BDB 1008) is similar to "shattering weapon" (BDB 479 CONSTRUCT BDB 658) in Ezek. 9:2.

entries.title: Ezekiel 9:2 "the upper gate which faces the north"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:2 "the upper gate which faces the north" These angelic executioners came from the very place of the image in Ezek. 8:3 and the women weeping in Ezek. 8:14. It was also the direction from which the invading Neo-Babylonian army came.

"North" became imagery for invasion.

NASB  "shattering weapon"
NKJV  "battle-ax"
NRSV  "weapon for slaughter"
TEV  "weapon"
NJB  "deadly weapon"
REB  "battle-club"
JPSOA  "club"
LXX  "ax"
Peshitta  "destroying weapon"

This NOUN (BDB 658) is found only here in the OT. The VERB means "shatter." The same root consonants are found in Jer. 51:20 and denote a war club.

▣ "a certain man clothed in linen" This, too, was one of the angelic beings sent by YHWH. He is dressed as a priest (cf. Exod. 28:42; 1 Sam. 22:18; Dan. 10:5; 12:6) and yet, is angelic and functions as a scribe. Recording angels are an aspect of apocalyptic literature (i.e. Enoch 89:59ff).

See list of the angelic and divine persons involved in chapters 8-9 at 8:5.

SPECIAL TOPIC: APOCALYPTIC LITERATURE

▣ "a writing case" This (BDB 903 CONSTRUCT 707, literally "ink horn for writing") is an Egyptian loan word which speaks of the equipment of a scribe. It is found only in this chapter in the OT (cf. Ezek. 9:2,3,11).

▣ "the bronze altar" This was the altar of sacrifice (i.e. Exod. 27:1-8 describes the bronze altar of the tabernacle; 2 Chr. 4:1 describes the bronze altar of Solomon's temple). This sacrificial altar had been moved to the north side of the temple to accommodate Ahaz's new pagan altar, patterned after one in Damascus (cf. 2 Kgs. 16:10-16). This same altar of sacrifice is also described in Ezekiel's future temple (cf. Ezek. 43:13-17).

SPECIAL TOPIC: ALTAR OF SACRIFICE

entries.title: Ezekiel 9:3 "went up from the cherub"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:3 "went up from the cherub" This can refer either to God moving

  1. from the Ark of the Covenant (cf. Exod. 25:10-22)
  2. from His portable throne chariot (cf. Ezek. 8:4)

This is part of the preparation for God leaving the temple and moving east to be with the exiles (cf. Ezek. 10:18-19; 43:2-5).

For "cherub" see SPECIAL TOPIC: CHERUBIM.

▣ "the threshold of the temple" The term "threshold" (BDB 837, cf. Ezek. 9:3; 10:4,18; 47:1) is uncertain. It has no cognates. Some think it is related to "asylum" or "protector." It has something to do with the entrance.

Interestingly the JPSOA translation has "to the platform of the House." The Jewish Study Bible's footnote says, "the raised platform on which the temple stood, cf. Ezek. 47:1," p. 1058.

entries.title: Ezekiel 9:4 "Go through the midst of the city"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:4 "Go through the midst of the city" The VERB (BDB 716, KB 778, Qal IMPERATIVE) commands that those who "sigh" (BDB 58, KB 70, Niphal PARTICIPLE) and "groan" (BDB 60, KB 72, Niphal PARTICIPLE, literally, "be in mourning") over Israel's idolatry be marked for protection (similar to Rev. 7:3; 9:4; 14:1). This shows YHWH's compassion and protection for those who seek Him even in the midst of judgment. This is related to the theological concept of a believing remnant.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE REMNANT, Three Senses

▣ "and put a mark on the forehead of the men" This is similar to the mark of protection placed on Cain's forehead in Gen. 4:15 and later in the NT on the saints in Rev. 7:1-3; 9:4; 14:1.

The term "mark" (BDB 1063, KB 1696, Hiphil PERFECT with waw, "set a mark") and the shape of the mark is not known. The same consonants form the word for "wound" or "pain" (cf. Ps. 78:41). Whatever it was it was visible to the angelic beings who brought death.

There is speculation (often allegorical) that the Hebrew t (tau) was in the shape of a t or x, which symbolized Christ (cf. Jack Finegan, Light From the Ancient Past, p. 332). Be careful of allegory. It can make Scripture mean anything! A book that means anything, means nothing (Gordon Fee).

entries.title: Ezekiel 9:5-6
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:5-6 The command is repeated from Ezek. 9:4 with the added command, "strike" (BDB 645, KB 697, Hiphil IMPERATIVE , cf, 7:9; 32:15).

The two commands, "go through" and "strike," are grammatically related to three JUSSIVES:

  1. do not let your eye have pity, BDB 299, KB 298, Qal JUSSIVE, YHWH states that He will have no pity in Ezek. 5:11; 7:4,9; 8:18; 9:10
  2. do not spare, BDB 328, KB 328, Qal IMPERFECT, but used in a JUSSIVE sense
  3. do not touch any man on whom is the mark, BDB 620, KB 670, Qal IMPERFECT, literally, "drawn near," used in a JUSSIVE sense, cf. Exod. 12:33; Rev. 9:4

entries.title: Ezekiel 9:6 "utterly slay"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:6 "utterly slay" This VERB (BDB 246, KB 255, Qal IMPERFECT) means "to kill" with an added NOUN (BDB 1008) "ruin," "destruction," cf. Exod. 12:13.

▣ "old men, young men, maidens, little children and women" This list adds shocking vividness to the order "kill" (i.e. kill everyone, of any sex, of any age, of any social, economic standing)! This is similar to the "Holy War" of Joshua.

▣ "and you shall start from My sanctuary" The VERB (BDB 320, KB 319, Hiphil IMPERFECT [twice]) is from a root which basically means "to pollute," "to defile," and "to profane."

I think this is probably the OT source of Peter's statement in 1 Pet. 4:17, "for it is time for judgment to begin with the household of God."

▣ "so they started with the elders who were before the temple" We must remember that privilege brings great responsibility. To whom much is given, much is required (cf. Luke 12:48; Gal. 6:7).

entries.title: Ezekiel 9:7
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:7 YHWH's commands to the angelic destroyers are three-fold in this verse.

  1. "defile the temple," BDB 379, KB 375, Piel iIMPERATIVE, cf. Ezek. 6:4-5
  2. "fill the courts with the slain," BDB 569, KB 583, Piel IMPERATIVE
  3. "go through," BDB 422, KB 425, Qal IMPERATIVE, similar statement to 9:4

entries.title: Ezekiel 9:8 "As they were striking"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:8 "As they were striking" Ezekiel begins to plead for the remnant when he realizes the destroying angels were killing everyone (BDB 645, KB 697, Hiphil INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT, cf. Gen. 7:23).

▣ "I alone was left" Apparently there were none who grieved over the dead (i.e. no righteous remnant left in Jerusalem)!

Remember this is a theological vision (Ezek. 8:1). This is a prediction of the Neo-Babylonian invasions (i.e. 605, 597, 586, 582 B.C.), culminating in the 586 B.C. destruction of Jerusalem and the temple. Many died, but not all! The terrible vision is a result of YHWH's revulsion to idolatry! In the vision there were no survivors. In reality there were. The vision drives home the theological truth with vividness and power! YHWH hates idolatry, especially in His own covenant people!

SPECIAL TOPIC: CONSEQUENCES OF IDOLATRY

entries.title: Ezekiel 9:9
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:9 This decree of guilt (BDB 730) is expressed by three words in the Hebrew text.

  1. "great," BDB 152
  2. "exceedingly," BDB 547 (twice)
  3. "is full," BDB 569, KB 583, Niphal IMPERFECT with waw and it is repeated in Qal PERFECT, "full of perversion" (BDB 642)

▣ "perversion" This term (BDB 642) occurs only here in the OT. It may be from the root "bend" or "twist" (BDB 639, initial "n" instead of "m"). If so, the root concept of sin as a perversion of the standard would make sense.

SPECIAL TOPIC: RIGHTEOUSNESS

▣ "they say" This reflects the idolaters' statement of Ezek. 8:12 (cf. Isa. 29:15; 47:10).

entries.title: Ezekiel 9:10
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:10 The Jerusalemite idolaters say YHWH does not see. In one sense, they are right. He will refuse to see (i.e. My eye) when calamity comes, cf. Ezek. 8:18.

▣ "I shall bring their conduct upon their heads" This phrase is used several times (cf. Ezek. 7:3,4,8,9; 9:11; 11:21; 16:43; 17:19; 22:31; 1 Kgs. 8:22). See note at Ezek. 7:4.

This is an often repeated biblical theme. See full lists of text at Gal. 6:7-10 online.

entries.title: Ezekiel 9:11
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:11 This refers to the angelic messenger/scribe. Angels obey God, but not His creatures made in His image. What irony!

 

Copyright © 2014 Bible Lessons International

entries.title: Ezekiel 10:1 "the expanse"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:1 "the expanse" See note at Ezek. 1:22.

▣
NASB, NKJV, LXX, JPSOA  "like a sapphire stone"
NRSV  "like a sapphire"
TEV  "a throne made of sapphire"
REB  "a sapphire in the shape
  of a throne"
NJB  "something like sapphire"
Peshitta  "something with the appearance
  of a sapphire stone"

The MT has a NOUN CONSTRUCT (BDB 6 "stone" and BDB 705 "sapphire) in Ezek. 10:1. This jewel appears several times.

  1. a pavement under YHWH's feet at Mt. Sinai ‒ Exod. 24:10
  2. a jewel in the ephod of the High Priest ‒ Exod. 28:18; 39:11
  3. foundation of the restored people of God to the Promised Land ‒ Isa. 54:11
  4. YHWH's throne in the midst of His portable throne chariot ‒ Ezek. 1:26; 10:1
  5. the covering of a cherub in Eden, used as imagery of the King of Tyre ‒ Ezek. 28:13

This jewel's name comes into Hebrew as a loan word from Sanskrit. It is a bluish (i.e. the color of the sky), brittle composite stone from Afghanistan. In Akkadian texts, it is mentioned as part of the temple structure dedicated to "the high god."

Since Pliny it has been identified as lapis lazuli (i.e. Persian loan word).

entries.title: Ezekiel 10:1-2
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 10:1-2 This is YHWH's portable throne chariot of Ezek. 1:13-25. It will return to the temple in Ezek. 43:1-9.
