FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Ezekiel 10:2
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:2 YHWH gives three commands to the angelic being dressed in linen.

  1. "enter," BDB 97, KB 112, Qal IMPERATIVE
  2. "fill," BDB 569, KB 583, Piel IMPERATIVE
  3. "scatter," BDB 284, KB 283, Qal IMPERATIVE

The imagery comes from the vision of Isa. 6:6, where it is initially a purification ritual inaugurating Isaiah's ministry. Here it is a judgment ritual, which is repeated in Rev. 8:5. In may ways Isaiah (i.e. chapter 24) and Ezekiel are an initial example of apocalyptic imagery. This is developed in Daniel and Zechariah and becomes a significant Jewish genre during the interbiblical period.

SPECIAL TOPIC: APOCALYPTIC LITERATURE

entries.title: Ezekiel 10:3 "the cloud filled the inner court"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:3 "the cloud filled the inner court" This is the theophanic cloud (BDB 777) of glory (a visual symbol of the presence of YHWH) that was present

  1. at the crossing of the Red Sea (cf. Exod. 13:21)
  2. on Mount Sinai (cf. Exod. 24:14-18)
  3. at the tabernacle of Moses (cf. Exod. 40:34-38; Num. 14:14)
  4. at the dedication of Solomon's temple (cf. 1 Kgs. 8:11; 2 Chr. 5:13-14)
  5. in Isaiah's vision (cf. Isa. 6:4)
  6. in Ezekiel's vision (cf. Ezek. 1:4)
  7. at the baptism of Jesus (cf. Mark 1:10-11)
  8. at the transfiguration of Jesus (cf. Matt. 17:5)
  9. at the ascension of Jesus (Acts 1:9)
  10. at the return of Jesus (cf. Matt. 24:30; 26:64; Mark 14:62; Luke 21:27; 1 Thess. 4:17; Rev. 1:7)

This ADJECTIVE "inner" (BDB 819) refers to parts of the temple or a king's palace (cf. Esther 4:11; 5:1). The VERB form means "to turn a specific direction" (cf. Ezek. 8:3). Ezekiel uses this term twenty-four times in his discussions of the Jerusalem temple and his eschatological temple.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SHEKINAH

entries.title: Ezekiel 10:4 "the glory of the Lord. . .brightness of the glory of the Lord"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:4 "the glory of the Lord. . .brightness of the glory of the Lord" Brightness becomes an added characteristic of His glory (cf. Ezek. 1:4,28) during the Wilderness Wandering period (i.e. the Shekinah Cloud of Glory).

SPECIAL TOPIC: GLORY (kabod, OT)

▣ "the threshold" See full note at Ezek. 9:3.

entries.title: Ezekiel 10:5 "the sound of the wings of the Cherubim"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:5 "the sound of the wings of the Cherubim" For the full notes see Ezek. 1:24.

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHERUBIM

▣ "God Almighty" This is the Hebrew title El Shaddai. This was the Patriarchal name for Israel's Deity (cf. Exod. 6:3).  It is first used as a self-designation by YHWH to Abram in Gen. 17:6.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ALMIGHTY (Shaddai)

entries.title: Ezekiel 10:6 "Take fire from between the whirling wheels and from between the Cherubim"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 10:6 "Take fire from between the whirling wheels and from between the Cherubim" The VERB (BDB 542, KB 534, Qal IMPERATIVE) is the fourth command to this angelic being (i.e. "the man clothed in linen," cf. Ezek. 10:2). This is obviously a reference to the burning coals, which represent God's holiness (i.e. Isa. 6:6).

entries.title: Ezekiel 10:7-8, 11-12, 14
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:7-8, 11-12, 14 The full description of the Cherubim is given in Ezek. 1:5-14.

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHERUBIM

entries.title: Ezekiel 10:9-10, 13
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 10:9-10, 13 The full description of the wheels is found in Ezek. 1:15-21.

entries.title: Ezekiel 10:9 "a Tarshish stone"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 10:9 "a Tarshish stone" See SPECIAL TOPIC: TARSHISH

entries.title: Ezekiel 10:12 "Their whole body, their back, and their hands, and their wings, and the wheels were full of eyes all around"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 10:12 "Their whole body, their back, and their hands, and their wings, and the wheels were full of eyes all around" This is an expansion of the description found in chapter 1, where the eyes were only found on the wheels (cf. Ezek. 1:18; Rev. 4:6,8). It seems to be an intensification of the all-knowingness of God. This is in contrast to the statements of the idolaters in Ezek. 8:12 and which is reacted to by God in Ezek. 9:9.

entries.title: Ezekiel 10:14 "The first face was the face of a cherub"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 10:14 "The first face was the face of a cherub" In Ezek. 1:10 it was the face of an ox. There is no real explanation for the change (cf. Rev. 4:7). Even in the book of Ezekiel it seems that the description changes even again in Ezek. 41:18-19.

entries.title: Ezekiel 10:15, 20 "The cherubim rose up. They are the living beings that I saw at the river Chebar"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:15, 20 "The cherubim rose up. They are the living beings that I saw at the river Chebar" Possibly, Ezekiel had not been in the inner court of the temple. Although he was in training to become a priest he was exiled before his thirtieth year. Apparently when he saw the pictures on the inside of the temple he recognized the creatures he saw in chapter 1 were the Cherubim.

10:17
NASB, NKJV, NRSV, JPSOA  "for the spirit of the living being
  was in them"
TEV  "because the creatures controlled
  them"
NJB  "since they shared the same living
  spirit"
LXX, Peshitta  "because the spirit of life was
  in them"
Rotherham  "for the spirit of the living one was
  in them"

The inanimate wheels followed the will of the four living creatures that supported the throne. The throne moved at YHWH's direction. It could move on the ground (i.e. wheels) and through the air (cherubim wings) in any direction.

entries.title: Ezekiel 10:18
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:18 God returns to His throne chariot. This is anthropomorphic imagery.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANTHROPOMORPHIC LANGUAGE TO DESCRIBE DEITY

entries.title: Ezekiel 10:19
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:19 This is the initial sequence of YHWH leaving His temple. This is where the symbolic title "Ichabod," which means "the glory has departed" (BDB 33, cf. 1 Sam. 4:21), was put over the temple. It is one thing for YHWH to refuse to listen to His people. It is far more devastating that He leave His temple!

The rabbis speculate that God stayed three and a half years on the Mount of Olives (cf. Ezek. 11:22-23) hoping that the Jews would repent, but they would not. This is surely an exaggeration. So He moved east to be with the exiles who formed a nucleus of the people of God who would return. The glory returns to this temple in Ezek. 43:12.

entries.title: Ezekiel 10:20 "cherubim"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:20 "cherubim" See SPECIAL TOPIC: CHERUBIM

Copyright © 2014 Bible Lessons International

entries.title: Ezekiel 11:1 "the Spirit lifted me up"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:1 "the Spirit lifted me up" This was not the first or last time Ezekiel was impacted by "Spirit" (i.e. no DEFINITE ARTICLE, cf. Ezek. 2:2; 3:12,14; 8:3; 11:24; 43:5). See full note at Ezek. 3:12.

SPECIAL TOPIC: BREATH, WIND, SPIRIT

SPECIAL TOPIC: SPIRIT IN THE BIBLE

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PERSONHOOD OF THE SPIRIT

SPECIAL TOPIC: TRINITY, II. C.

▣ "the east gate of the Lord's house" We know from Jer. 26:10 that this was a place of public assembly (like the city gate in local settings). This gate is mentioned in Ezek. 10:19. This is where the portable Throne Chariot lifted up and left the temple area.

▣ "Jaazaniah son of Azzur" There are three others mentioned by this same first name (BDB 24) but who have different fathers (cf. Ezek. 8:11; 2 Kgs. 25:23; Jer. 35:3). Be careful of confusion.

▣ "Pelatiah" We know nothing of this man (BDB 812). It is obvious that these two men were leaders of the people. The nobility had been exiled with Ezekiel in 597 B.C. and, therefore, these were new leaders.

NASB, NJB, JPSOA, LXX  "leaders of the people"
NKJV, Peshitta  "princes of the people"
NRSV  "officials of the people"
TEV  "leaders of the nation"
REB  "of high office"

The NKJV has the literal (BDB 978 construct BDB 766). This would imply they are high government leaders. The problem comes in how to identify them because most of these leaders were exiled with Ezekiel and the royal court (597 B.C.). These may have been:

  1. some who escaped capture and deportation and were idolators ‒ Ezek. 8
  2. some of lesser stature who assumed the role of leadership in the vacuum caused by the exile

In context, option #1 is best because Ezekiel is taken by the Spirit to Jerusalem.

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Ezekiel 11:2 "Son of man"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:2 "Son of man" See note at Ezek. 2:1.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SON OF MAN

▣ "who devise iniquity and give evil advice in the city" Their attitude is depicted in Ezek. 11:3 and 15. They are false leaders (cf. Ezek. 11:4), so common in Israel's religious and civic life!

entries.title: Ezekiel 11:3 "Is it not time to build houses? This city is the pot and we are the flesh"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:3 "Is it not time to build houses? This city is the pot and we are the flesh" What they were saying is

  1. "We are the chosen ones. Those who were exiled were judged by God, but He is not going to judge us who remain in the chosen city! We are His choicest vessels" (cf. Ezek. 28:26; Jer. 29:5, i.e. build houses in Jerusalem now! Also note Jer. 21:8-10, where the prophets were preaching "Peace, peace" and yet the destruction of Babylon is surely coming).
  2. The phrase "to build houses" may be an idiom for starting a family (or family line, cf. Deut. 25:9; Ruth 4:11).

    Not only is the first phrase in doubt, but also the second. It could be

    1. imagery for protection
    2. imagery for destruction

    All being noted, I think it is a parallel to the false prophets' message of

    1. peace is sure
    2. the city will never fall
    3. we who remain are the chosen ones
  3. YHWH has already rejected us, why should we serve Him?
  4. Let us prepare for war (i.e. build fortifications, not build houses)!

The false, idolatrous leaders are the cause of Jerusalem's fall (cf. v. 6). The imagery here is from a sacrificial offering. The people of Jerusalem are the meat offering and the city is the sacrificial pot they are cooked in (i.e. siege, cf. v. 7)!

Notice v. 11 negates this prediction of the false, idolatrous leaders. YHWH will judge them, not in the city but at the borders of Israel.

  1. as they try to escaape
  2. as they go into Neo-Babylonian exile
  3. they were executed at Riblah (cf. 2 Kgs. 25:18-21; Jer. 52:24-27)

entries.title: Ezekiel 11:4 "prophesy against them"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:4 "prophesy against them" Ezekiel had done this earlier in Ezek. 3:4,17.

The verb "prophesy" (BDB 612, KB 659) is a Niphal imperative. It is used twice for emphasis! YHWH, by His Spirit, directed the prophet (Ezek. 11:5) what to say, when to say it, and who to say it to.

SPECIAL TOPIC: PROPHECY (OT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: INSPIRATION

11:5 "said. . .say. . .says" The Hebrew word "say" (BDB 55, KB 65) is found often in this chapter. It refers to

  1. YHWH speaking to and through Ezekiel
  2. the false leaders speaking
  3. Ezekiel praying to YHWH

See note at Ezek. 11:4. Ezekiel is YHWH's mouthpiece!

▣ "I know your thoughts" This same truth is expressed in several ways (cf. 1 Sam. 16:7; 1 Chr. 28:9; Ps. 7:9; Prov. 16:2; 21:2; 24:12; Jer. 11:20; 17:10; Luke 16:15; Acts 1:24; 15:8; Rom. 8:27; Rev. 2:23). God knows the thoughts and motives of His human creatures! We reap what we sow (see full lists of texts at Gal. 6:7-10 online) and what we think!

The literal phrase is "what comes up in your spirit"( NASB margin). The Hebrew term "spirit," "wind," "breath" (BDB 924) is understood here as "mind" (cf. Ezek. 20:32).

SPECIAL TOPIC: BREATH, WIND, SPIRIT

entries.title: Ezekiel 11:6
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 11:6 The terrible judgment about to destroy Jerusalem and the temple (God's protected place, Jer. 7:26) is because of their evil, not a lack of YHWH's power to protect nor His compassion to care!

entries.title: Ezekiel 11:7
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 11:7 This statement reverses the false leaders' statement of confidence in Ezek. 11:3.

entries.title: Ezekiel 11:9 "I shall deliver you into the hands of"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:9 "I shall deliver you into the hands of" This is an idiom of military defeat.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HAND

▣ "of strangers" This is a fulfillment of Deut. 28:36,49,50. As Assyrians exiled the northern tribes, so Neo-Babylon will exile the southern tribes!

entries.title: Ezekiel 11:10 "so you shall know that I am the Lord"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:10 "so you shall know that I am the Lord" See note at Ezek. 6:13.

▣ "to the borders of Israel" This could be "as far as the borders of Israel," or it could refer to "at the borders of Israel" as fulfilled in 2 Kings 25:18-21, where King Zedekiah, when trying to fleeing, is captured and taken to Nebuchadnezzar II at Riblah.

entries.title: Ezekiel 11:11
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 11:11 This is a clarification of Ezek. 11:7.

entries.title: Ezekiel 11:12
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:12 Israel sinned against two "laws."

  1. the statutes and ordinances of YHWH (see SPECIAL TOPIC: TERMS FOR GOD'S REVELATION; known as "special revelation," cf. Ps. 19:7-12)
  2. the society norms of the surrounding nations (cf. Ezek. 5:7; known as "natural revelation," cf. Ps. 19:1-6; Rom. 1:19; 2:14)

Israel "walked" (i.e. lifestyle actions, BDB 229, KB 246, Qal PERFECT) in ways more evil than their pagan neighbors. This demanded judgment (cf. Gen. 15:16; Lev. 18:24-30).

entries.title: Ezekiel 11:13 "it came about as I prophesied, that Pelatiah son of Benaiah died"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:13 "it came about as I prophesied, that Pelatiah son of Benaiah died" This was a visible and immediate sign to the elders back in the exile of the validity of Ezekiel's message. The word of this man's death would not reach them for several weeks.

▣ "Alas, Lord God!" This is literally the divine title "Adon YHWH."

SPECIAL TOPIC: LORD (Adon and Kurios)

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

▣ Will You bring the remnant of Israel to a complete end" This same question was asked by Ezekiel as the six angelic destroyers went through the city (Ezek. 9:8).

It is uncertain why the death of an evil leader (Ezek. 11:2) would illicit this response.

For the theological concept of "remnant" see SPECIAL TOPIC: THE REMNANT (three senses).

entries.title: Ezekiel 11:15 "Son of man"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:15 "Son of man" See note at Ezek. 2:1.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SON OF MAN

NASB, NRSV  "your fellow exiles"
NASB margin, Jewish Study Bible  "the men of your
  redemption"
NKJV, Peshitta  "your kinsmen"
NRSV footnote  "people of your kindred"
NJB, REB  "to your kinfolk"
LXX  "the men of thy captivity"
JPSOA  "the men of your kindred"

The MT has "the men of your kindred" (BDB 35 construct BDB 145), which seems to refer to other exiles, possibly of the same tribe clan or family.

For "kindred" (i.e. Go'el) see notes at Ruth 3:9.

SPECIAL TOPIC: KINSMAN REDEEMER

▣ "Go far from the Lord; this land has been given us as a possession" "Go far" (BDB 934, KB 1221) can be a Qal IMPERATIVE or a Qal PERFECT. This is related to verse 3. The current residents of Jerusalem were saying they were the new chosen seed and the exiles (the royal family, the civil and religious leaders, and the artisans) had been rejected. But in reality just the opposite was true. This can be seen in Ezek. 11:16, where God says, "I am going to dwell with the exiles" and Ezek. 11:17, where He says He will restore them to the land. Both Ezek. 11:16 and 17 start with an IMPERATIVE!

Although it is true that Ezekiel focuses on Judah's destruction and exile through chapter 24 (chapters 25-32 are oracles against the nations, except for 28:25-26), there are hints here and there in these early chapters of Ezekiel's message of restoration to the faithful remnant exiled in Mesopotamia.

  1. Ezek. 5:3
  2. Ezek. 6:8-9
  3. Ezek. 11:14-21
  4. Ezek. 12:16
  5. Ezek. 16:60-63
  6. Ezek. 17:22-24
  7. Ezek. 20:39-44
  8. Ezek. 28:25-26

entries.title: Ezekiel 11:16 "I was a sanctuary for them"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:16 "I was a sanctuary for them" YHWH is described as a place of sacredness and safety to the faithful exiles (cf. Isa. 8:14, in Isa. 25:4 He is a "refuge"). These are all powerful imagery for care and protection! The physical sanctuary in Jerusalem will be destroyed, but the "true" sanctuary (i.e. YHWH) was with them in exile as the visions of Ezekiel would clearly reveal. YHWH had left Jerusalem and moved east (cf. Ezek. 11:22-25), but He would return with the exiles. YHWH moving to Babylon showed His universality. He was not limited to Canaan. He was the God of all creation!

This phrase may have been the OT background for Jesus' statement in John 2:19, quoted in Mark 14:58; 15:29; and Acts 6:14. Jesus saw Himself as the new temple! He is our sanctuary!

The term "little" (BDB 589), depending on context, can mean "a little" or "a few." It can denote numbers, kinds, or time. In this context "time" (i.e. the exile) fits best (NET). YHWH Himself cannot be described as "a little sanctuary"!

SPECIAL TOPIC: REFUGE

entries.title: Ezekiel 11:17 "the land of Israel"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:17 "the land of Israel" See note at Ezek. 7:2.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ISRAEL (the name)

entries.title: Ezekiel 11:18-19
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:18-19 Notice that "they will remove" (BDB 693, KB 747, Hiphil, PERFECT with waw, PLURAL) follows Ezek. 18:31-32. However, this has been the problem of fallen humanity, they cannot keep God's covenant! Therefore, YHWH will act on their behalf (i.e. similar to the "new covenant" of Jer. 31:31-34; described in Ezek. 36:22-36).

  1. "I will give," Ezek. 11:19, BDB 678, KB 773, Qal PERFECT  with waw, SINGULAR
  2. "I shall put, Ezek. 11:19, BDB 678, KB 773, Qal IMPERFECT SINGULAR
  3. "I shall take out," Ezek. 11:19, BDB 693, KB 747, Hiphil PERFECT with waw, SINGULAR
  4. "I will give," Ezek. 11:19, BDB 678, KB 773, Qal PERFECT with waw, SINGULAR

Notice that human response is still required (cf. Ezek. 11:20).

  1. "they will walk," Ezek. 11:20, BDB 229, KB 246, Qal IMPERFECT PLURAL
  2. "they will keep," Ezek. 11:20, BDB 1036, KB 1581, Qal IMPERFECT PLURAL
  3. "they will do," Ezek. 11:20, BDB 793, KB 889, Qal PERFECT with waw, PLURAL

The covenant will be restored ("they will be My people, and I shall be their God"), but it still required obedience (cf. Ezek. 11:21; Deut. 30:2,10).

The returning exiles were meant to remove all the idolatrous evil from the land. By reading Ezra and Nehemiah this hope was only partially fulfilled. Idolatry was forsaken, but other evils returned.

The terms"detestable" (BDB 1055) and "abominations" (BDB 1072) are used together in Ezek. 5:11; 7:20; 11:18,21; and Jer. 16:18.

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

SPECIAL TOPIC: ABOMINATION (OT)

entries.title: Ezekiel 11:19 "I shall give them one heart, and shall put a new spirit within them"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:19 "I shall give them one heart, and shall put a new spirit within them" The MT has "one" heart, but note the following translations.

  1. LXX ‒ "another heart"
  2. Peshitta ‒ "a new heart"
  3. REB ‒ "singleness of heart"
  4. NIV ‒ "an undivided heart"

If "one," then it denotes

  1. loyalty to YHWH
  2. unity of Jacob's children (cf. Ezek. 37:15-23)

Because of (1) the parallelism within Ezek. 11:19 and (2) the textual parallel of Ezek. 36:26-27, I think the concept of "new" fits best. Not just restoration, but reorientation from an outward performance standard to an inner motivation based on divine performance (cf. Deut. 30:3-9). It is not just a new day for the children of Jacob, but for the children of Adam!

This is the new covenant (cf. Luke 22:20; 1 Cor. 11:25; 2 Cor. 3:3,6; Heb. 8:6-13; 9:15; 12:24) described in Jer. 31:31-34 and Ezek. 36:22-36. Israel had been characterized by Moses as being stiff-necked, hard-faced, and hard-hearted (see SPECIAL TOPIC: STUBBORNNESS); now they will have a soft heart (i.e. obedient heart, cf. Ezek. 36:27) that is turned toward God (cf. Ezek. 16:60-63).

This is a good example of both God's sovereignty and individual responsibility in the sense that this same phrase is repeated in Ezek. 18:31, where the people are commanded to make themselves a new heart and a new spsirit. Yet, again in Ezek. 36:26, it says that YHWH will give them a new heart and a new spirit. Here is the paradox of God's sovereignty and human responsibility! At this point let me insert three theological Special Topics that deal with this issue.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ELECTION/PREDESTINATION AND THE NEED FOR A THEOLOGICAL BALANCE

SPECIAL TOPIC: PREDESTINATION (Calvinism) vs. HUMAN FREE WILL (Arminianism)

SPECIAL TOPIC: EASTERN LITERATURE (biblical paradoxes)

entries.title: Ezekiel 11:20 "that they may walk in My statutes and keep My ordinances, and do them"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:20 "that they may walk in My statutes and keep My ordinances, and do them" Obedience is crucial! It is not optional. These are conditional covenants! Notice the repetition used for emphasis.

  1. "walk," BDB 229, KB 246, Qal imperfect, cf. Deut. 5:33; 8:6; 10:12; 11:22; 13:4-5; 19:9; 26:17; 28:9; 30:16 (SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PATH, THE WAY)
  2. "keep," BDB 1036, KB 1581, Qal imperfect, cf. Deut. 2:4; 4:2,6,9,15,23,40 (SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP)
  3. "do,"  BDB 793, KB 889, Qal perfect with waw, cf. Deut. 4:1,3,6,13,14,16,23,25

▣ "Then they will be my people and I will be their God" These are covenant terms (cf. Gen. 17:8; Exod. 6:7; Ezek. 14:11; 34:30; 36:28; 37:27). This was so important for these exiled people to hear because they wondered if YHWH would keep His covenant with Israel's descendants. They wondered if they had been rejected. They wondered if their sin had totally altered their relationship with YHWH.

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT PROMISES TO THE PATRIARCHS

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT REQUIREMENTS OF ISRAEL

entries.title: Ezekiel 11:21 "their detestable things and abominations"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:21 "their detestable things and abominations" See SPECIAL TOPIC: ABOMINATION (OT)

▣ "I shall bring their conduct down on their heads" Humans are responsible for their choices and actions! See note at Ezek. 9:10.

entries.title: Ezekiel 11:22
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:22 This is referring to the portable throne chariot of YHWH, first seen by Ezekiel in chapter 1 and seen again in chapter 10. In Ezek. 11:23 it moves from the temple to the Mt. of Olives and then in Ezek. 11:24 it moves to the east to be with the exiles in Babylon.

11:23 This shows the depth of the idolatry of the city of Jerusalem and particularly the priests (cf. Ezek. 8) that YHWH would have to leave the place where He had chosen to dwell (i.e. the temple) and go to be with the exiles, who would become the nucleus of His new covenant community. See specific idolatry in Ezek. 8.

entries.title: Ezekiel 11:24 "I had seen"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:24 "I had seen" This VERB (BDB 906, KB 1157, Qal PERFECT) is one of the terms used to describe a prophet (i.e. "seer."

SPECIAL TOPIC: PROPHET (the different Hebrew terms)

entries.title: Ezekiel 11:25 "I told the exiles all the things God had shown me"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:25 "I told the exiles all the things God had shown me" This refers to the elders who were mentioned in Ezek. 8:1. Therefore, chapters 8-11 form a literary unit.

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

  1. Why did the elders come to Ezekiel?
  2. What does the series of idolatry in chapter 8 mean?
  3. Why is the description of the Cherubim and the portable throne chariot in chapter 10 slightly different from chapter 1?
  4. Why is Ezek. 11:16 and 23 so significant to the exiles?
  5. Describe the significance of Ezek. 11:19 in relationship to the New Covenant of Jeremiah and the NT emphasis on individual responsibility.

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Ezekiel 12:2 "you live in the midst of the rebellious house"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:2 "you live in the midst of the rebellious house" Shockingly, this described the covenant people living and worshiping in Jerusalem (cf. Ezek. 2:5,7,8; 3:7; 20:8; Isa. 6:5,9-13; 29:13).

▣ "who have eyes to see but do not see, who have ears to hear but do not hear" Spiritual blindness and deafness has always been a problem for the children of Jacob (cf. Deut. 29:1-4; 32:5; Isa. 1:2-3; 6:9,10; Jer. 5:21; 6:10; Zech. 7:11; Matt. 13:13, 14; Mark 8:18; John 9:39-41; 12:39-40; Acts 28:26, 27) and all fallen humanity in general! The results of Eden are pervasive!

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FALL OF MANKIND

entries.title: Ezekiel 12:3 "son of man"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:3 "son of man" See note at Ezek. 2:1.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SON OF MAN

▣ "prepare for yourself baggage for exile" Ezekiel is to pack bags as if he were being exiled (he had done this very thing in 597 B.C.). The VERB (BDB 793, KB 889) is the first of two Qal IMPERTAIVES.

▣ "go into exile" This VERB's (BDB 162, KB 191) basic meaning is "to uncover" or "to remove," but here it is used for going into exile (cf. Jdg. 18:30; 2 Kgs. 17:23; 25:21; Isa. 5:13; Jer. 1:3; 52:27; Lam. 1:3; Ezek. 12:3; 39:23; Amos 1:5; 5:5; 6:7; 7:11,17; Micah 1:16). It is the second Qal IMPERATIVE.

▣ "by day in their sight" "In their sight" (BDB 744) is repeated twice for emphasis. It is a wordplay on their blindness mentioned in Ezek. 12:2.

This wordplay continues in the phrase "perhaps they will understand," which is literally the verb "to see" (BDB 906, KB 1157, Qal IMPERFECT).

Some modern theologians have taken literary phrases like this and Jer. 26:3; 36:3,7 and have asserted that YHWH does not know how free moral human agents will act. It is called "Open Theism." In my opinion all truth comes in tension-filled pairs. There are theological ditches on both sides. In this case the two extremes are

  1. God's sovereignty chose some to heaven and others to hell (no human choice at all)
  2. Human choice is ultimate and free and unknown by God (human choice is the deciding factor)

Our text is a literary statement, not a theological doctrine! YHWH desires that none should perish (cf. Ezek. 18:30-32), but He requires a repentant, faithful human response.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE BIBLE IN EASTERN LITERATURE (biblical paradoxes)

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

entries.title: Ezekiel 12:3-6
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 12:3-6 This describes in dramatic symbolism the fall of Jerusalem brought about by Nebuchadneaazr's army in 586 B.C.

entries.title: Ezekiel 12:5 "Dig a hole through the wall"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:5 "Dig a hole through the wall" This refers to the wall of his house, which was made of dried bricks (little wood was available in southern Mesopotamia). Obviously Ezekiel's activity caught the people's attention. The noise of breaking through the walls right after dark (cf. Ezek. 12:4,6) caused quite a disturbance.

The VERB "dig" (BDB 369, KB 365) is the third Qal IMPERATIVE in this context. Ezekiel's dramatic actions were not his own design, but YHWH's (cf. Ezek. 12:6,7). This action mimicked the siege techniques of the Neo-Babylonian army in Jerusalem.

entries.title: Ezekiel 12:6 "in the dark"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:6 "in the dark" This rare term (BDB 759, KB 832) occurs only here and Gen. 15:17. Both occur in visions.

  1. Genesis 15, of YHWH removing Canaanites from Canaan because of their sin and giving the land to Israel
  2. Ezekiel 12, of YHWH about to remove the remaining Judeans from Jerusalem

▣ "You shall cover your face so that you shall not see the land, for I have set you as a sign before the house of Israel" This probably relates to King Zedekiah (called "the prince" in vv. 10,12) who attempted escape from Jerusalem during the neo-Babylonian siege (cf. 2 Kgs. 25:1-7; Jer. 39:4), as do Ezek. 12:10 and 12. He was caught and blinded by Nebuchadnezzar II at Riblah (cf. Ezek. 12:13).

For the covenant people there were two things which they depended on

  1. YHWH's covenant promises about Jerusalem (Deuteronomy and Isaiah)
  2. YHWH's promises about a Davidic king (2 Samuel 7; 1 Chronicles 17)

For both of these to be taken and destroyed was a theological blow that was unimaginable for them. They had forgotten the conditional nature of all the covenant promises!

SPECIAL TOPIC: KINGS OF THE DIVIDED MONARCHY

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

entries.title: Ezekiel 12:8
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 12:8 YHWH communicated to Ezekiel regularly as he performed the previous revelation.

entries.title: Ezekiel 12:9 "the rebellious house"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 12:9 "the rebellious house" This phrase refers to the exiles (cf. Ezek. 2:5-8). The term "rebellion" (BDB 598) is used often by Ezekiel (cf. Ezek. 2:5,6,7,8; 3:9,26; 12:2 [twice], 3,9,25; 17:12; 23:3; 44:6).

entries.title: Ezekiel 12:10 "Say to them"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 12:10 "Say to them" This (BDB 55; KB 65) Qal INFINITIVE is repeated twice (Ezek. 12:10 and Ezek. 12:11) to emphasize that Ezekiel is modeling the future judgment of YHWH on idolatrous Jerusalem.

entries.title: Ezekiel 12:11 "a sign"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:11 "a sign" This term (BDB 69) basically means "wonder," "sign," or "portent." Here it is used to show YHWH's control of future events (i.e. Ezek. 12:6,11; 24:24,27; 1 Kgs. 13:3,5; 2 Chr. 32:24;31). In the Ancient Near East a military defeat demonstrated the power of one national god over another. Israel was defeated because of her covenant disobedience, not YHWH's impotence! Passages such as this demonstrate His omnipotence and control!

SPECIAL TOPIC: SIGN (OT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: BIBLE (its uniqueness and inspiration)

▣ "As I have done, so it will be done to them" Notice these are words from YHWH for Ezekiel to speak to the exiles. They show

  1. the power of YHWH's word (cf. Isa. 44:24-28; 45:23; 55:11; Matt. 24:35)
  2. that Ezekiel is a true prophet (i.e. his prophecies came true)

Both of these theological items are crucial, especially when Ezekiel begins to prophesy about the restoration!

▣ "they will go into exile, into captivity" The "they" refers to the few in Judah and Jerusalem who will escape the destruction and horror of the invasion (cf. Ezek. 12:16).

The terms "exile" (BDB 163) and "captivity" (BDB 985) are parallel. Judgment is coming! YHWH will do it! His own people will be taken out of the land (cf. Jer. 13:19; 15:2; 20:4,6) which He promised to their fathers! YHWH is no respecter of persons. He removed the evil Canaanites (cf. Gen. 15:12-22), now He will remove evil Judah.

SPECIAL TOPIC: CONSEQUENCES OF IDOLATRY

entries.title: Ezekiel 12:12 "They will dig a hole"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:12 "They will dig a hole" This refers to the attendants (cf. v. 4) of Zedekiah, who apparently dug a secret hole in the wall of Jerusalem for the king to secretly escape.

Surprisingly, the LXX and Peshitta, followed by the RSV and NRSV, have "he." The UBS Text Project, p. 33, gives "they" a "B" rating. It is simply a literary way of referring to Zedekiah and his entourage (cf. v. 14).

entries.title: Ezekiel 12:13 "I shall also spread My net over him"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:13 "I shall also spread My net over him" This refers to the capture of King Zedekiah. It was YHWH who planned and executed (by means of the Neo-Babylonian army) his capture (i.e. 5:10,12; 6:8; 12:14,15; 20:23; 22:15; 36:19).

The imagery used is for a "net" (BDB 440, cf. Ezek. 17:20; 19:8), which denotes either

  1. a fishing net
    1. casting, Ezek. 12:13; 32:3
    2. dragging, Ezek. 26:5,14; 47:10
  2. a snare (for birds)

▣ "the Chaldeans" See SPECIAL TOPIC: CHALDEANS

▣ "yet he will not see it" See 2 Kgs. 25:1-7; Jer. 39:1-10, especially Ezek. 12:7. Zedekiah will be blinded by Nebuchadnezzar, just after his failed attempt to escape.

▣ "he will die there" The blinded and exiled Davidic King Zedekiah will die in captivity (cf. Jer. 52:11).

The king that would not "see" now can not "see" (cf. Isa. 6:9-13). The result of his faithless reign was destruction and exile (cf. Jeremiah 39).

12:14
NASB, NRSV, JPSOA, LXX  "his helpers"
NKJV, Peshitta  "to help him"
TEV  "all the members of his court and
  his advisers and bodyguards"
NJB  "his army"
REB  "body guard"

The UBS Text Project, p. 34, mentions:

  1. the MT has "his guard" (עזרה, BDB 740 I, MASCULINE NOUN)
  2. the Massoretic scholars suggested (Qere) "his help" (עזרו, BDB 740 I, FEMININE NOUN)

SPECIAL TOPIC: MASORETIC TEXT

▣ "I shall scatter to every wind" This VERB (BDB 279, KB 280, Piel IMPERFECT) is used in Ezek. 5:2, which describes Ezekiel's prophetic acts of judgment (see note at Ezek. 12:13).

"Every wind" is an idiom for every direction (i.e. complete exile).

entries.title: Ezekiel 12:15
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:15 This verse, which describes the exile of Judah into all the surrounding nations, can be viewed theologically in two ways.

  1. This is the consequence of covenant rebellion predicted in Deuteronomy (i.e. Deut. 4:27; 28:64; 29:28).
  2. This had a secondary effect of forcing Israel to fulfill her missionary mandate (similar to the dispersion of the Tower of Babel). Ezekiel makes this missionary mandate definite in Ezek. 36:20-21, 22-38!

▣ "they will know" This VERB (BDB 393, KB 390, Qal PERFECT) is used in a special sense in Ezekiel. It describes YHWH's desire that His people, all people, know (in the sense of intimate personal relationship, i.e. Gen. 4:1; Jer. 1:5) Him. The characteristic phrase "they will know that I am the Lord" first occurs in the covenant context of the exodus (cf. Exod. 6:7; 7:5,17; 16:12; 29:46). The phrase refers to future actions of YHWH, positive and negative. All His acts are revelations of His character and purposes!

SPECIAL TOPIC: KNOW

entries.title: Ezekiel 12:16 "But I will spare a few of them"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:16 "But I will spare a few of them" The VERB (BDB 451, KB 451, Hiphil PERFECT) is used in several senses by Ezekiel.

  1. spare, Ezek. 6:8; 12:16
  2. the rest, Ezek. 34:18
  3. some survivors, Ezek. 14:22
  4. what remains, Ezek. 39:14,28; 48:15,18,21

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE REMNANT, three senses.

▣ "the sword, the famine, the pestilence" These are the three major enemies of a city under siege (cf. Ezek. 5:12; 6:11-12; 7:15; 14:21). These are mentioned repeatedly in Deuteronomy (esp. Deuteronomy 27-29).

▣ "and may know that I am the Lord" The goal of a "chosen people" was to be a means of revelation to the nations. Israel was called to be a kingdom of priests (cf. Exod. 19:5-6), but she failed.

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

entries.title: Ezekiel 12:18
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:18 Ezekiel is told to emulate the fear of the people of Judah facing invasion (cf. Ezek. 12:19; Deut. 28:65).

  1. eat bread with trembling (BDB 950)
  2. drink water
    1. with quivering (BDB 919)
    2. with anxiety (BDB 178)

It is possible that this is a reversal of the Exodus meal (cf. Exodus 11-12)! YHWH gave them the land (cf. Gen. 15:12-21), but now He takes it away!

entries.title: Ezekiel 12:19 "the people of the land"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:19 "the people of the land" In the earlier parts of the OT this phrase means the landed nobility, but after the exile and in Jesus' day it speaks of the poorest people of the land. Here it refers to Ezekiel's fellow exiles.

SPECIAL TOPIC: PEOPLE OF THE LAND

entries.title: Ezekiel 12:20
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:20 Two terms describe YHWH's judgment of Judah.

  1. the VERB "will be laid waste," BDB 351, KB 349, Qal IMPERFECT, cf. Ezek. 6:6; 25:19; 30:7
  2. the NOUN "desolation," BDB 1031, cf. Ezek. 6:14; 14:15,16; 15:8; 23:33; also used often in the prophecies against the nations, chapters 25-32

entries.title: Ezekiel 12:21-25
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:21-25 There are two stated reasons why the exiles were holding out hope that Jerusalem would not fall and that they might return.

  1. Ezekiel's prophecies were far into the future and would not affect them, Ezek. 12:22-23,26-28.
  2. There were other prophets who were predicting the opposite of Jeremiah and Ezekiel.

entries.title: Ezekiel 12:22 "the days are long and every vision fails"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 12:22 "the days are long and every vision fails" This was a proverb spoken by the rebellious house of Israel (cf. Ezek. 12:27) that God was not going to fulfill His prophecy through Ezekiel. Ezekiel started preaching in the fifth year of the exile and the city of Jerusalem did not fall until the thirteenth year of the exile. Delay does not mean YHWH's word will not be accomplished (cf. Ezek. 12:23,25,28). Ezekiel often quotes (or alludes to) popular proverbs (cf. Ezek. 16:44; 18:2,3) or parables (cf. Ezek. 17:2; 24:3).

entries.title: Ezekiel 12:24 "false"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:24 "false" See SPECIAL TOPIC: EMPTY, VAIN, FALSE, NOTHINGNESS

▣ "divination" This (BDB 890) was strictly forbidden for the people of God. It is an attempt by humans to know and control future events! The fact that a prophet would use this forbidden method to know God's will shows the degradation of the leadership (cf. Lev. 19:26; Deut. 18:10-12; Ezek. 13:6,7,9,23; 21:21,22,23,29; 22:28; Jer. 14:14).  For an interesting discussion of occult practices in the OT see Synonyms of the Old Testament by Robert G. Girdlestone, pp. 296-302, and Dictionary of Biblical Imagery, pp. 608-610.

SPECIAL TOPIC: DIVINATION

SPECIAL TOPIC: MAGIC

entries.title: Ezekiel 12:25 "'I shall speak the word and perform it,' declares the Lord God"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 12:25 "'I shall speak the word and perform it,' declares the Lord God" Also note Ezek. 6:10; 12:28; 17:24; 22:14; Isa. 14:24; 55:6-13. YHWH's word is sure (i.e. Isa. 55:9-11), but often His patience and longsuffering are misunderstood.

entries.title: Ezekiel 12:26-28
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:26-28 See note at Ezek. 12:21-25.

entries.title: Ezekiel 13:1 "Then the word of the Lord came to me saying"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 13:1 "Then the word of the Lord came to me saying" This chapter is an amplification of Ezek. 12:24, dealing with "false" prophets.

entries.title: Ezekiel Contextual Insights
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
EZEKIEL 13

PARAGRAPH DIVISIONS OF MODERN TRANSLATIONS

13:17-19 13:17-19 13:17-19 13:17-18a 13:17-19

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Ezekiel 13:2 "prophesy against the prophets of Israel"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:2 "prophesy against the prophets of Israel" Another category of Judean society is condemned! There are six charges brought against these prophets.

  1. they prophesied from their own inspiration
  2. they followed their own spirit
  3. they have seen nothing
  4. they have not gone into the breaches for My people
  5. they see falsehood
  6. they have misled My people

The question, "How do you know a false prophet?" is extremely important (see full notes on the following texts online, Deut. 13:1-5; 18:21-22; Matt. 7; 1 John 4:1-3). This passage in Ezekiel is reminiscent of Jeremiah, chapters 23; 28; 29.

The VERB "prophesy" (BDB 612, KB 659) is used twice in this verse.

  1. Niphal IMPERATIVE
  2. Niphal PARTICIPLE

The NOUN "prophets" (nabi, BDB 611) is also used. See Special Topic following.

A good discussion of the characteristics of false prophets is found in The Hermeneutical Spiral by Grant R. Osborne, pp. 210-211.

SPECIAL TOPIC: PROPHECY (OT), I. B.

▣ "who prophesy from their own inspiration" See 2 Pet. 2:1-3 description of false prophets. The Hebrew term behind "inspiration" is "hearts" (BDB 524).

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEART

▣ "'Listen to the word of the Lord'" The VERB "listen" is literally "hear" (BDB 1033, KB 1570, Qal IMPERATIVE). YHWH is addressing the false prophets. This is a common VERB in the prophets. Notice a sample of who/what is addressed.

  1. Ezek. 3:17 ‒ Ezekiel
  2. Ezek. 6:3; 36:1,4 ‒ the mountains of Israel
  3. Ezek. 13:2 ‒ false prophets
  4. Ezek. 16:35 ‒ harlot
  5. Ezek. 18:25; 33:7,30 ‒ house of Israel
  6. Ezek. 20:47 ‒ forest of the Negev
  7. Ezek. 25:3 ‒ sons of Ammon
  8. Ezek. 34:7,9 ‒ shepherds (i.e. leaders)
  9. Ezek. 37:4 ‒ the dry bones

SPECIAL TOPIC: LISTEN/HEAR (shema), I. B.

entries.title: Ezekiel 13:3 "the Lord God"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:3 "the Lord God" This title is a combination of the terms

  1. Adon ‒ BDB 10 (SPECIAL TOPIC: LORD [adon and kurios])
  2. YHWH ‒ BDB 217 (SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.)

▣ "'Woe'" This is the literary marker (BDB 222) for a prophetic literary form known as a funeral dirge. It is common in Isaiah (e.g. Isa. 5:8,11,18, 20, 21,22) and Jeremiah (e.g. Jer. 22:13,18 [four times]), but found in Ezekiel only in Ezek. 13:3,18 and 34:2.

Several of the chapters in Isaiah begin with "Woe" (cf. Isaiah 28; 29; 30; 31; 33).

▣ "foolish prophets" This seems to refer to self deception (cf. Jer. 23:21-22), not low intelligence. The ADJECTIVE (BDB 614, KB 663 II) is used to describe Israel in Deut. 32:6,21.

There is a Hebrew word play between

  1. prophet ‒ נביאום
  2. foolish ‒ נבלום

SPECIAL TOPIC: FOOLISH, #3

▣ "who are following their own spirit" Here is the problem! It is their own spirit that is leading them, not God's Spirit! They speak their word in God's name!

SPECIAL TOPIC: SPIRIT IN THE BIBLE

entries.title: Ezekiel 13:4 "your prophets have been like foxes among ruins"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:4 "your prophets have been like foxes among ruins" Their only concern was for themselves (Ezek. 13:5). The word "foxes" (BDB 1043) may be a theological wordplay on

  1. "ruins" (BDB 352) ‒ places where foxes live (i.e. Jerusalem will be a place of ruins)
  2. "foxes" ‒ some desert animals that lived in the ruins of destroyed cities became associated with the demonic (NEB)
  3. "foxes" ‒ this term may also imply that these false prophets fed on the people (cf. Ps. 63:10)

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE DEMONIC IN THE OT, B. #6

entries.title: Ezekiel 13:5
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:5 This verse uses siege imagery to describe the false prophets' lack of action on behalf of the covenant people.

  1. did not go into the breaches ‒ BDB 829, "breaches" were holes made in the walls of cities by the enemy (cf. Isa. 58:12; Amos 4:3; 9:11)
  2. did not fortify the wall ‒ BDB 154, a good parallel to both images is Ezek. 22:30

Israel's only hope is in their God. These false religionists do not know Him.

▣ "the day of the Lord" This is imagery for the coming of YHWH's personal presence (cf. Ezek. 7:10,19; 30:3; Isa. 2:2; 13:6,9; 22:5; 34:8; Jer. 46:10; Joel 1:15; 2:1,11,31; 3:14; Amos 5:18,20; Zeph. 1:7,14; Zech. 14:1; Mal. 4:5). Israel often expected it to be a day of blessing and affirmation, but here it was a day of judgment. Judah was not in compliance with the Mosaic Covenant.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE DAY OF THE LORD (NT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: THAT DAY

entries.title: Ezekiel 13:6-7
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:6-7 These false prophets are characterized by several terms.

  1. they see falsehood (literally "vanity" or "nothingness," BDB 996; see SPECIAL TOPIC: EMPTY, VAIN, FALSE, NOTHINGNESS
  2. they see lying divination (BDB 890 construct 469; see SPECIAL TOPIC: DIVINATION), cf. Ezek. 22:28; Micah 2:11
  3. the Lord has not sent them (BDB 1018, KB 1511, Qal PERFECT, cf. Jer. 14:14; 23:21)
  4. their message is not from YHWH, Ezek. 13:7 (BDB 180, KB 210, Piel PERFECT)

They claim to be YHWH's representatives, but they knowingly speak their own messages (cf. Ezek. 13:6c). These false prophets/preachers/teachers are always a problem for the people of God, Old Testament and New Testament.

SPECIAL TOPIC: FALSE TEACHERS

▣ "the Lord declares" This is exactly the prophetic formula that Ezekiel and Jeremiah used. It was so difficult to know who was/is from God and who was/is not (cf. Jeremiah 28-29). See the important note at Ezek. 13:2.

entries.title: Ezekiel 13:9 "My hand is against the prophets who see false visions and utter lying divinations"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:9 "My hand is against the prophets who see false visions and utter lying divinations" There are three things God says He will do to these false prophets.

  1. they will lose their leadership ("council of My people," cf. Ps. 111:1)
  2. their names will be taken out of the register of the people of God (cf. Ps. 87:6; similar to the lists referred to in Neh. 7:64)
  3. they will not enter the Promised Land (this message is addressed to false prophets in both Babylon and Judah).

They are completely removed from God's people!

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE TWO BOOKS OF GOD

SPECIAL TOPIC: APOSTASY

13:10
NASB, NRSV, NJB, REB, JPSOA  "they have misled My people"
NKJV  "because they have seduced
  My people"
TEV  "the prophets misled My
  people"
Peshitta  "they have deceived My
  people"
NET  "they had led My people
  astray"
LXX  "caused my people to err"

The VERB (BDB 380, KB 377, Hiphil PERFECT) is found only here in the prophets. It occurs only one other time in Song of Songs 1:7, where it is translated "veils," NASB; "wanders," REV.

  1. In Arabic the root means "to exceed a just limit" or "one who deviates from the right path."
  2. In Ethiopian it means "apostasy," "superstition," or "idolatry."

It seems that the term is used of not following the right path or way. YHWH's word was seen as a clearly marked path/road (cf. Ps. 89:15; 119:105; Prov. 6:2; Isa. 2:5; 1 John 1:6-7). To deviate from this path was to knowingly violate YHWH's covenant (e.g. Job 6:18; Ps. 16:11; 17:4; 25:4,10; Prov. 2:8,13,19,20; 3:6; 4:18; Isa. 2:3; 3:12). The prophets are willfully self-deluded and leading others astray also.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PATH, THE WAY

▣ "saying 'Peace' when there is no peace" This was the problem of the false prophets (cf. Ezek. 13:16). They were preaching the destruction of Neo-Babylon and the restoration of Israel (possibly following Isaiah's insistence that Jerusalem would not fall, but things had changed, the covenant promises were conditional on covenant obedience). The prophets Ezekiel and Jeremiah were prophesying judgment and destruction (cf. Jer. 8:18; 28-29), not peace and safety!

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

SPECIAL TOPIC: PEACE (OT)

▣ "a wall" This is a rare term (BDB 300) used only here in the OT. Kimchi (a Jewish commentator of the Middle Ages) says it means "an inferior partition." It is used in the sense of pretending to build something strong, but which is really very weak (i.e. Neh. 4:3). Here, it is used symbolically for the theological pronouncements of these false prophets.

▣ "they plastered over the whitewash" They hid their false religious pronouncements with a thin coating of religious language (cf. Ezek. 13:11)! There may be a wordplay between "plaster" (תפל, BDB 1074 II) and "tasteless" or "unsatisfying prophecies" (תפל, BDB 1074 II, cf. Lam. 2:14).

entries.title: Ezekiel 13:11
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:11 YHWH will expose the weakness of their false prophecies (cf. Ezek. 38:22) using imagery from nature.

  1. flooding rain, Ezek. 13:13
  2. hailstones, Ezek. 13:13
  3. a violent wind, Ezek. 13:13

Against these three the true nature of the wall (i.e. prophecies) of these false prophets will be clearly revealed (i.e. "fall," BDB 656, KB 709, Qal IMPERFECT, twice in Ezek. 13:11 and the Qal PERFECT in Ezek. 13:12).

In the MT these three natural occurrences are not grammatically parallel, but from the context they are.

NASB, NKJV, JPSOA  "and you"
NRSV, NJB   ——
TEV, REB  "I will send"
LXX  "I will give"
Peshitta  "I will bring"
Vulgate  "I will make"

The MT has "and you" (ואתנה, BDB 61) but BDB suggests an alternate vocalization (cf. Gen. 31:6; Ezek. 13:11,20; 34:17). The UBS Text Project, p. 36, gives "and you" a "C" rating (considerable doubt) and suggests the translation, "as for you (O stones)." This is either:

  1. the personification of the hailstone judgment
  2. an affirmation that YHWH is the direct cause of weather judgment(s), cf. Isa. 28:2; 30:30

entries.title: Ezekiel 13:13 "in My wrath. . .in wrath"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:13 "in My wrath. . .in wrath" Wrath (BDB 404, cf. Ezek. 13:15) is anthropomorphic language.

SPECIAL TOPIC: GOD DESCRIBED AS HUMAN (anthropomorphism)

entries.title: Ezekiel 13:14 "its foundation is laid bare"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 13:14 "its foundation is laid bare" This is an idiom of total destruction (cf. Micah 1:6 and possibly Hab. 3:13). The VERB is a Niphal PERFECT (BDB 162, KB 191). The term in the Niphal is often used of nakedness (cf. Ezek. 16:36; 23:29). YHWH will show the true nature of the false prophets' (male and female) messages of hope and security.

entries.title: Ezekiel 13:15
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 13:15 This is a proverb that YHWH directs to these false prophets. All of their efforts and words will come to naught. No lasting results! Their words and they themselves are no more!

entries.title: Ezekiel 13:16 "peace"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:16 "peace" The term "peace" (BDB 1022; see note at v. 10) is used in two senses in this verse.

  1. The false teachers used it in the sense of the political autonomy of Judah.
  2. Ezekiel uses it in the sense of a restored relationship with YHWH.

Judah will fall and become a vassal nation to Neo-Babylon, but the exiles who trust and obey will be restored (i.e. in their heart and one day to their land)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: PEACE (OT, shalom)

entries.title: Ezekiel 13:17 "set your face against"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:17 "set your face against" The VERB (BDB 962, KB 1321, Qal IMPERATIVE) is used here in the sense of "direct your intention against" (i.e. Ezek. 6:2; 14:8; 15:7; 21:2; 29:2; 35:2; Lev. 20:5; Jer. 21:10; 44:11). The face symbolized the person and thereby one's personal attention to someone or some thing.

YHWH repeats His opposition to these false prophets (men and women) by using the phrase "prophesy against them" (BDB 612, KB 659, Niphal IMPERATIVE) at the end of Ezek. 13:17!

▣ "the daughters of your people who are prophesying from their own inspiration" Apparently, along with the false prophets, there were false prophetesses (cf. Ezek. 13:23). Women active in God's service was/is not an unusual thing. However, as there are false prophets, there are also false prophetesses.

SPECIAL TOPIC: WOMEN IN THE BIBLE

entries.title: Ezekiel 13:18 "sew magic bands on all their wrists"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:18 "sew magic bands on all their wrists" This group is seen more like sorceresses (see note online at Deut. 18:10-11) than prophetesses. The word "magic band" (BDB 492) is found only here (vv. 18, 20) in the OT and has been interpreted several ways.

  1. as amulets
  2. as phylacteries (Origen's Hexapla; see SPECIAL TOPIC: PHYLACTERIES)
  3. as pillows (LXX, JPSOA, KJV)
  4. bands that bind another person's will (Akkadian root)

The phrase "on all their wrists" is literally "all joints of the hands" (BDB 69 CONSTRUCT BDB 388). This seems to be similar to modern voodoo with its spells and incantations.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MAGIC

▣ "make veils for the heads of persons of every stature" The NOUN "veils" (BDB 705) appears only here and in Ezek. 13:21 in the OT, possibly from Akkadian root, "to loosen." KB (607) calls it a robe of coarse material, while LXX has "scarf," or "head covering." Whatever these items were, they were attempts to control the destinies of people (both negatively as curses and positively as charms, cf. Ezek. 13:19). This is the essence of divination and the occult. It is an expression of egocentric, superstitious, fallen humanity!

SPECIAL TOPIC: VEIL, SHAWL, COVERING

SPECIAL TOPIC: DIVINATION

▣ "but preserve the lives of others for yourselves" This shows that whatever their occultic practices were, they were done for self interest! These false prophets/prophetesses wanted to destroy some people and protect others, but not for the glory of YHWH rather for their own selfish, manipulative purposes! Religion can be self-deceptive, superstitious, and destructive!

entries.title: Ezekiel 13:19 "for a handful of barley and fragments of bread"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 13:19 "for a handful of barley and fragments of bread" It seems improbable that this refers to the payment that these false prophetesses will receive because it is so meager. However, this phrase is very ambiguous because of the rarity of the words "handful" (BDB 1043) and "fragments" (BDB 837). In Anatolia and later in Syria handfuls of barley and bread were used as a means of divination and this seems to be the possible historical allusion.

entries.title: Ezekiel 13:20-21
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:20-21 YHWH will destroy these false spiritualists! He will free their deluded followers!

▣
NASB, REB  "magic bands"
NRSV  "bands"
NKJV  "magic charms"
NJB  "ribbons"
TEV, NET  "wristbands"
Peshitta  "embroidered garments"
LXX  "cushions"
JPSOA  "pads"

The MT has "band" or "fillet" (BDB 492). KB 491 suggests it is from an Akkadian root meaning "to bind one's hands" for magic purposes. This fits the context best.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MAGIC

▣ "birds" The term (BDB 827 III) occurs twice. It is translated "birds" or "flying things" because of the context of "hunt" (BDB 844, KB 1010, Polel PARTICIPLE, twice). However, the term normally means

  1. "to break out" (BDB 827 II, like leprosy, cf. Lev. 13:39)
  2. "to bud" or "to sprout" (BDB 827 I, cf. Exod. 25:31-34; 37:17-20; Isa. 18:5)

This passage is the only place in the OT that the translation "birds" is used. Because of the occultic context it may refer to giving people diseases by means of incantations! See the TEV translation, "I hate the wristbands that you use in your attempt to control life and death. I will rip them off your arms and set free the people that you were controlling."

entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley

entries.title: Ezekiel 13:22
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:22 This verse assumes that the superstition or magic had some psychological effect!

The VERBAL "disheartened" (BDB 456, KB 454, Hiphil INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT) is found only here in this form. Many (KB 454) have assumed it could be a Hiphil PERFECT of a similar root meaning "to cause pain."

  2. What is divination?

14:1 "elders of Israel" This must refer to tribal leaders already in exile in Babylon (cf. Ezek. 8:1, where a group of faithful elders were called "elders of Judah"). These particular ones are idolaters (cf. Ezek. 20:1).

This is Judah's problem, her leaders are not faithful YHWHists!

  1. kings, princes
  2. priests
  3. prophets
  4. elders

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Ezekiel 14:3 "these men have set up idols in their hearts"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
14:3 "these men have set up idols in their hearts" Apparently the idolatry of Jerusalem described in chapter 8 had already spread to the leaders in exile in Babylon (cf. Ezek. 14:4,6,11; 7:19; 20:7-8). These elders looked like YHWHists, but in the secret place of their hearts (God knows the heart), they were corrupted by pagan worship and theology.

The term "idols" comes from several possible roots. The Jewish Study Bible, p. 1066, translates it as "dung balls" (BDB 165, KB 192, NIDOTTE, vol. 1, pp. 864-865) see note at Ezek. 6:4. The term is used almost exclusively in Ezekiel (39 times) and only once in Jeremiah (i.e. Jer. 50:2) and never in Isaiah. It originally occurred in the key covenant passages of Lev. 26:30 and Deut. 29:17.

SPECIAL TOPIC: IDOLATRY

▣ "stumbling block" This term (BDB 506) is used often in Ezekiel (cf. Ezek. 3:20; 14:3,4,7; 18:30; 21:15; 44:12). Its basic meaning is "to stumble" or "the means by which one stumbles." The origin of its idiomatic usage comes from

  1. YHWH's word or covenant was characterized as a clearly marked path (i.e. Ps. 119:105; see SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PATH, THE WAY)
  2. faith originally meant to be stable, walking easily in the path (see SPECIAL TOPIC: BELIEVE, TRUST, FAITH AND FAITHFULNESS IN THE OT)
  3. therefore, to stumble is parallel to leaving the path, to stumbling in the path

This term came to have a Messianic aspect in Isaiah (cf. Isa. 8:14; Rom. 9:33; 1 Pet. 2:8). The Messiah (the Cornerstone, Gen. 49:24; Ps. 118:22; Isa. 28:16) will become a stumbling block to some.

SPECIAL TOPIC: CORNERSTONE

▣ "Should I be consulted by them at all" This is a grammatically emphatic sentence (an INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE and an IMPERFECT VERB of the same root [BDB 205, KB 233, Niphal, cf. Ezek. 20:3,31]). The covenant leaders were consulting idols and false prophets, not YHWH (cf. Ezek. 20:3,21). So why should YHWH now allow them to consult Him?

This VERB has a negative connotation in most of its occurrences in Ezekiel (cf. Ezek. 14:10; 20:1-4,31).

SPECIAL TOPIC: DIVINATION

entries.title: Ezekiel 14:4 "speak to them and tell them, ‘Thus says the Lord God'"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
14:4 "speak to them and tell them, ‘Thus says the Lord God'" This is an emphatic construction.

  1. a Piel IMPERATIVE, "speak," BDB 180, KB 201
  2. two Qal PERFECTS, "says," BDB 55, KB 65

YHWH's prophet must address this situation of "apparent" faith!

▣ "I the Lord will be brought to give him an answer" See note at Ezek. 14:7.

▣ "in the matter" There are three options of how to translate this word (UBS Text Project, p. 38).

  1. he (idolator) comes (Qere reading BDB 97, KB 112), בא; Qal PERFECT; same form used earlier in the verse, NRSV
  2. "in it" understood as "according to it," בה (MT; UBS Text Project gives this option a "C" rating)
  3. "in me," the idolator comes to YHWH, בי (RSV, NEB, NJB, TEV), which results in
    1. mercy, forgiveness
    2. judgment (vv. 3,7, Peshitta)

entries.title: Ezekiel 14:5 "who are estranged from Me"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
14:5 "who are estranged from Me" The VERB "estranged" (BDB 266, KB 267, Niphal PERFECT) describes the alienation of YHWH's people from Him because of idolatry. YHWH's people are now strangers/foreigners (cf. Ezek. 7:21; 11:9; 16:22; 28:7,10; 30:12; 31:12) and thus enemies (cf. Isa. 1:4; Ps. 69:8).

SPECIAL TOPIC: CONSEQUENCES OF IDOLATRY

entries.title: Ezekiel 14:6
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
14:6 The phrase "Thus says the Lord God" (Adon YHWH) is used in several senses in Ezekiel.

  1. positive
    1. a call to repentance, Ezek. 14:6
    2. forgiveness of the covenant people, Ezek. 36:33
    3. resurrection, Ezek. 37:12
    4. gathering exiles, Ezek. 37:21
    5. restoration of the fortunes of Jacob and having mercy on the whole house of Israel, Ezek. 39:25
  2. negative
    1. YHWH gives Ezekiel a message that His people will not listen to, Ezek. 2:4; 3:11
    2. prophecies against the false prophets, Ezek. 13:3,8
    3. prophecies against
      (1) apostasy, Ezek. 20:30 (see SPECIAL TOPIC: APOSTASY)
      (2) social justice, Ezek. 45:9
    4. prophecies against the surrounding nations
      (1) Ammon, Ezek. 25:3
      (2) Tyre, Ezek. 28:2
      (3) Cush, Put, Lud, Arabia, Libya, Ezek. 30:2-5
      (4) Gog, Ezek. 39:1
    5. prophecies against Judah, Ezek. 5:8; 6:3; 12:19

▣ As Ezek. 14:4 was emphatic, so too, Ezek. 14:6.

  1. "say" ‒ BDB 55, KB 65, Qal IMPERATIVE
  2. "say" ‒ BDB 55, KB 65, Qal PERFECT

YHWH commands them to do three things (all using one VERBAL root, BDB 996, KB 1427).

  1. repent" (cf. Ezek. 18:30,32; 33:11; Isa. 55:6-7)
  2. "turn away from your idols"
  3. "turn away from all your abominations"

SPECIAL TOPIC: ABOMINATION (OT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE (OT)

entries.title: Ezekiel 14:7 "the immigrants"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
14:7 "the immigrants" Non-Jews were to be treated as equals in the legal realm (cf. Lev. 19:33-34,35). Israel was to deal with them graciously (cf. Lev. 23:22; Deut. 10:19; 24:17; 27:19). Israel had also been an alien in Egypt (cf. Exod. 22:21; 23:9) and knew how it felt (cf. Deut. 16:11)! But, they were required to function within Israel's faith (i.e. Exod. 12:19; Lev. 16:29; 17:8; Num. 9:14; Deut. 1:16; 16:11)

However, in this context, these immigrants are viewed in a negative sense as someone who claimed to worship YHWH but retained their pagan origins in their hearts. These foreigners were

  1. from the Exodus of Egypt (i.e. "mixed multitudes," cf. Exod. 12:38; Num. 11:4)
  2. those who migrated to Canaan
  3. neighbors in the exilic community in Babylon who brought idolatry into the covenant community

▣ "who separates himself from Me" This VERB (BDB 634, KB 684, Niphal IMPERFECT) means to dedicate oneself by separating oneself from ceremonial evil. The NOUN form is used of those in Numbers 6 who separate themselves by vow and restrictions to YHWH (i.e. Nazirites, both male and female). There is a play on words here.

  1. "holy," means separated to God for His service
  2. those who separate themselves (men and women) to God by special vow (Numbers 6).
  3. these idolaters have separated themselves from God to idols

SPECIAL TOPIC: HOLY

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAZIRITE VOW

▣ "I the Lord will be brought to answer him in My own person" What an ominous phrase. YHWH comes personally, not for blessing, but for destruction (cf. Ezek. 14:4; also note Heb. 10:31).

entries.title: Ezekiel 14:8 "I shall set My face against that man"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
14:8 "I shall set My face against that man" As the idolater sets his idol "right before his face" (cf. Ezek. 14:4), so now YHWH sets His face against him (cf. Ezek. 15:7). The face (BDB 815) is an idiom of personal presence (cf. Ezek. 14:4,7).

Notice what YHWH threatens to do to the idolater.

  1. make him a sign (BDB 16)
  2. make him a proverb (BDB 605, possibly "byword," cf. Deut. 28:37; 1 Kgs. 9:7; 2 Chr. 7:20; Ps. 44:14; Jer. 24:9; Joel 2:17)
  3. cut him off from the covenant people (BDB 503, KB 500, Hiphil PERFECT)

entries.title: Ezekiel 14:9
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
14:9 YHWH reveals Himself to true prophets, but hides His word from false prophets. He uses even them for His own purposes (i.e. 1 Kgs. 22:22-23). These false prophets were prophesying "peace" and "security" (cf. Jer. 14:15), but they were lying! The refusal of Judah to repent caused YHWH's judgment to come!

YHWH uses even "evil" for His purposes and plans! One way the ancient Hebrew Scriptures demonstrated monotheism was by attributing all causality to God (i.e. Deut. 32:39; Job 5:18; 12:13-25; Isa. 30:26; 45:7; Hosea 6:1; Amos 3:6).

SPECIAL TOPIC: ONE CAUSALITY

▣ "My hand" See SPECIAL TOPIC: HAND

entries.title: Ezekiel 14:11
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
14:11 The purpose of judgment is restoration (cf. Ezek. 14:22-23)! However, for this to occur, some other things must happen first.

  1. "Israel may no longer stray" (BDB 1073, KB 1766, Qal IMPERFECT, cf. Ezek. 44:10,15; 48:11)
  2. Israel "no longer defile themselves" (BDB 379, KB 375, Hithpael IMPERFECT, cf. Ezek. 37:23)

If these criteria are not met, then they will not be His covenant people (cf. Ezek. 11:20; 34:30; 36:28; 37:27; Exod. 6:7; Lev. 11:45; 22:33; 25:38; 26:12,44,45). The covenant promises are conditional on covenant obedience (cf. Leviticus 26; Deuteronomy 28; 30:1,15,19).

Passages such as this cause me to question if the modern state of Israel is truly the Israel of Promise. They are a secular, European-type, state government. Very few Jews keep or practice the Mosaic Law. The promises to Israel were conditional!

For a good YouTube video on this subject, see Steve Gregg, The Modern State of Israel

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

▣ "they will be My people, and I shall be their God" This is covenant language (cf. Lev. 26:12; Jer. 7:23; 11:4; 30:22; 31:33; 32:38; Ezek. 11:20; 14:11; 36:28; 37:23,27).

entries.title: Ezekiel 14:13
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
14:13 The Jewish Study Bible marginal note (p. 1066) asserts that the "ifs" of Ezek. 14:13,15,17,19 are textual markers for a legal case (i.e. casuistic law).

SPECIAL TOPIC: LAWS IN THE ANCIENT NEAR EAST

▣ "committing unfaithfulness" This VERB (BDB 591, KB 612, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT) comes from the priestly realm and denotes

  1. acts of idolatrous treachery (i.e. idolatry)
  2. marital infidelity in Num. 5:12,27
  3. in Ezekiel for unfaithfulness towards YHWH (cf. Ezek. 15:8; 17:20; 18:24; 20:27; 39:23,26)

This phrase is emphatic by the repetition of the Hebrew root (BDB 591) in the INFINITIVE and the NOUN.

Notice YHWH's reactions.

  1. "I stretch out My hand against it" (i.e. His nation, His capital), which is an idiom of purposeful action
  2. "I destroy (lit. "break the staff," cf. Ezek. 4:16; 5:16) its supply of bread," which denotes famine
  3. "I send famine against it"
  4. "I cut off (i.e. destroy completely) from it both man and beast" (cf. Ezek. 14:7,19,21)
  5. "cause wild beasts to pass through the land" (Ezek. 14:15, cf. Lev. 26:22)
  6. "bring a sword on that country"
  7. "send a plague against that country" (Ezek. 14:19)

All of them are summarized in four severe judgments (Ezek. 14:21; 5:12; Deut. 32:23-24)

  1. sword (BDB 352)
  2. famine (BDB 944)
  3. wild beasts (BDB 312, cf. Lev. 26:22)
  4. plague (BDB 184)

Many of these reflect the covenant warnings of Leviticus 26 and Deuteronomy 28.

entries.title: Ezekiel 14:14 "even though these three men"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
14:14 "even though these three men" It is clear from the OT who Noah (cf. Genesis 6-9) and Job (cf. Job) are. It is not so clear who Daniel (BDB 193) is.

  1. the father-in-law of Enoch, Jubilees 4:20, who surprisingly is not mentioned as an ancient righteous person
  2. a son of David, 1 Chr. 3:1
  3. a priest of the line of Ithamar, Ezra 8:2; Neh. 10:7
  4. a well known Canaanite sage, Ezek. 14:14,20; 28:3
  5. a prophet, hero, administrator under Nebuchadnezzar II from the biblical book of Daniel
  6. an unknown famous righteous person

The biblical Daniel is a contemporary with Ezekiel and may not have had time for his faith and life to be well known (i.e. become a proverb of wisdom and faithfulness). Daniel might really be Danel (or Dan-El, Ezekiel's spelling is different from Dan. 6:16 and is spelled like the hero of the Ugaritic text), a Canaanite sage (from Ras Shamra Ugaritic texts) known for his upright thoughtful life. If this identification is true, then all three examples were not directly related to Abraham.

The problem is that he is involved with the Canaanite pantheon! Therefore, even with all the questions the biblical Daniel seems the best option (cf. Ezek. 28:3). For more historical information of the identity of "Danil," see IVP Biblical Background Commentary (OT), p. 700.

▣ "by their own righteousness they could only deliver themselves" This phrase reflects OT theology of a performance-based righteousness (cf. Ezek. 3:21, or better an OT sense of "blamelessness, like Noah," Gen. 6:9 or Job, Job 1:1). This section is a theological precursor to chapter 18. The people thought that a few faithful worshipers of YHWH would cause YHWH to withhold His wrath (like Gen. 18:22-33, also note Jer. 15:1-4), but this proved not to be true!

SPECIAL TOPIC: BLAMELESS, INNOCENT, GUILTLESS, WITHOUT REPROACH

SPECIAL TOPIC: RIGHTEOUSNESS

The term "deliver" (BDB 664, KB 717, Piel IMPERFECT) in the Piel, usually means "to strip off" in the sense of "plunder" (cf. Exod. 3:22; 12:36; 2 Chr. 20:25). Only here is it translated "deliver" or "save," although the Niphal (cf. Ezek. 14:16,18) and Hiphil (cf. Ezek. 3:19,21; 14:20; 33:19; 34:10) stems have this sense.

A righteous person (in the OT Mosaic sense, cf. Ezek. 3:20-21; 14:12-20; 18:5-32; 33:12-20) can only deliver himself/herself. OT righteousness is not transferable to others. It is an individual performance-based covenant.

14:15
NASB, JPSOA  "depopulate"
NKJV  "empty"
NRSV  "ravage"
TEV  "kill"
NJB  "rob it of its children"
REB  "destroy the population"
Peshitta  "destroy it"
LXX  "take vengeance"

The NJB captures the essence of the VERB (BDB 1013, KB 1491, Piel PERFECT). This is part of the covenant curses (cf., Leviticus 26; Deuteronomy 28). If the Israelites violate YHWH's covenant, their children will die (no posterity, no family joy).

  1. by sword, Deut. 32:35; 1 Sam. 15:33; Lam. 1:20
  2. by wild beasts, Lev. 26:22; Ezek. 5:17; 14:15

entries.title: Ezekiel 14:17 "Let the sword pass through"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 14:17 "Let the sword pass through" This VERB (BDB 716, KB 778) is a Qal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense. The sword (i.e. invasion and exile) became the will and command of YHWH against His own covenant people!

entries.title: Ezekiel 14:21
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 14:21 The four judgments mentioned were common in the ancient world (i.e. Lev. 26:22,25-26; they are also mentioned in the Babylonian flood texts).

entries.title: Ezekiel 14:22 "you will see their conduct and actions"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
14:22 "you will see their conduct and actions" This phrase has been interpreted two contrasting ways.

  1. the wicked receive their just judgment ("actions," BDB 760 is always used in a negative sense)
  2. the wicked are changed by YHWH's judgment and repent (cf. Ezek. 18:21-23)

The question is, does this refer to an illustration of God's justice or an example of a believing, faithful remnant?

It is possible that the message to the exiles was "the current generation does not have to bear the sins of their fathers" (or fellow Israelites). Each person's personal faith and action (cf. Ezekiel 18) will determine one's relationship with YHWH. This is a rare example of an individual emphasis in a corporate society. This will form a crucial aspect of "new" covenant theology (cf. John 1:12; 3:16; Rom. 10:9-13).

SPECIAL TOPIC: What Does It Mean to "Receive," "Believe," "Confess/Profess," and "Call Upon?"

Copyright © 2014 Bible Lessons International

entries.title: Ezekiel 14:22-23
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
14:22-23 The terrible judgments on Judah and Jerusalem were for the purpose of redemption! A new Israel will rise out of the ashes of the old rebellious one. There will be a believing remnant (cf. Ezek. 6:7-9; see SPECIAL TOPIC: REMNANT [three senses]). There will be days of repentance (cf. Ezek. 14:6; see SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE [OT])! There will be a new day of righteousness (cf. Isaiah 55-66).

The tragedy is that even restored Judah/Israel (Ezra, Nehemiah) could not keep the Mosaic Law. The Law's function is clearly spelled out in Galatians 3. The performance-based covenant must become the grace-based "new covenant" of Jer. 31:31-34, described in Ezek. 36:22-36. Fallen humanity cannot approach a holy God with personal righteousness (cf. Eph. 2:8-9)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: REMNANT (three senses)

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Ezekiel 15:2 "how is the wood of the vine better"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
15:2 "how is the wood of the vine better" The vine is often used as a symbol of Israel (cf. Ezek. 19:10; Ps. 80:8-16; Isa. 5:1-7; Hosea 10:1; Rom. 11:17-22). In this brief parable Judah and Jerusalem are given to Neo-Babylon for the burning (cf. Ezek. 19:12; 23:25; Jer. 21:10; 32:28-29; 39:8; 52:13; 2 Chr. 36:19).

Grapevines are not good fuel for cooking because they burn too hot and too quickly! It is also too soft to be used for furniture or construction. One cannot even make a tent peg out of vine wood! It is useless except for producing fruit, but Israel did not produce (cf. Deut. 32:32; Isa. 5:1-7; Jer. 2:21)!

The prophets often symbolized idolatry as an imported vine (cf. Isa. 17:10; Ezek. 8:17).

The personification of trees is not unusual in the OT. Note Jdgs 9:7-15! Parables and riddles are common ways for eastern people to express themselves. In reality chapters 15, 16, and 17 form this genre of literature.

entries.title: Ezekiel 15:4 "fuel. . .consumed"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
15:4 "fuel. . .consumed" There are two terms (the NOUN, lit. "food," BDB 38 and the VERB, BDB 37, KB 46) which form a wordplay found only in Ezekiel (cf. Ezek. 15:4,6; 21:32).

▣ "fire" See SPECIAL TOPIC: FIRE.

entries.title: Ezekiel 15:6 "give"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 15:6 "give" The VERB (BDB 678, KB 733, Qal PERFECT) is used twice in this verse and again in Ezek. 15:7 and 9. YHWH's judgment of Jerusalem is sure.

entries.title: Ezekiel 15:7 "I set (lit. "give") My face against them"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
15:7 "I set (lit. "give") My face against them" See note at Ezek. 14:8. This phrase also appears in the Levitical passage on covenant disobedience (i.e. covenant curses for disobedience, cf. Lev. 26:17), which is alluded to three times in this chapter (and often in Ezekiel).

▣ "Though they have come out of the fire, yet fire will consume them" If they (i.e. the inhabitants of Jerusalem) escape one of the four judgments of YHWH, another will get them (cf. 1 Kgs. 19:17; Isa. 24:18; Amos 9:1-4).

It is possible that this refers to the first two groups of Judeans who were exiled in 605 and 597 B.C. and who were currently in Babylon. They are the potential repentant remnant that YHWH will begin again with (cf. Ezek. 6:7-9; 14:22-23).

entries.title: Ezekiel 15:8 "I will make the land desolate"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
15:8 "I will make the land desolate" "Desolate" (BDB 1031) is a recurrent threat in Jeremiah (15 times) and Ezekiel (21 times). This threat is first stated in the curses of Lev. 26:33 and reiterated by Isaiah (6 times).

▣ "acted unfaithfully" This VERB (BDB 591, KB 612, Qal PERFECT) is first used in Ezek. 14:13 (see note there) and 17:20; 18:24; 20:27; 39:29. The term is mentioned specifically in the penalties for covenant disobedience in Lev. 26:40. It does not appear in Isaiah or Jeremiah. In Ezek. 20:27 the covenant people had a history of disobedience starting from the Exodus (i.e. Exodus 32; Neh. 9:16-32) and continuing.

This parable's imagery sets the literary stage for Jesus' condemnation of Israel in His day (cf. Matt. 21:33-46; Mark 12:1-12; Luke 20:9-19)! I have come to believe that Jesus' Olivet Discourse, Paul's "man of lawlessness" text, and John's book of Revelation all refer to the fall of Jerusalem in A.D. 70. Please look at my exegetical verse-by-verse commentaries on these texts (free online).
