READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

  1. This chapter provides a good opportunity to mention how the interpreter's presuppositions often distort the original author's intent. As an evangelical I have often used this text as an example of individual, personal response being necessary for salvation (i.e. personal relationship; see SPECIAL TOPIC: WHAT DOES IT MEAN TO "RECEIVE," "BELIEVE," "CONFESS/PROFESS," AND "CALL UPON"?). However, in context, it is referring to Judah's claim that it was because of their ancestors' sins that they were suffering (cf. Exod. 20:5; Deut. 5:9). This chapter is more related to the current generation (corporate) rather than individuals of that generation.
     Another way this chapter is used is seen in Ezek. 18:32. It is often linked with John 3:16; 1 Tim. 2:4; and 2 Pet. 3:9 to show YHWH's love for all humans (which is surely true), but this text is really about Israel's descendants (cf. Ezek. 18:30; see SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN). We tend to read our systematic theology into every text. We tend to assign theological content to certain words and then read that definition into every usage of the term (i.e. "repent," "live"). We must discipline ourselves to let the inspired authors speak to their day before we use it in our systematic theologies (which often say more about us than about God! see "Bible Interpretation Seminar").
     Ezekiel is addressing a sinful people who do not think they are sinful, but rather blame their parents and previous generations for YHWH's judgment.

  2. This chapter also offers an opportunity to show how biblical authors present truths in tension-filled pairs. Notice how Ezek. 18:31 demands that the believers "make yourselves a new heart and a new spirit," yet Ezek. 36:26-27 asserts that YHWH will give them a new heart and a new spirit.
    SPECIAL TOPIC: EASTERN LITERATURE (biblical paradoxes)
     There are two ways to view these statements.
    1. OT
      1. The first way reflects the first covenant based on human performance (i.e. Deut. 4:1; 5:33; 8:1; 30:16,19).
      2. The "new" covenant focuses on God's performance (i.e. Ezek. 36:22-36; Jer. 31:31-34).
    2. NT
      1. These statements describe a covenant relationship where God initiates (cf. John 6:44,65) and sets the conditions for fellowship.
      2. Humans must respond initially and continually in repentance and faith (i.e. John 1:12; 3:16; Eph. 2:8-10). Salvation is not a ticket to heaven or an insurance policy, but a daily personal relationship.
        SPECIAL TOPIC: Seek the Lord

  3. Note that the NKJV prints Ezek. 18:4-18 (i.e. Ezek. 18:4-9, 10-13, 14-17,18) as poetry; NIV prints Ezek. 18:5-17 (i.e. Ezek. 18:5-9, 10-13a, 15-17a) as poetry and Ezek. 18:13b-14 as prose, however, the NASB, NRSV, TEV, NJB, JPSOA, and REB print the whole chapter in prose. It is difficult to identify poetry vs. elevated prose.

  4. I like the brief outline in the Oxford Study Bible, p. 874.
    "Maintaining right relations with God frees one from
    1. the past of one's parents, Ezek. 18:1-20
    2. the past of one's own life, Ezek. 18:21-32"

  5. The Jewish Study Bible, p. 1073, makes a good point that the normal introductory phrase, "the word of the Lord came to me," is present in 18:1, but not in 19:1. This may mean they should go together as one context.
    1. the individual's responsibility
    2. each Judean King's responsibility

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Ezekiel 18:2 "proverb"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
18:2 "proverb" The use of this word (BDB 605, KB 647) ties this chapter to a unified context (i.e. chapters 12-18, cf. Ezek. 12:22,23; 14:8; 17:2; 18:2,3).

▣ "The fathers eat the sour grapes,

 But the children's teeth are set on edge"

One person's (or generation's) actions affect others. This is uniquely an eastern viewpoint. Eastern peoples are far more tribal, clan, and family-oriented. One is a member of a group and lives to serve that group. One's attitudes and actions affect that group. Here are some biblical examples.

  1. Adam and Eve affect the whole human family and the earth, Genesis 3; Rom. 5:12-21 (see SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FALL OF MANKIND)
  2. Parent's sin or faithfulness affects the children, Exod. 20:5-6; 34:7; Deut. 5:9; 7:9; Ezekiel 18
  3. Achan's sin affects all of Israel and even some Israeli soldiers die because of his sin, Joshua 7
  4. David sins, but his first son by Bathsheba dies and Israel languishes, 2 Samuel 11-12; Psalm 32, 51
  5. Jesus' substitutionary, vicarious death on behalf of all humans, Isaiah 53; Mark 10:45; John 1:29; Rom. 5:18-19; 2 Cor. 5:21.

In this context the current inhabitants of Jerusalem/Judah are blaming their current situation of being judged by YHWH on the sins of previous generations. YHWH will not let this excuse stand!

SPECIAL TOPIC: BIBLICAL FAITH IS CORPORATE

entries.title: Ezekiel 18:3 "As I live"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
18:3 "As I live" This is an oath based on the covenant name of God, YHWH (cf. Ezek. 5:11; 14:16,18,20; 16:48; 17:16,19; 18:3; 20:3,31,33; 33:11,27; 34:8; 35:6,11). YHWH is the only-living, ever-living God. All life is derived from Him, belongs to Him, and remains through Him (i.e. "all souls are Mine," Ezek. 18:4). What He swears will surely come true (cf. Isa. 55:9-11)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

▣ "you are surely not going to use this proverb in Israel any more" This same proverb is mentioned in Jer. 31:29, but in the setting of "the last days." This proverb impugns the justice and fairness of God (cf. Jer. 16:20; Lam. 5:7).

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD (OT)

entries.title: Ezekiel 18:4 "soul"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
18:4 "soul" This is not the Greek concept that we have a soul (i.e. divine spark), but the Hebrew concept that we are a soul (i.e. nephesh, cf. Gen. 2:7). The Hebrew word (BDB 659, KB 711-713) used four times in this verse, describes the life force (i.e. breath) in both animals and humans (cf. Gen. 1:20-30; 2:7,19; 7:22; Job 34:14-15; Ps. 104:29, 30; 146:4; Eccl. 3:19-21). Humans are uniquely related to YHWH by His personal formation of them and His breathing life into them (cf. Gen. 2:7), yet they are also creatures of this planet. We eat, breathe, reproduce just like other animals of this planet. However, we are also created in God's image and likeness (cf. Gen. 1:26-27). We are a physical and spiritual unity (i.e. Ps. 42:1).

SPECIAL TOPIC: NEPHESH

SPECIAL TOPIC: BODY AND SPIRIT

▣ "all souls are Mine" This is not a theological statement of monotheism (as in Num. 16:22; 27:16; Isa. 42:5; 57:16). The original author is speaking of the covenant people and particularly of Judah's royal line (i.e. Hezekiah, Manasseh, and Josiah).

▣ "The soul who sins will die" The emphasis is on individual covenant responsibility (cf. Ezek. 14:20; Deut. 24:17). Remember it is not "either/or," but "both/and" between individual responsibility and corporate responsibility. This same tension can be seen between original sin and volitional sin (cf. Gen. 2:17; Rom. 6:23; see SPECIAL TOPIC: EASTERN LITERATURE [biblical paradoxes]). This truth is also seen in Deut. 24:16.

What does "die" (BDB 559, KB 562) mean here? It must be more than physical death! It is the opposite of true "life" (cf. Ezek. 18:9). There is "life" (BDB 310, KB 309) beyond this reality. This "life" is characterized by the presence and character of God.

One wonders how the Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE "sins," should be understood. Does it imply that a one-time sin brings death or is that already a reality in the Fall (cf. Genesis 3; see SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FALL OF MANKIND)? How would one relate this statement to 1 John 3:6,9 (PRESENT ACTIVE INDICATIVE)? Are we speaking of sin that characterizes the life or acts of sin? I would assume, because of the idolatrous actions of Ezek. 18:7 and the covenant partners' violations of Ezek. 18:8, that we are speaking of a life characterized by covenant rebellion (cf. Ezek. 18:9).

The Bible mentions three kinds of death or possibly progressive stages of death. The first is Genesis 3. Adam and Eve ate of the forbidden fruit, but they were still alive physically. The "death" referred to was relational (i.e. God to human, human to human, and human to self), as well as contextual (i.e. the planet, the ethos was altered).

The second aspect of death is personal, physical death (cf. Genesis 5). Spiritual death (cf. Eph. 2:1) resulted in the physical cessation of life.

The third aspect (or progress) is ultimate, everlasting death (cf. Rev. 2:11; 20:6,14), which involves

  1. a permanent separation from fellowship with God
  2. a permanent isolation from God's purpose for creation (i.e. loss of heaven)
  3. a permanent fellowship of punishment with evil persons and rebellious angels (i.e. Isa. 14:9-20)

SPECIAL TOPIC: ETERNAL PUNISHMENT

SPECIAL TOPIC: WHERE ARE THE DEAD?

entries.title: Ezekiel 18:5 "practices justice and righteousness"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
18:5 "practices justice and righteousness" These two often appear together in describing the person who lives pleasing to God (cf. 2 Sam. 8:15; 1 Kgs. 10:9; 1 Chr. 18:14; 2 Chr. 9:8; Ps. 99:4; Isa. 9:7; 32:16; 33:5; 59:14; Jer. 4:2; 9:24; 22:3,15; 23:5; 33:15; Ezek. 18:5,19,21,27; 33:14,16,19; 45:9; Amos 5:7,24). Pleasing God involves the inner life (heart, mind) and the outer life (worship, ethical actions, compassion). These cannot be divided. Faith permeates all of life! It is not an isolated ritual, liturgy, or worship time, but a daily, personal relationship! We must not separate justification from sanctification!

SPECIAL TOPIC: JUDGE, JUDGMENT, JUSTICE

SPECIAL TOPIC: RIGHTEOUSNESS

SPECIAL TOPIC: SANCTIFICATION

18:6,15
NASB  "does not eat at the mountain shrines"
NKJV, JPSOA  "not eaten on the mountains"
TEV  "eat the sacrifices offered at forbidden
  shrines"
NET  "does not eat pagan sacrifices on the
  mountains"
REB  "never feasts at mountain shrines"
Peshitta  "has not eaten the meat sacrificed to
  idols on the mountains"
LXX, NRSV, NJB  "who shall not eat upon the mountains"

The MT has "upon the mountains, if he does not eat." From the translations, one can see the implications of the Hebrew text.

  1. The mountains represent the places of pagan fertility worship (cf. Ezek. 6:13; 20:28; 22:9; and many passages in Hosea).
  2. To eat there implied participation in pagan rituals, feasts, and sexual activity.

The JPSOA footnote mentions a possible emendation, "with blood," implying two sins.

  1. fertility worship
  2. violation of food laws (cf. Lev. 17:10-11; 19:26; Ezek. 33:25)
    SPECIAL TOPIC: FOOD LAWS

SPECIAL TOPIC: FERTILITY WORSHIP OF THE ANE

SPECIAL TOPIC: ASHERIM

▣ "lift up his eyes to the idols. . ." This would be an act of worship and trust, thinking the pagan idols could help the worshiper (cf. Deut. 4:19; Ezek. 18:12,15; 20:24; 33:25).

▣ "defile his neighbor's wife" Adultery was so serious because one's children were involved in the concept of the afterlife (one's name cut off). Also, it caused great problems in inheritance rights (cf. Lev. 25; Josh. 12-19), which were so important to the Israelites.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ADULTERY (Exod. 20:14)

▣ "approach a woman during her menstrual period" This refers to sexual intimacy (cf. Lev. 18:14; Deut. 22:14; Isa. 8:3). This is a cultural element dealing with ceremonial defilement (cf. Lev. 12:2,5; 18:19). The Israelites felt any bodily emission made one ceremonially unclean (cf. Lev. 15:1-24). This has nothing to do with sex being considered unclean.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HUMAN SEXUALITY

entries.title: Ezekiel 18:5-9
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
18:5-9 Notice the characteristics of a righteous covenant follower.

  1. practices justice (lit. "what is lawful," BDB 1048), Ezek. 18:5
  2. practices righteousness (lit. "what is right," BDB 842), Ezek. 18:5
  3. does not eat at the mountain shrines, cf. Ezek. 18:15; 22:9; (this refers to local Ba'al worship, cf. Ezek. 6:13), Ezek. 18:6
  4. does not lift up his eyes to the idols, Ezek. 18:6, cf. Ezek. 18:12,15; 20:24; 33:25; Deut. 4:19 (this denotes looking to them for favors and answers to prayers)
  5. does not defile his neighbor's wife, Ezek. 18:6, cf. Ezek. 18:15; 22:11; 33:26; Exod. 20:14; Lev. 18:20; 20:10; Deut. 5:18
  6. does not have sex with a woman during her menstrual period, Ezek. 18:6, cf. Ezek. 22:10; Lev. 15:19,20,24,25
  7. does not oppress anyone, Ezek. 18:7, cf. Ezek. 18:12,16; 22:7,29; Exod. 20:21; Lev. 19:33; 25:14,17; Deut. 23:16
  8. restores to the debtor his pledge, Ezek. 18:7, cf. Deut. 24:13 (#7 and #8 go together)
  9. does not commit robbery, Ezek. 18:7, cf. Lev. 19:13 (e.g. the rich exploiting the poor, Isa. 3:14; 10:2; Micah 2:2)
  10. gives his bread to the hungry, Ezek. 18:7, cf. Ezek. 18:16; Deut. 15:11
  11. covers the naked with clothing, Ezek. 18:7, cf. Isa. 58:7; Matt. 25:35; Luke 3:11
  12. does not lend money on interest, Ezek. 18:8, cf. Exod. 22:25; Deut. 23:19-20 (next phrase "or take increase" is parallel to Lev. 25:36)
  13. keeps his hand from iniquity, Ezek. 18:8
  14. executes true justice between man and man, Ezek. 18:8, cf. Zech. 7:9; 8:16
  15. walks in My statutes, Ezek. 18:9 (see SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PATH, THE WAY)
  16. so as to deal faithfully, Ezek. 18:9

Notice some of these are prohibitions and some are mandated actions; some deal with ceremonial issues, others with sins against a covenant brother. They reflect the Mosaic Covenant.

entries.title: Ezekiel 18:7 "restores to the debtor his pledge"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
18:7 "restores to the debtor his pledge" Often a poor person's outer cloak was used as collateral for a loan. It was to be returned before evening because it was used by the debtor to sleep in (cf. Exod. 22:26-27; Deut. 24:17; Amos 2:8), but land owners often kept it to insure the laborer would return to work the next day.

▣ "does not commit robbery" This refers to the rich landowners taking advantage of the poor people of the land (cf. Ezek. 18:18:7,12,16; 22:7,29; 45:8; 46:18; Exod. 22:21; Lev. 19:13; Jer. 22:3). They loaned them money and when they could not pay, they took their land (i.e. God's inheritance to tribes and families from Joshua 12-19).

▣ "gives bread to the hungry and covers the naked with clothing" YHWH cares for the underprivileged and socially powerless (i.e. widow, orphan, alien); those who know God will also (cf. Deut. 15:11; Isa. 58:7; Matt. 25:31-45; James 2:15-16). Biblical faith has both a private, internal aspect and an outward, daily living aspect.

entries.title: Ezekiel 18:8 "does not lend money on interest"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
18:8 "does not lend money on interest" This was forbidden to fellow Israelites, but permitted to foreigners (cf. Ezek. 18:13,17; 22:12; Exod. 22:25; Lev. 25:35-38; Deut 23:19-20; Ps. 15:5). To be sure, this is mostly an issue of the heart! One's attitude and actions toward the needy are the focus of these verses (i.e. NT book of James).

▣ "he keeps his hand from iniquity" See SPECIAL TOPIC: HAND

▣ "true justice" See SPECIAL TOPIC: JUSTICE

entries.title: Ezekiel 18:9 "he walks"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
18:9 "he walks" This is the biblical imagery for lifestyle faith.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PATH, THE WAY

▣ "My statutes and My ordinances" See SPECIAL TOPIC: TERMS FOR GOD'S REVELATION.

▣
NASB  "so as to deal faithfully"
NKJV  "faithfully"
NRSV  "acting faithfully"
TEV  "carefully keeps"
REB  "loyally observes"
JPSOA  "acted honestly"
LXX  "to do them"
Peshitta  "he who does"

The MT has a VERBAL PHRASE followed by the ADVERB "truly" (BDB 54, אמת), which is translated as "he is sure to observe truly."

The UBS Text Project, p. 52, gives two options.

  1. the MT, "(to act in accordance with) truth"
  2. the LXX, "(to act in accordance with) them" (אתם, to which it gives a "C" rating)

Both make sense in context. For a brief discussion of this major theological root, see Special Topics below.

SPECIAL TOPIC: BELIEVE, TRUST, FAITH AND FAITHFULNESS (OT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: FAITH, BELIEVE, OR TRUST (NT)

▣ "will surely live" This is a repeated grammatical form (cf. Ezek. 18:17,19,21,28) used for emphasis (i.e. a Qal INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE plus a Qal IMPERFECT of the same root, BDB 310, KB 309). This same grammatical pattern appears with two other terms in this chapter.

  1. surely die, Ezek. 18:13 (BDB 559, KB 562)
  2. do not have any pleasure, Ezek. 18:23 (BDB 343, KB 339)

entries.title: Ezekiel 18:10
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 18:10 This verse shows that although parents are admonished to train their children in God's way (i.e. Deut. 4:9-10; 6:7,20-25; 11:19; 31:13; 32:46; Exod. 10:2; 12:26; 13:8,14; Proverbs), the child is ultimately responsible for his own acts. The child commits every sin mentioned in Ezek. 18:5-9 (i.e. Ezek. 18:11-13).

entries.title: Ezekiel 18:11
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 18:11 The parenthesis refers to the father described in vv. 5-9.

entries.title: Ezekiel 18:12 "abominations"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 18:12 "abominations" See SPECIAL TOPIC: ABOMINATION (OT)

entries.title: Ezekiel 18:13 "he will surely be put to death"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
18:13 "he will surely be put to death" See note at Ezek. 18:9.

SPECIAL TOPIC: DEATH PENALTY IN ISRAEL

▣ "his blood will be on his own head" Environment (society) and heredity (parents) are significant factors in social and religious development, but they do not remove individual responsibility (note Ezek. 33:4,5).

SPECIAL TOPIC: BLOOD

entries.title: Ezekiel 18:14
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
18:14 Verse 14 is addressing the next generation of Ezek. 18:5 and 10 (i.e. righteous, wicked, righteous, cf. Ezek. 18:20).

▣ There is a MSS variant relaterd to "and he sees" (BDB 906, KB 1157, Qal IMPERFECT with waw). The RSV emends this to "and he is afraid." The UBS Text Project, p. 54, gives the MT a "B" rating.

  1. and he sees ‒ ויראה (most English translations follow the MT and LXX)
  2. and he is afraid ‒ וירא (RSV)

entries.title: Ezekiel 18:17 "he keeps his hand from the poor"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
18:17 "he keeps his hand from the poor" This is an idiom for not retaliating against the poor debtor. There have been two suggested translation emendations.

  1. "from the poor" ‒ מעני (NASB, NKJV, JPSOA, Peshitta)
  2. "from iniquity" (LXX) ‒ מעול (LXX, NRSV, NJB, REB, NET)
  3. The UBS Text Project, p. 54, gives the MT, "poor," a "B" rating.

entries.title: Ezekiel 18:19
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
18:19 This shows the diatribe nature of the chapter. Ezekiel is answering the unspoken (or veiled) questions whispered against YHWH's justice.

NASB, LXX  "has observed"
NKJV  "done"
NRSV  "has been careful to observe"
TEV  "kept. . .carefully"
NJB, Peshitta  "kept"
REB  "careful to obey"

The VERB (BDB 1036, KB 1581, Qal PERFECT) means "to keep," "to watch," or "to preserve." It implies a careful diligence in observing God's laws (i.e. Lev. 22:31; Deut. 4:40; 6:2; 26:17). One's love for YHWH was expressed in obedience and love for other covenant brothers, and aliens. One could not claim to love God if he did not practice it toward other humans (i.e. 1 John 3:16-24; 4:8-21).

Righteousness in its OT sense implied a care and concern for others, especially the underprivileged, that goes beyond a strict legal standard. Justice was extended by covenant compassion (see Norman H. Snaith, The Distinctive Ideas of the Old Testament, pp. 159-173). This is what Jesus teaches in the Sermon on the Mount, Matthew 5-7.

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

entries.title: Ezekiel 18:21 "if the wicked man turns"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
18:21 "if the wicked man turns" This shows the continuing love of God. Any moment that a human (in this case a covenant member) will repent and execute trust, God is there to forgive and receive him!

SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE (OT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: FORGIVENESS in the OT

▣ "he shall surely live" This is the Qal INFINITIVE and Qal IMPERFECT of the same root (BDB 310, KB 309) for emphasis and in contrast to death (BDB 559, KB 562, Qal IMPERFECT). See also Lev. 18:5. God wants to bless us!

entries.title: Ezekiel 18:22 "All his transgressions"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
18:22 "All his transgressions" The term "transgressions" (BDB 833) literally means "to rebel." It is used as imagery for rebelling against YHWH (cf. Isa. 1:28; 46:8; 53:12 [twice]; Hosea 14:9; Amos 4:4 [twice]).

▣ "will not be remembered" This VERB (BDB 269, KB 209, Niphal IMPERFECT) is also used as imagery for YHWH forgetting human rebellion (cf. Ezek. 18:24; 3:20; 33:13). When God forgives, God forgets (i.e. Ps. 103:11-13; Isa. 1:18; 38:17; 43:25; 44:22; Micah 7:19). What a wonderful Truth! What a wonderful God!

SPECIAL TOPIC: FORGIVENESS in the OT

▣ "because of his righteousness which he has practiced, he will live" This is an OT understanding of "righteousness." It should not be understood in the sense of "sinlessness," but in the sense it was used to describe Noah (cf. Gen. 6:4) and Job (cf. Job 1:1). They lived up to their understanding of the will of God (see SPECIAL TOPIC: BLAMELESS, INNOCENT, GUILTLESS, WITHOUT REPROACH). True and complete obedience is not a possibility for fallen humanity (cf. Gen. 6:5,11-12; Ps. 14:3; Isa. 53:6; Rom. 1:18-3:20; 5:12-14). Covenant obedience was the criteria for "a ceremonial righteousness" within ancient Israel. Even in the Judaism of Jesus' day "righteousness" was defined as

  1. almsgiving, see SPECIAL TOPIC: ALMSGIVING
  2. prayer
  3. fasting (cf. Matt. 6:1-18, see SPECIAL TOPIC: FASTING)

as well as required sacrifices, feast days, and Sabbath observance.

SPECIAL TOPIC: RIGHTEOUSNESS

entries.title: Ezekiel 18:23 "Do I have any pleasure in the death of the wicked"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
18:23 "Do I have any pleasure in the death of the wicked" The phrase "any pleasure" is a combination of the INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE and the IMPERFECT VERB of the same root (BDB 342, KB 339), which expresses intensity. This grammatical form occurs often in this chapter. See note at Ezek. 18:9.

This chapter is an allusion to the transgenerational communication of sin through families (cf. Exod. 20:5; Deut. 5:9). However, it also alludes to the gracious character of YHWH (cf. Deut. 5:10; 7:9). The mercy of God vs. the judgment of God can be compared to judgment, 3-4 generations but mercy to a 1,000 generations! But Ezekiel even removes the 3-4! Each human created in God's image and likeness will stand before God as an individual based on his/her actions and motives (i.e. Deut. 24:16).

Notice that "the wicked" is parallel with "anyone" in Ezek. 18:32. Contextually this must refer to covenant people (i.e. here, Judeans), but the OT inclusion of

  1. non-Israelites such as Job, Melchizedek, Caleb, and Ninevites
  2. the Mosaic covenant's concern for the resident alien
  3. Isaiah's revelations of YHWH's love for and inclusion of "the nations" (i.e. Isa. 66:23), causes one to expand the reference to all humans, which is surely the focus of the "New Covenant" (i.e. John 1:12; 3:16; 4:42; Rom. 11:32; 1 Tim. 2:4; 4:10; Titus 2:11; Heb. 2:9; 2 Pet. 3:9; 1 John 2:1; 4:14).

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

▣ "rather than that he should turn from his ways" The VERB (BDB 996. KB 1427, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT) is one of two words used to describe "repentance" (cf. v. 32).

SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE (OT), III.

▣ "live" This VERB (BDB 310, KB 309, Qal with waw CONSECUTIVE PERFECT) is very common, "to be alive," "to be revived," "to preserve alive." It theologically related to God's covenant name, YHWH. True life comes only from the Creator God.

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D,

entries.title: Ezekiel 18:24
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
18:24 This verse demonstrates that an OT covenant person could

  1. be righteous, Ezek. 18:24
  2. become wicked, Ezek. 18:24
  3. become righteous again, Ezek. 18:27,28

The Mosaic Covenant is a performance-based, conditional covenant! The question remains, is the NT a conditional covenant? NT acceptance by God is not performance-based, but the goal of both the OT and NT is a righteous people who reflect God's character to a lost world! The problem of "easy believism" is the issue. We must not separate justification from sanctification! The NT is a conditional covenant, which requires

  1. repentance
  2. faith, trust, belief
  3. obedience
  4. perseverance
  5. service
  6. worship

The fallen nature which characterizes the OT is matched by the indwelling Spirit of the NT. This is the newness of Jer. 31:31-34 (cf. Ezek. 36:22-36). The rabbinical proverb, "in every person's heart are two dogs (black and while). The one you feed most (i.e. yetzer) becomes the biggest" (parapahrase).

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

SPECIAL TOPIC: APOSTASY (aphistēmi)

SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE (OT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: BELIEVE, TRUST, FAITH AND FAITHFULNESS in the OT

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

SPECIAL TOPIC: PERSEVERANCE

▣ Notice the phrases used to describe one who turns from righteousness.

  1. commits iniquity (lit. "injustice," BDB 732, cf. Ezek. 3:20; 18:24,26 [twice]; 33:13 [twice],15,18; Lev. 19:15,35; Deut. 25:16
  2. does according to all the abominations (BDB 1072, see SPECIAL TOPIC: ABOMINATION (OT)
  3. wicked man does (lit. "wicked," BDB 957, cf. Ezek. 3:18 [twice]; 7:21; 21:30; 33:8 [twice])
  4. treachery which he has committed (lit. "act unfaithfully," BDB 591, cf. Ezek. 14:13; 15:8; 17:20; 20:27; 39:23,26)
  5. sin which he has committed (BDB 308, cf. Ezek. 16:51; 18:14; 21:29; 33:10,16)

All of these phrases refer to covenant people. Their genealogy in the family of Abraham did not protect them (note John 8:31-59) from the consequences of evil acts (cf. Isa. 65:7; Jer. 31:29-30; Lam. 5:7).

SPECIAL TOPIC: SIN IN THE OT

18:25
NASB  "not right"
NKJV, Peshitta  "not fair"
NRSV, JPSOA  "unfair"
TEV  "isn't right"
NJB  "unjust"
REB  "acts with out principle"
LXX  "does not go straight"

This VERB (BDB 1067, KB 1733, Niphal IMPERFECT) refers to actions that do not fit a standard of weight or measurement (cf. Ezek. 18:29; 33:17,20). YHWH judges precisely because He weighs the human heart and knows the actions of all (cf. 1 Sam. 2:3; 16:7; 1 Kgs. 8:39; 1 Chr. 28:9; Ps. 7:9; 26:7; 139:1,23; Prov. 16:2,11; Jer. 11:20; 17:10; Luke 16:15; John 2:24-25; Acts 1:24; 15:8; Rom. 8:27; Rev. 2:23).

SPECIAL TOPIC: DEGREES OF REWARDS AND PUNISHMENT

▣ This verse shows the purpose of the chapter (cf. Ezek. 18:2). The Judeans in Jerusalem are trying to explain YHWH's judgment by blaming

  1. their ancestors
  2. their parents
  3. God (He is unjust in His actions, cf. Ezek. 18:29; 33:17,20)

They were attempting to deflect spiritual responsibility. This whole chapter must contextually be seen in this light!

"Hear now" is a Qal IMPERATIVE (BDB 1033, KB 1570). YHWH is still dealing with His covenant people. He wants them to repent and return to Him (cf. Ezek. 18:30-32).

SPECIAL TOPIC: LISTEN/HEAR (shema)

entries.title: Ezekiel 18:28 "because he considered"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
18:28 "because he considered" This is literally "see" (BDB 906, KB 1157, Qal IMPERFECT), but used in the sense of mental enlightentment (TEV "realizes"). It is similar to "came to himself" of Luke 15:17. Spiritual choices all begin in the mind! The new thoughts result in modified behavior!

The phrase "he shall surely live" is a repeated divine affirmation (see Ezek. 18:9,17,19,21).

▣ "and turned away" This is one of the main VERBS for "repentance" (shub, BDB 996, KB 1427). Biblical faith involves a turning from (i.e. self and sin, cf. Genesis 3) and a turning to (i.e. seeking God and His will).

SPECIAL TOPIC: Seek the Lord

SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE (OT)

entries.title: Ezekiel 18:29
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 18:29 The VERB "is not right" (BDB 1067, KB 1733, Niphal IMPERFECT) is used in this context three times; once as an accusation against God, but twice of the Judeans' sinful actions.

entries.title: Ezekiel 18:30 "a stumbling block"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
18:30 "a stumbling block" This (BDB 506) can be understood as the means or occasion of stumbling or literally of a rock in the road. See note at Ezek. 3:20.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PATH, THE WAY

entries.title: Ezekiel 18:30-32
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
18:30-32 This is a key theological summary. "Each according to his conduct" is a spiritual principle recurrent throughout Scripture (i.e. "reap what you sow," cf. Job 34:11; Ps. 28:4; 62:12; Prov. 24:12; Eccl. 12:14; Jer. 17:10; 32:19; Matt. 16:27; 25:31-46; Rom. 2:6; 14:12; 1 Cor. 3:8; 2 Cor. 5:10; Gal. 6:7-10; 2 Tim. 4:14; 1 Pet. 1:17; Rev. 2:23; 20:12; 22:12). See full note at Gal. 6:7-10.

▣ This summary has a series of IMPERATIVES.

  1. repent ‒ BDB 996, KB 1427, Qal IMPERATIVE repeated in Ezek. 18:32,
  2. turn away ‒ BDB 996, KB 1427, Hiphil IMPERATIVE, used in an exclamatory sense
  3. cast away ‒ BDB 1020, KB 1527, Hiphil IMPERATIVE, cf. Ezek. 20:7,8
  4. make yourselves a new heart and a new spirit ‒ BDB 793, KB 889, Qal IMPERATIVE
  5. live ‒ BDB 310, KB 309, Qal IMPERATIVE, this is the key term used 17 times in this chapter (and 10 times in the parallel, chapter 33). YHWH lives, Ezek. 18:3, and He wants us to live, but spiritual life has conditions and requirements.

I have come to believe that Adam and Eve were not created immortal. Their exclusion from the Garden, where they had access to the tree of life, is the first clue. Only YHWH has life. He is the ever-living, only-living Being.

In the NT only believers in Jesus are said to have eternal life. This theological understandiing is called "limited immortality." It surely affects the theology of "eternal punishment" (see SPECIAL TOPIC: ETERNAL PUNISHENT).

This whole area of theology has been unfortunately affected by Greek thought (i.e. every person has a divine spark). Biblically speaking, humans do not have a soul; they are a soul (i.e. Gen. 2:7).

SPECIAL TOPIC: NEPHESH

SPECIAL TOPIC: BODY AND SPIRIT

entries.title: Ezekiel 18:31
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
18:31 It is obvious that even with YHWH's available revelation and mercy, some covenant people will not return to Him. Some never knew Him. There are two inseparable ways this "knowledge" is manifest.

  1. personal faith (cf. Gen. 15:6)
  2. personal obedience (cf. Ezek. 18:21-22)

The second is evidence that the first is present. The "new" covenant will accentuate (not initiate) this relationship.

One more theological point on these verses. Israel's physical condition was related to her spiritual condition. Israel's problems were related to her disobedience to YHWH, not YHWH's weakness related to the other national gods (i.e. Babylonian Marduk). This truth emphasizes the tension between a sovereign monotheistic Deity and a covenant people with true free will! Israel reaped the consequences of her choices, not YHWH's (i.e. Ezek. 18:23,32)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM

SPECIAL TOPIC: ELECTION

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

  1. Why is this chapter so important in understanding the OT?
  2. Are we affected by the sins of others? How? Can we be corporately guilty for our society?
  3. Does God love all humans or just a chosen group?
  4. What spiritual principle is mentioned in Ezek. 18:30?

entries.title: Ezekiel 19:1 "take up"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
19:1 "take up" The VERB (BDB 669, KB 724, Qal IMPERATIVE) literally means "to lift" or "to carry." Here it is used in an idiom for "speak loudly" or "make heard."

It is surprising that this chapter does not start with "the word of the Lord came to me saying" (cf. Ezek. 1:3; 6:1; 7:1; 11:14; 12:1,8,17,21,26; 13:1; 14:2,12; 15:1; 16:1; 17:1; 18:1; 20:2,45; 21:1,8,18; 22:1; etc.). Does this imply that chapters 18 and 19 form a literary unit? I think not since chapter 19 has two poetic lamentations (i.e. three beats per line and then two beats per line of poetry).

▣ "lamentation" This term (BDB 884) refers to a specific type of funeral song (cf. Ezek. 2:10; 19:1,14; 26:17; 27:2,32; 28:12; 32:2,16). It becomes a literary marker for a new topic (genre, cf. Isa. 14:3-21; Amos 5:1-3). In prophetic literature there are several standard oracle forms.

  1. promise oracle
  2. court terminology
  3. funeral dirge

A good brief discussion of funeral rites in Israel can be seen in Roland DeVaux's Ancient Israel, vol. 1, pp. 57-61.

▣ "the princes of Israel" This title ("prince," BDB 672) is used in Ezekiel to refer to several groups.

  1. King Zedekiah, Ezek. 7:27; 12:10,12; 21:25
  2. leaders of Judah, Ezek. 21:12; 22:6; 45:8,9
  3. future Davidic kings, Ezek. 34:24; 37:25; 44:3; 45:7,16,17,22; 46:2,4,8,10,12,16,17,18; 48:21,22
  4. foreign kings, Ezek. 26:16; 27:21; 30:13; 32:29; 38:2,3; 39:1,18

The term implies members of a royal family. Here, because it is PLURAL, it refers to the king and others of his extended family in places of leadership.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Ezekiel 19:1-9
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
19:1-9 These two verses describe the exile of two Judean kings.

  1. Jehoahaz, taken to Egypt by Necco II
  2. Jehoiachin, taken to Babylon by Nebuchadnezzar II

entries.title: Ezekiel 19:2 "your mother"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
19:2 "your mother" This refers to

  1. Judah (cf. Ezek. 19:10) producing a line of Davidic kings (cf. Gen. 49:9; Num. 23:24; Rev. 5:5). This ceased with Zedekiah's exile. In a sense (i.e. tribe of Judah but not family of Jesse), Zerubbabel (Sheshbazzar, Ezra 1:8) continued the Davidic line (cf. Haggai 2:23; Zechariah 4).
  2. The wife of King Josiah producing two sons (i.e. Jehoahaz Zedekiah)
19:7
NASB  "destroyed"
NKJV, Targums  "knew"
NRSV, JPSOA, Peshitta  "ravaged"
TEV  "wrecked"
NJB  "tore down"
REB, NET  "broke down"
LXX  "laid waste"

The MT has "knew" (וידע, BDB 393), but most English translations assume an emendation "destroyed" (וירע). With it, this poetic line is parallel to Ezek. 19:7b. The UBS Hebrew OT Project, p. 57, gives the emendation a "C" rating.

NASB  "fortified towers"
NKJV  "desolate places"
NRSV, NET  "strongholds"
TEV  "forts"
NJB  "palaces"
JPSOA, REB  "widows"

The MT has "windows" (אלמנותין, BDB 48), but most English translations use an emendation "citadel" or "strongholds" (ארמנותינ, BDB 74) because of the next word, "cities" (BDB 746).

The MT is barely understandable in the context. However, the UBS Hebrew OT Project, p. 57, gives it an "A" rating. The imagery would then be of a new leader of the pride (i.e. king, cf. v. 6).

19:9
NASB  "in hunting nets"
NKJV  "in nets"
NRSV, LXX  "into custody"
TEV  "under guard"
NJB, JPSOA  "into a fortress"
REB, Peshitta  "in prison"

The MT has a root that could have several meanings.

  1. מצד ‒ BDB 844, FEMININE NOUN, "stronghold," cf. Jer. 48:41; 51:30
  2. מצוד ‒ BDB 844, MASCULINE NOUN, "net," Job 19:6; Eccl. 7:26
  3. םץודה ‒ BDB 845, FEMININE NOUN
    1. "net for fish," cf. Eccl. 9:12
    2. "snare for prey," cf. Ezek. 12:13; 17:20

In this context "stronghold" or "prison" in Babylon fits the next line of poetry best.

The UBS Text Project, p. 58, gives the MASCULINE form of the NOUN "stronghold" a "B" rating (some doubt).

entries.title: Ezekiel 19:2-9
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
19:2-9 This section of the lamentation refers to the kings of Judah, from the death of Josiah until the fall of Jerusalem (586 B.C.).

  1. Jehoahaz (Shallum, cf. Jer. 22:11), 2 Kgs. 23:31-33; 2 Chr. 36:1-4, who was Josiah's son and successor, but exiled by Pharaoh Neco II after three months and replaced by
  2. Jehoiakim (Eliakim), 2 Kgs. 23:34-24:7, who was also a son of Josiah. He reigned eleven years and died. He was replaced by
  3. Jehoiachin (Jeconiah, Coniah), 2 Kgs. 24:8-17; 2 Chr. 36:9-10, who reigned three months and was exiled to Babylon (cf. Ezek. 19:9, 597 B.C.) by Nebuchadnezzar II and replaced with
  4. Zedekiah, 2 Kgs. 24:18-20, who was placed on the throne by Nebuchadnezzar II. He rebelled and was captured, blinded, and exiled to Babylon.

Special Topic: Kings of the Divided Monarchy

▣ "lions" See Special Topic: Lions in the OT

entries.title: Ezekiel 19:10-14
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
19:10-14 These verses change the imagery describing Judah's royal family not as a lion pride but a huge, tall grapevine. They also change time frames back to the beginnings of a unified kingdom (i.e. Saul, David, Solomon). The vine is described as

  1. Positive
    1. planted by waters, Ezek. 19:10 (cf. Ps. 1:3)
    2. fruitful, Ezek. 19:10
    3. full of strong branches, Ezek. 19:10-11
    4. tall above the clouds, Ezek. 19:11
  2. Negative
    1. plucked up in fury, Ezek. 19:12
    2. cast down to the ground, Ezek. 19:12
    3. east wind dried up its fruit, Ezek. 19:12
    4. strong branch torn off, Ezek. 19:12
    5. planted in a wilderness, Ezek. 19:13
    6. planted in a dry land, Ezek. 19:13
    7. burned, Ezek. 19:14

The royal family was decimated (similar to chapter 17).

The lion imagery for Judah may refer to Jacob's prophecies about his children (esp. Judah, cf. Gen. 49:9). Balaam also used this imagery to describe Israel (cf. Num. 23:24; 24:9).

19:10
NASB, NRSV, NET, JPSOA footnote  "vineyard"
NKJV  "bloodline"
TEV  "grapevine" (Targum
  and LXX, "vine")
NJB   —omitted—
Peshitta, JPSOA  "in your blood"

The MT has "blood" (בדמך, BDB 196).The UBS Text Project (p. 58) gives it a "C" rating (considerable doubt). Most English translations use an emendation.

  1. "to be like" (תדמה)
  2. "height"
  3. "vineyard" (בכרם)
  4. omit the phrase (cf. REB).

The Ancient Near East often used the imagery of a giant plant to describe world powers (e.g. Ezek. 17:3,22-24; 19:10-14; 31:2-18; Dan. 4:4-17,19-27; and possibly Amos 2:9).

▣ "planted by waters" This reminds one of Psalm 1.

19:11
NASB, NKJV, TEV, REB  "branches"
NRSV, NJB  "stem"

There is a wordplay between "branches" (BDB 641), which can refer to a "staff," or "scepter" (BDB 986); also notice the same play in Ezek. 19:14.

NASB, TEV  "the clouds"
NKJV, NRSV, NJB  "the thick branches"

NIDOTTE, vol. 3, p. 310, reads "In Ezek. 19:11; 31:3,10,14 one should read 'clouds' from 'āb, rather than 'branches' from 'ābōt."

entries.title: Ezekiel 19:12 "the east wind"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
19:12 "the east wind" This term (BDB 924 CONSTRUCT BDB 870) is used in Ezekiel many times (over fifty), but most often in chapters 40-48 simply as "the east." It denotes

  1. the direction of the rising sun
  2. imagery for destruction (i.e. desert wind), often with the added theological connotation of being sent by YHWH to accomplish His purposes.
    1. Gen. 41:6,23,27 (negative)
    2. Exod. 10:13; 14:21; Isa. 11:15 (positive)
    3. Wisdom Literature, Job 27:21; 38:24; Ps. 48:7; 78:26 (representative sample)
    4. Isa. 27:8
    5. Jer. 18:17
    6. Ezek. 17:10; 19:12; 27:26
    7. Hosea 13:15
    8. Jonah 4:8
    9. Hab. 1:9
  3. used as imagery to describe YHWH ‒ Exod. 15:8-10

The hot desert wind (Arabic, "sirocco" wind), like the rain, is at YHWH's disposal! Wind (BDB 924, ruah) is often associated with YHWH's power (i.e. Spirit) in the OT.

Special Topic: Breath, Wind, Spirit

Special Topic: Spirit in the Bible

entries.title: Ezekiel 19:13
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 19:13 This is imagery for the Neo-Babylon exile of most of the population of Judah. There were several deportations (i.e. 605, 597, 586, 582 B.C.). This specific context is referring to the exile of the legitimate Davidic king (Jehoiachin).

entries.title: Ezekiel 19:14
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
19:14 Fire is YHWH's instrument of judgment (cf. Ezek. 15:4; 20:47-48). There will be no Davidic king after the exiled Zedekiah. Even Zerubbabel (Sheshbazzar, Ezra 1:8) was only a prince of the line, not a direct son. The direct son of 2 Samuel 7 will be the Messiah.

Special Topic: Messiah

Special Topic: Fire

entries.title: Ezekiel 20:1 "in the seventh year, in the fifth month, on the tenth of the month"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
20:1 "in the seventh year, in the fifth month, on the tenth of the month" Ezekiel makes an attempt to date his prophecies (i.e. 591 B.C., cf. 2 Kgs. 25:8; compare with Jer. 52:12; also note the dates in Ezek. 1:1; 8:1; 20:1; 26:1; 29:1,17; 30:20; 31:1; 32:1,17; 33:21). The purpose for this may be

  1. a literary way of asserting that YHWH spoke to him
  2. a way of showing he was a true prophet (i.e. YHWH spoke to him before the event)
  3. just his meticulous personality or possibly priestly training

The elder's question is not stated, but the date causes one to imagine it was related to Egypt's power and Zedekiah's proposed alliance with Pharaoh Psammetik II (595-589 B.C.).

Special Topic: ANE Calendars

▣ "the elders of Israel came to inquire of the Lord" They had done this before (cf. Ezek. 8:1,11,12; 14:1). We do not know what they came to ask because Ezekiel receives another vision while they sat there. This revelation relates to their questions.

Special Topic: Elder

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

  1. First paragraph
  2. Second paragraph
  3. Third paragraph, etc.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Ezekiel 20:3
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
20:3 The motives and sins of this (these) group(s) of elders are consistently negative (cf. Ezek. 8:1; 14:1). They came as if they were seeking YHWH's advice and guidance (cf. Ezek. 14:3; 20:31), but in reality, they were idolaters (cf. Ezek. 14:7). The wickedness of Jerusalem (chapters 8-10) has already affected the exiles (leaders reflect the populace). This uniform evil demonstrates that YHWH's choosing the exiles to reconstitute Israel, while judging and destroying those in Palestine, was an act of mercy, not merit (cf. Ezek. 36:22-38). He chose them because of His eternal redemptive purposes for all mankind!

One day YHWH will listen again (cf. Ezek. 36:37-38)!

Special Topic: YHWH's Eternal Redemptive Plan

▣ "Son of Man" See note at Ezek. 2:1.

▣ "speak" This (BDB 180, KB 210) is a Piel IMPERATIVE (cf. Ezek. 3:1; 12:23; 14:4; 20:27; 29:3; 33:2; 37:19,21). Ezekiel passes on YHW's message, not his own.

▣ "the Lord God" This is literally Adon YHWH. Notice the number of titles used for Deity in this chapter. This is a chapter about God and His intentions for Israel, but they would not!

  1. Lord (YHWH), Ezek. 20:2 (see Speial Topic: Names for Deity, D.)
  2. Adon YHWH, Ezek. 20:3(twice), 5,27,30,31,33,36,39,40,44,47,49 (see Special Topic: Lord (adon and kuiros)
  3. YHWH your Elohim, Ezek. 20:5,7,19,20 (see Special Topic: Names for Deity, C.)
  4. I am the Lord (YHWH), Ezek. 20:26,38,42,44
  5. I, the Lord (YHWH), Ezek. 20:48

Also notice the personal PRONOUNS and phrases.

  1. Myself, Ezek. 20:5,9
  2. against Me, Ezek. 20:8,13,21,27,38
  3. My wrath, Ezek. 20:8,13,21
  4. My anger, Ezek. 20:8,21
  5. My name, Ezek. 20:9,14
  6. My statutes, Ezek. 20:11,13,16,19,21,24
  7. My ordinances, Ezek. 20:11,13,16,19,21,24
  8. My sabbaths, Ezek. 20:11,13,16,20,21,24
  9. My eye, Ezek. 20:17
  10. My hand, Ezek. 20:22
  11. blasphemed Me, Ezek. 20:27
  12. listen to Me, Ezek. 20:39
  13. My holy name, Ezek. 20:39
  14. My holy mountain, Ezek. 20:40
  15. serve Me, Ezek. 20:40
  16. prove Myself holy, Ezek. 20:41
  17. My name's sake, Ezek. 20:44

entries.title: Ezekiel 20:4
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
20:4 YHWH seems to be asking Ezekiel if he is ready to act as His mouthpiece in confronting (cf. Ezek. 16:2; 22:2) these idolatrous elders. The repeated VERB "judge" (BDB 1047; KB 1622) could be Qal IMPERFECT or Qal IMPERFECT used as a JUSSIVE (cf. Ezek. 20:7,18 [thrice]).

▣ "Make them know" This VERB (BDB 393, KB 390) is a Hiphil IMPERATIVE (Hiphil PERFECT in Ezek. 22:2). It implies both

  1. truth
  2. a relationship with YHWH (e.g. Gen. 4:1; Jer. 1:5)

▣ "abomination" See Special Topic: Abomination (OT).

▣ "of their fathers" This is surprising in light of Ezekiel 18. Are these elders being confronted because of their parents' or ancestors' sins? Our parents and society often instill destructive patterns or licenses which reap judgment (cf. Exod. 20:5; Deut. 5:9,10). There is both an individual and corporate ethical, moral, religious responsibility. It is not an either/or situation. These elders are affected, but also responsible, as were the Davidic kings of Ezekiel 19.

entries.title: Ezekiel 20:5 "swore"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
20:5 "swore" This is literally "lift the hand" and is used twice in this verse. This forms the central theme of this chapter (cf. Ezek. 20:6,15,23,28,42): YHWH's gracious provisions and covenant promises in contrast to Israel's repeated covenant failures (cf. Psalm 106; Nehemiah 9).

The gesture of raising/lifting (BDB 669, KB 724) the hand can have several meanings.

  1. oath taking, Exod. 6:8; Num. 14:30; Ps. 106:26; Ezek. 20:5-6
  2. rebellion, 2 Sam. 20:21
  3. positive action, Ps. 10:12 (YHWH); 119:48 (human)
  4. blessing, Lev. 9:22; Ps. 28:2; 63:4; 134:2; 1 Tim. 2:8
  5. prayers, Lam. 2:19

Special Topic: Hand

entries.title: Ezekiel 20:5-7
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
20:5-7 These verses describe YHWH's actions/admonitions towards the descendants of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob ("the seed of the house of Jacob," Ezek. 20:5).

  1. "I chose Israel," BDB 103, KB 119, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT, this election terminology, so common in Deuteronomy and Isaiah, occurs only here in Ezekiel.
  2. "I swore" (lit. "lifted hand"), Ezek. 20:5(twice), BDB 669, KB 724, Qal IMPERFECT with waw (i.e. that I would be their God)
  3. "I made Myself known to them," Ezek. 20:5, BDB 393, KB 390, Niphal IMPERFECT with waw
  4. "I swore," Ezek. 20:6, BDB 669, KB 724, Qal PERFECT (that I would bring them out of bondage, out of Egypt, cf. Gen. 15:12-21)
  5. "that I had selected for them," Ezek. 20:6, BDB 1064, KB 1707, Qal PERFECT (I would give them the land of Canaan, cf. Gen. 15:12-21)
  6. "cast away. . .the detestable things," Ezek. 20:7, BDB 1020, KB 1527, Hiphil IMPERATIVE
  7. "do not defile yourselves," Ezek. 20:7, BDB 379, KB 375, Hithpael IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense, cf. Ezek. 18:15; 20:7,18,31; 22:3-4; 23:7,30; 36:18,25; 37:23

entries.title: Ezekiel 20:6 "to bring them out"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
20:6 "to bring them out" This VERB (BDB 422, KB 425, Hiphil INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT, cf. Ezek. 20:6,9,10, 14,22,34,38,41) is often used (in the Hiphil) of YHWH's act of

  1. prophetic fulfillment (cf. Gen. 15:12-21)
  2. mercy in delivering Israel from Egypt.

It is also used of YHWH delivering Israel from the Assyrian and Babylonian exiles (cf. Ezek. 20:34,38,41; 34:13).

NASB  "that I had selected for them"
NKJV, NRSV  "that I had searched out for them"
TEV  "I had chosen for them"
NJB  "which I had reconnoitered for them"
LXX  "that I spied for them"
REV, JPSOA  "that I had sought out for them"
Peshitta  "that I given to them"

The VERB (BDB 1064, KB 1707, Qal PERFECT) means "to seek out," "to spy out," or "to explore," in light of the fact that

  1. it is used so often for the twelve spies (cf. Num. 13:2,16,17,25,32; 14:6,7, 34,36,38)
  2. it is found only here in the Prophets.

The translation "spy out" seems best in light of Deut. 1:33. YHWH took special, personal care of young Israel (cf. Ezekiel 16)!

▣ "flowing with milk and honey" This phrase is first used in Exod. 3:8,17; 13:5; 33:3; Lev. 20:24; Num. 13:27; 14:8; 16:13-14. It became a technical name used in Aramaic sources (i.e. Persian) for the land of Palestine/ Canaan (cf. Jer. 3:19). It was a very fertile place (cf. Ezek. 20:15).

NASB, NKJV, Peshitta  "the glory"
NRSV  "the most glorious"
TEV  "the finest"
NJB  "the loveliest"
JPSOA, REB  "the fairest"
LXX  "it is a honeycomb"

The MT has "the gazelle" (BDB 840 II, cf. v. 15), which was an idiom for beauty. The LXX seems to relate the root to another root for "honey."

entries.title: Ezekiel 20:7,8 "cast away"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
20:7,8 "cast away" This VERB (BDB 1020, KB 1527, Hiphil IMPERATIVE) is often used of people rejecting God's revelation, word (cf. NIDOTTE, vol. 4, p. 127).

  1. 1 Kgs. 14:9, Jeroboam I cast YHWH behind his back (i.e. out of sight, out of mind)
  2. Neh. 9:26, Israelites, during the period of the Judges, cast God's law behind their backs
  3. Ps. 2:3, the kings of the earth reject the Lord's anointed
  4. Ps. 50:17, the wicked reject YHWH's word
  5. Ezek. 23:35, Judah forgot YHWH and cast Him behind their backs

What these rebels should have cast away was their rebellion (cf. Ezek. 18:31; 20:7-8). One day they will fling their idols out in the street (cf. Ezek. 7:19).

entries.title: Ezekiel 20:7 "defiled yourselves with the idols of Egypt"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 20:7 "defiled yourselves with the idols of Egypt" This could refer to the golden calf of Exodus 32 or the idols mentioned in Josh. 24:14.

entries.title: Ezekiel 20:8a
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
20:8a This describes Israel's rebellion against their covenant God (i.e. during and after the Exodus).

  1. they rebelled against Me, Ezek. 20:8 BDB 598, KB 632, Hiphil IMPERFECT with waw
  2. they were not willing to listen to Me, Ezek. 20:8, "listen," BDB 1033, KB 1570, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT, cf. Ezek. 3:7; 12:2
  3. they did not cast away the detestable things, Ezek. 20:8, BDB 1020, KB 1527, Hiphil PERFECT, cf. Ezek. 5:11; 11:21
  4. they did not forsake the idols of Egypt, Ezek. 20:8, BDB 736, KB 806, Qal PERFECT, cf. Exodus 32; Ps. 106:19-23

The foolishness of idol worship is highlighted in Ps. 115:4-8; 138:15-18; Isa. 44:9-17; Jer. 2:27-28; 10:3-5; Hab. 2:18-19!

Special Topic: Idolatry

entries.title: Ezekiel 20:8b
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
20:8b This describes YHWH's reaction to Israel's rebellions (i.e. bondage in Egypt).

  1. I resolved to pour out My wrath, Ezek. 20:8
  2. I resolved to accomplish My anger, Ezek. 20:8
  3. I acted for the sake of My name, that it should not be profaned ("profane" lit. "pollute," BDB 320, KB 319, cf. Ezek. 20:13,14,16,21,22,24,39; 36:22-36)

Special Topic: "The Name" of YHWH (OT)

entries.title: Ezekiel 20:9-12
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
20:9-12 God's actions towards Israel during the Exodus and beyond (Ezek. 20:9c).

  1. I took them out of Egypt.
  2. I brought them into the wilderness.
  3. I gave them My statutes, I informed them of My ordinances.
  4. I gave them My sabbaths to be a sign between Me and them (a regular worship time and place, Exod. 31:13).
  5. That they might know. This Hebrew word (BDB 393, KB 390, cf. Ezek. 20:20) implies both
    1. a personal relationship
    2. knowledge about something

Special Topic: Know

entries.title: Ezekiel 20:9
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
20:9 Notice that YHWH has a concern for "the nations." Israel was meant to reveal YHWH to the nations (cf. Ezek. 20:14,39; 36:22-38; 39:7). I think there is a direct link to Gen. 3:15; 12:4; Acts 3:24-26; Gal. 3:8-9!

▣ "I acted for the sake of My name" This idea that historical actions related to Israel defined the character of YHWH seems to have begun with Moses' intercessory prayer in Exod. 32:11-14. It becomes a recurrent theme (cf. 2 Kgs. 19:34; 20:6; Ps. 23:3; 25:11; 31:3; 79:9; 106:8; 119:21; 143:9; Isa. 37:35; 43:25; 48:9,11; Jer. 14:7,21; Ezek. 20:9,14,22,44; 36:21,22-38).

YHWH's choice, love, and care for Israel was redemptively purposeful! There was/is an eternal redemptive plan: YHWH created humanity in His image and likeness for fellowship (cf. Genesis 1-2). See Millard Erickson, Christian Theology, 2nd ed., pp. 377-381.

Special Topic: YHWH's Eternal Redemptive Plan

entries.title: Ezekiel 20:11 "statutes. . .ordinances"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
20:11 "statutes. . .ordinances" See Special Topic: Terms for God's Revelation.

▣ "by which, if a man observe them, he will live" This alludes to the promises of Lev. 18:5; Deut. 30:15-20 and Ezekiel 18 (cf. Ezek. 20:13,21).

Life on earth is both physical and spiritual, similar to John 5:40; 10:10. Life is far more than mere physical existence. There is a quality of life that only God can give, which involves more than things or time. Augustine put it well when he said, "there is a God-shaped hole in every person." This is the image, likeness of the Creator, which only He can fill!

Special Topic: Keep

entries.title: Ezekiel 20:12 "sabbaths"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
20:12 "sabbaths" This term (BDB 992) is surprisingly mentioned several times in this chapter in correlation with words for YHWH's revelation (statutes, ordinances, cf. Ezek. 20:11-12, 13, 16, 19-20, 21, 24). The exact reason is uncertain. For a good brief discussion on the origin of the Sabbath see Roland de Vaux, Ancient Israel, vol. 2, pp. 475-483.

YHWH created this planet with cycles of nature (night, day) and worship times (feasts, sabbaths). They were initially given to regulate times of work and rest, as well as regular worship times, events, and feasts.

For Israel four things were crucial for a faithful follower.

  1. circumcision
  2. keeping the sabbaths
  3. regular attendance at the central shrine three times a year
  4. covenant obedience to YHWH's laws

Special Topic: Sabbath (OT)

Special Topic: Feasts of Israel

Special Topic: Circumcision

Special Topic: Keep

▣ "who sanctifies them" This PARTICIPLE (BDB 872, KB 1073, Piel PARTICIPLE) is from the root term "holy" (i.e. set apart for service to YHWH). Israel was made holy by God (cf. Exod. 31:13) in order to reveal holiness to the nations. Their holiness would be YHWH's way to manifest Himself to the nations (cf. Ezek. 20:9,14,22,39; 36:22-38).

Holiness is a covenant position (i.e. related to YHWH), but also a call to holy living!

Special Topic: Holy

Special Topic: Holiness/Sanctification

entries.title: Ezekiel 20:12-13
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
20:12-13 A brief content outline (compare with Nehemiah 9 and Acts 7):

  1. Ezek. 20:7-8 shows the rebellion of the people of God during the Exodus
  2. Ezek. 20:12-13 shows the rebellion of the people of God during the wilderness wandering period
  3. Ezek. 20:20-21 shows the rebellion of the second generation during the wilderness period
  4. Ezek. 20:24-25 shows the continual rebellion of the people of God even in the Promised Land
  5. in the midst of all this rebellion, God's grace and provision remain steadfast

entries.title: Ezekiel 20:13
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
20:13 Israel sins during the wilderness wandering period (i.e. from Egypt to Canaan).

  1. They did not walk in My statutes, BDB 229, KB 246, Qal PERFECT, cf. Ezek. 20:16 (twice), 18, 19, 21,39
  2. They rejected My ordinances, BDB 549, KB 540 Qal PERFECT, cf. Ezek. 20:16,24
  3. They profaned My sabbaths, BDB 320, KB 319, Piel PERFECT

Special Topic: Terms for God's Revelation

entries.title: Ezekiel 20:14
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
20:14 Again YHWH's concern for His name before the nations is emphaasized (cf. Ezek. 20:9,22,39; Isa. 48:9). YHWH has a personal interest in Israel (i.e. the coming Messiah).

Special Topic: Messiah

entries.title: Ezekiel 20:15
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 20:15 Here the reason for the forty years in the wilderness is explained. It was Israel's continuing sin (i.e. idolatry [cf. Ezek. 20:16b, Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE] and other covenant disobedience).

entries.title: Ezekiel 20:17
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
20:17 Even amidst their sin YHWH limited His wrath so as not to destroy Israel (cf. Isa. 48:9). In my opinion, so that Messiah would/could come from Abraham's line and fulfill Gen. 3:15! There has always been an eternal redemptive plan for all humanity (i.e. Isa. 66:23). Israel was a tool, a servant in that divine plan (cf. Acts 2:23; 3:18; 4:28; 13:29)!

Special Topic: YHWH's Eternal Redemptive Plan

entries.title: Ezekiel 20:18-20
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
20:18-20 A series of commands expresses YHWH's intent for the second generation of the Exodus.

  1. Negative (Israel's reality), Ezek. 20:18
    1. do not walk in the statutes of your fathers, Ezek. 20:18, BDB 229, KB 246, Qal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense (Special Topic: The Path, The Way)
    2. do not keep their ordinances, Ezek. 20:18, BDB 1036, KB 1581, Qal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense (Special Topic: Keep)
    3. do not defile yourselves with their idols, BDB 379, KB 375, Hithpael IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense (Special Topic: Idolatry)
  2. Positive (YHWH's hope), Ezek. 20:19-20
    1. walk in My statutes, Ezek. 20:19, BDB 229, KB 246, Qal IMPERATIVE
    2. keep My ordinances, Ezek. 20:19, BDB 1036, KB 1581, Qal IMPERATIVE
    3. observe them (lit. "do"), Ezek. 20:19, BDB 793, KB 889, Qal IMPERATIVE
    4. sanctify My sabbath, Ezek. 20:20, BDB 872, KB 1073, Piel IMPERATIVE

entries.title: Ezekiel 20:18-26
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 20:18-26 Again we return to the issue of multi-generational sin. Ezekiel, chapters 18-20, are related by this theme. If one generation rebels, YHWH tries to encourage and inform the next one. Tragically Israel continued its rebellion through time. It ultimately resulted in the Assyrian and Babylonian exiles (the bondage of Egypt in another land). Moses predicted this (cf. Deut. 4:25-31; 28:64-68), as did Joshua (cf. Josh. 24:19-20).

entries.title: Ezekiel 20:21-26
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
20:21-26 Israel did not obey, but rebelled against YHWH).

  1. They did not walk in His statutes, Ezek. 20:21
  2. They were not careful to observe His ordinances, Ezek. 20:21
  3. They profaned His sabbaths (cf. Ezek. 20:20), Ezek. 20:21

So YHWH

  1. resolved to pour out His wrath, Ezek. 20:21
  2. accomplished His anger against them in the wilderness, Ezek. 20:21
  3. withdrew His hand, Ezek. 20:22, cf. Ps. 74:11; Lam. 2:3
  4. acted for the sake of His name, Ezek. 20:22 (cf. Ezek. 36:22-38)
  5. scattered them among the nations, Ezek. 20:23 (cf. Ps. 106:19-27 describes the wilderness period, Ezek. 20:26-27 make the threat)
  6. dispersed them among the lands, Ezek. 20:23 (parallel to #5)
  7. gave them statutes that were not good, Ezek. 20:25
  8. gave them ordinances by which they could not live, Ezek. 20:25 (apparently from false prophets or faithless leaders; see full note at v. 25)
  9. pronounced them unclean (i.e. worship of Molech, child sacrifice, see Special Topic: Molech), Ezek. 20:26
  10. made them desolate, Ezek. 20:26

entries.title: Ezekiel 20:22 "I withdrew My hand"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
20:22 "I withdrew My hand" This idiom can mean

  1. YHWH chose not to punish (cf. v. 17; Ps. 74:11)
  2. YHWH chose not to help Israel (cf. Lam. 2:3)
  3. a prayer of Job (cf. Job 13:21)

entries.title: Ezekiel 20:25 "I also gave them statutes that were not good and ordinances by which they could not live"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
20:25 "I also gave them statutes that were not good and ordinances by which they could not live" This verse has been a great concern to many commentators because it seems to impugn God's character.

  1. Rashi says that YHWH let their inner evil loose (cf. Ps. 81:12; Isa. 66:4; Rom. 1:24, 26, 28).
  2. Kimchi, another Jewish expositor, says that they were given over to the enemy (i.e. Canaanite tribes) and they tried to live by their standards (i.e. worship of Molech, cf. Ezek. 20:26).
  3. This may be sarcasm, like Ezek. 20:29 and 39; they were using His guidelines (cf. Ezek. 20:11-13,16,19-21,24) in Canaanite ways (one example, Genesis 22 became a model for child sacrifice, cf. Ezek. 20:26). These people had the appearance of being faithful worshipers (like the elders of Ezek. 20:1-4), but in reality were idolaters (cf. Isa. 29:13-14).
  4. The IVP Bible Background Commentary (OT), p. 706, mostly written by John H. Walton, gives several key grammatical and lexical insights.
    1. he says this does not refer to the laws given at Mt. Sinai
    2. the word "torah" is not used
    3. the word "statutes" in v. 24 is FEMININE, which is normal, but in this verse it is MASCULINE
    4. it is possible it refers to YHWH's "decree" related to Judah's judgment for covenant infidelity
  5. This verse refers to the prophecies and regulations given by false prophets who YHWH used as the cause of His coming judgment (i.e. Ezek. 14:9).

entries.title: Ezekiel 20:26 "they caused all their first-born to pass through the fire"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
20:26 "they caused all their first-born to pass through the fire" This refers to the worship of the Phoenician fire god, Molech (cf. Ezek. 16:20; Lev. 18:21; 20:2-5; 2 Kings 17:17; 21:6; 23:10; 11 Chr. 28:3; Jer. 32:35). This may have been a misunderstanding about the death of the first-born recorded in Exodus 12, 13 or even the offering of Isaac in Genesis 22.

Special Topic: Molech

entries.title: Ezekiel 20:27
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 20:27 Israel was meant to be a light to the nations (cf. Ezek. 20:9, 14, 22, 41), but idolatry turned their witness into confusion, darkness, and blasphemy (e.g. "to throw accusations," BDB 154, KB 180, Piel PERFECT). Their covenant disobedience was seen as "unfaithfulness" or even "treachery" (BDB 591, KB 612, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT, cf. Ezek. 14:13; 17:20; 18:24; 20:27; 39:26) against YHWH.

entries.title: Ezekiel 20:28 "which I swore to give them"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
20:28 "which I swore to give them" This refers to the repeated promise by YHWH to give Abraham and his seed the Promised Land (i.e. Canaan).

  1. Abraham, Gen. 12:1,7; 13:15; 15:18
  2. Isaac, Gen. 50:24; Exod. 13:11; 33:1; Num. 11:12; 14:23; 32:11; Deut. 1:8; 9:5; 29:13
  3. Jacob, Gen. 26:3
  4. Israel, Num. 14:16; Deut. 4:21; 6:23; 8:1; 11:9; 19:8; 26:3,15; 28:11; 31:7,23; 34:4; Josh. 1:6; 21:43-44

Special Topic: Covenant Promises to the Patriarchs

▣ "then they saw every high hill and every leafy tree" This refers to the worship of the gods of the Canaanite fertility cult of Ba'al and Asherah/Astarte. They turned every hill and valley into a place of sexual idolatry (i.e. imitation magic, cf. Ezek. 6:13; 16:23-29; Isa. 57:5-8; Jer. 2:20; 3:6,13; 17:2; Hosea 4:13).

Special Topic: Fertility Worship of the Ancient Near East

Special Topic: Asherah

NASB, NRSV  "the provocation"
NKJV  "provoked Me"
TEV  "made Me angry"
NJB  "provoked My anger"
REB  "roused my anger"

The term (BDB 495) means "vexation" or "anger." It often refers to YHWH's anger at idolatry (cf. 1 Kgs. 15:30; 21:22; 2 Kgs. 23:26; see Special Topic: Idolatry).

The phrase "they poured out their libations" is mentioned as part of pagan rituals which provoked YHWH several times in Jeremiah (cf. Jer. 7:18; 19:13; 32:29; 44:17-19). YHWH is a jealous God (cf. Lev. 26:30-31). He will not accept rivals!

Special Topic: Jealous/Zealous

▣ "soothing aroma" This (BDB 629) is imagery for an acceptable sacrifice (incense or meat, cf. Gen. 8:21; Exod. 29:18,25,41; Lev. 1:9,13,17; Ezek. 6:13; 16:19; 20:28). It must be stated that this phrase does not imply that sacrifices were seen as a "feeding" of YHWH, which is part of the Mesopotamian texts (i.e. Gilgamesh Epic). It is an idiom!

Special Topic: A Soothing Aroma

▣ "poured out their libations" This refers to liquid offerings (usually wine), which often accompanied other sacrifices.

Special Topic: Alcohol (fermentation) and Alcoholism (addiction)

entries.title: Ezekiel 20:29 "Bamah"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
20:29 "Bamah" This is the Hebrew word for "high place" (BDB 119). Originally they were local shrines (cf. 1 Sam. 7:17; 9:12-25; 10:5,13; 1 Kgs. 3:2-4) which were not condemned.

However, the same places became the sites of fertility worship (cf. Num. 22:41; 1 Kgs. 11:7; 12:31-32; 14:23; 15:14; 22:43; 2 Chr. 21:11; Jer. 7:31; 19:5; 32:35; Hosea 4:13; 10:8; Amos 7:9; Micah 1:5). Josiah ordered them to be destroyed (cf. 1 Kgs. 13:2,32,33; 2 Kgs. 23:5-20; 2 Chr. 34:3-4). The centralization of worship in Jerusalem (cf. Lev. 17:3-5; Deut. 12:13-14) was meant to control this potential abuse.

entries.title: Ezekiel 20:30-32
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
20:30-32 The question is to whom does "your fathers" refer?

  1. immediate past generation
  2. wilderness wandering generation
  3. early settlers in the Promised Land
  4. or, collective of all past generations

The specific idols referred to are the fertility gods of Canaan (i.e. Ba'al, Asherah, Molech). Verse 32 describes the enormity of the problem in the statement "we will be like the nations, like the tribes of the land, serving wood and stone." Remember that the Israelites were given the land of Canaan because of the continuing idolatry of the tribes of the land (cf. Gen. 15:12-21). If Israel repeats their abominations, she will also be removed from the land (uniquely dedicated/owned by YHWH). Israel loses that which makes her distinct! Israel cannot be a light to the nations because she has become one of the nations! She was lost as a vehicle of revelation!

entries.title: Ezekiel 20:32
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
20:32 This statement of desire by the idolatrous Judeans will never come to pass (the Qal INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE and the Qal IMPERFECT of the VERB "to be," BDB 224, KB 243). God's covenant people cannot be allowed to be like the other people. God desires that He (the only true God) be revealed to the nations through His people! They are His people for this very purpose.

Special Topic: YHWH's Eternal Redemptive Plan)

entries.title: Ezekiel 20:33
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
20:33 YHWH will not allow His covenant people to completely degenerate into idolatry.

  1. surely with a mighty hand
  2. with wrath poured out, cf. Lam. 4:11

These phrases (i.e. #1,#2) were originally used of YHWH's great and merciful acts of deliverance (in the Exodus, cf. Deut. 3:24; 4:34; 5:15; 6:21; 7:8,19; 9:26,29; 11:2; 26:8; Josh. 4:24). But now they are used to demonstrate that YHWH is fighting against rebellious Israel, not for her!

YHWH will be king (i.e. 1 Sam. 8:7)! He will accomplish His purposes through national Israel! Even though He exiles them, He will bring them back into the land (cf. Ezek. 20:34,41; 11:17; 28:25; 29:13; 34:12-13; Deut. 30:3; Jer. 23:3).

entries.title: Ezekiel 20:37 "pass under the rod"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
20:37 "pass under the rod" This refers to a shepherd's rod (BDB 986) used for counting sheep (i.e. Lev. 27:32; Jer. 33:13).

NASB, NKJV, JPSOA  "into the bond of the covenant"
NRSV, NEB  "within the bond of the covenant"
TEV  "make you obey my covenant"
NJB  "bring you to respect the covenant"
REB  "counting you as you enter"
LXX, RSV  "bring you in by number"
Peshitta  "bring you into the discipline of the
  covenant"

The MT is reflected in the NASB. The UBS Text Project, p. 60, gives it a "C" rating (considerable doubt). The LXX, REB, RSV emend the word "bond" (מסרת; BDB 64, KB 608) to "by number" (מספר; KB 607). Both make sense in this context.

entries.title: Ezekiel 20:38
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
20:38 The exile will "purge" (BDB 140, KB 162, Qal PERFECT)

  1. those who continue to rebel, BDB 597, KB 632, Qal PARTICIPLE
  2. those who continue to transgress, BDB 833, KB 981, Qal PARTICIPLE

▣ "they will not enter the land" See Ezek. 20:15, 16, and 13:9. Evil will be purged from the Promised Land (and one day all the earth)!

entries.title: Ezekiel 20:39-40
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
20:39-40 The verse begins with sarcasm (two Qal IMPERATIVES, "go" and "serve"), denoting Israel's current idolatry. However, a new day is coming (i.e. "afterwards," BDB 29)! This is the great news of chapter 20. Judah has been so consistently unfaithful, but YHWH is consistently faithful. He will restore a repentant and purged seed of Abraham!

Note how the text expresses this.

  1. You will surely listen to Me, Ezek. 20:39
  2. My holy name you will profane no longer, Ezek. 20:39, cf. Ezek. 36:21,22; Lev. 18:21; 19:12; 20:3; 21:6
  3. All Israel will serve Him, Ezek. 20:40
  4. I shall accept them, Ezek. 20:40
  5. I shall accept their sacrifices, Ezek. 20:40
  6. I shall accept them as an approved sacrifice, Ezek. 20:41
  7. I will gather them from the nations, Ezek. 20:41
  8. I shall prove Myself holy among you in the sight of the nations, Ezek. 20:41

entries.title: Ezekiel 20:40 "For on My holy mountain"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
20:40 "For on My holy mountain" In context this refers to Mount Moriah, on which Abraham offered Isaac (i.e. Genesis 22) and on which the temple was later built (i.e. 1 Kings 7-8). This is a symbolic way of asserting the effective working of the Mosaic covenant.

The term "mountain(s)" (BDB 249) is used often in Ezekiel.

  1. It often is a way of referring to the whole land (as Mt. Seir stands for Edom, cf. Ezek. 35:2-3), i.e. Ezek. 6:3; 19:9; 33:28; 34:13,14; 37:22
  2. It often is a way of identifying the site of fertility worship, i.e. Ezek. 6:3-4,13; 18:6,11
  3. It refers to YHWH's special holy mountain (i.e. the temple), cf. Ezek. 17:22-23; 20:40; 28:14,16 (possibly a divine mountain in the north); Ezek. 43:12

The phrase "the mountains of Israel" is unique to Ezekiel (i.e. note repetition in Ezekiel 36).

Special Topic: Moriah, Salem, Jebus, Jerusalem, Zion

entries.title: Ezekiel 20:41 "As a soothing aroma I shall accept you"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
20:41 "As a soothing aroma I shall accept you" This CONSTRUCT (BDB 629 and 926) is imagery for a sacrifice (see note at Ezek. 20:28). In Ezekiel it has been used consistently of pagan offerings (cf. Ezek. 6:13; 16:19; 20:28). But here it refers to the people of Israel (cf. Ezek. 43:27). YHWH brought back the remnant from exile and denotes His acceptance of them by this priestly phrase (remember Ezekiel was a trained priest of the line of Zadok)! A people in fellowship with their Creator has always been the goal of the tabernacle and Levitical sacrifices.

Special Topic: A Soothing Aroma

entries.title: Ezekiel 20:43
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
20:43 Israel's true repentance will cause them

  1. to remember (BDB 269, KB 269, Qal PERFECT) their sin (cf. Ezek. 16:61,63; 36:31, in Ezek. 6:9 they will remember how they hurt YHWH).
  2. to loathe (BDB 876, KB 1083, Niphal PERFECT) themselves for it (cf. Ezek. 6:9; 36:31).

entries.title: Ezekiel 20:44 "not according to your evil ways or according to your corrupt ways"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
20:44 "not according to your evil ways or according to your corrupt ways" Grace, oh grace! What a marvelous message to share! God will deal with us according to who He is and what He has done, not according to who we are or what we have done (i.e. Ps. 103:8-14)! Hallelujah.

The spiritual principle "we reap what we sow" is abrogated by the mercy and eternal redemptive purposes of YHWH. Israel has a place in a larger scheme, as do the nations (cf. Romans 9-11).

entries.title: Ezekiel 20:45
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
20:45 A new revelation of a cleansing fire to sweep Canaan of idolatry. This parable introduces Ezekiel 21. This is where the MT starts a new chapter.

Special Topic: Fire

entries.title: Ezekiel 20:46 "set your face toward"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
20:46 "set your face toward" This is a literary marker for a judgment pronouncement (cf. Ezek. 6:2; 13:17; 20:46; 21:2; 25:2; 28:21; 29:2; 35:2; 38:2) which follows the same imagery used of YHWH (cf. Lev. 26:17; Jer. 21:10; Ezek. 14:8; 15:7).

▣ "Teman" This is one of three different words which denote the south.

  1. Temas (BDB 412, cf. Ezek. 40:24,27,28,44,45; 41:11,12,13,18)
  2. Darom (BDB 204, cf. Ezek. 21:2; 40:24,27,28,44; 41:11; 42:12,13)
  3. Negeb (BDB 616, cf. Ezek. 21:3; 40:2; 46:9; 47:19; 48:16,28,33)

All of these are allusions to the capital city of Jerusalem (cf. Ezek. 21:1).

entries.title: Ezekiel 20:47 "it shall consume every green tree in you, as well as every dry tree"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
20:47 "it shall consume every green tree in you, as well as every dry tree" This parable describes a coming judgment that will affect all Israelites. Here again, we are confronted with the two different ways of judgment.

  1. from father to children to the third and fourth generations, cf. Exod. 20:5; Deut. 5:9
  2. one individual's life does not affect the children, cf. Ezekiel 18

Somehow both are true! One deals with individuals and one with a national collective. The tension remains! For me personally, my hope lies in Deut. 5:10 and 7:9! My nation may experience the judgment of God, which affects me, but My God knows me and will bring me (and my faithful descendants) to Himself!

entries.title: Ezekiel 20:49
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
20:49 The idolatrous elders listening to Ezekiel (cf. Ezek. 20:1) heard these words and thought he was speaking only figuratively. Chapter 21 is a reaction to this!

▣
NASB, Peshitta, NKJV  "speaking parables"
LXX  "spoken in a parable"
NRSV  "a maker of allegories"
TEV, NJB  "speak in riddles"
REB  "He deals only in figures of speech"
JPSOA  "a riddle monger"

The MT has a double form, משׁל (BDB 605) made up of a Piel PARTICIPLE and the PLURAL NOUN. The Jewish Study Bible, p. 1080, says this echoes Ezek. 17:2.

entries.title: Ezekiel 21:1
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
21:1 The context starts in Ezek. 20:45, which marks off a new vision by the characteristic phrase "the word of the Lord came to me saying" (cf. Ezek. 3:16; 6:1; 7:1; 11:14; 12:1,8,17, 21,26; 13:1; 14:2,12; 15:1; 16:1; 17:1,11; 18:1; 20:2,45; 21:1,8,18; 22:1,17,23; 23:1; 24:1,15,20; 25:1; 26:1; 27:1; 28:1,7; 30:1,20; 31:1; 32:1,17; 33:1,23; 34:1; 35:1; 36:16; 38:1). Remember that the original manuscripts had no chapters, paragraphs, or verse divisions in the ancient Hebrew scrolls. This repeated phrase helped scroll readers find the place to begin reading. It also helped to show (1) new contexts and (2) related contexts.

Special Topic: Names for Deity, D.

▣ "saying" This VERB (BDB 55, KB 65) occurs twenty-two times in this chapter. YHWH wants His wayward people to hear Him clearly!

entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
