Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

  1. First paragraph
  2. Second paragraph
  3. Third paragraph, etc.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Ezekiel 41:4 "This is the most holy place"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
41:4 "This is the most holy place" This refers to the Holy of Holies where the Ark of the Covenant originally dwelt (cf. Exod. 26:33-34; 1 Kgs. 6:16; 8:6). This was the place of atonement, the place of YHWH's personal presence (cf. Leviticus 16).

Special Topic: Chart of the Tabernacle

Special Topic: Ark of the Covenant

41:7
NASB  "the second story"
NKJV, NRSV, JPSOA  "the middle one"
LXX  "third story"
REB  "the middle tier"
LXX  "the middle part"

The ADJECTIVE (BDB 1064, KB 1724) means "middle." From the context it must refer to the middle or second level (cf. Ezek. 42:5,6).

The Jewish Study Bible, p. 1122, says Ezek. 41:7 is describing a spiraling staircase.

41:16
NASB  "latticed windows"
NKJV  "beveled window frames"
NRSV  "windows with recessed frames"
TEV  "the windows could be covered"
NJB  "the windows were screened with latticework"

This descriptive term (BDB 31, KB 36) can mean

  1. closed, barred, cf. Ezek. 41:16c
  2. framed, cf. 1 Kgs. 6:4; 7:4-5
  3. narrow

▣ "were paneled with wood all around" This was just like Solomon's temple (cf. 1 Kgs. 6:15).

entries.title: Ezekiel 41:18 "cherubim and palm trees"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
41:18 "cherubim and palm trees" These were the same decorations that were used in Solomon's temple (cf. 1 Kgs. 6:8,29; 7:29,36). There is some doubt as to the exact physical description of the Cherubim:

  1. the Ark of the Covenant had Cherubim who had one face each
  2. in Ezekiel 1 and 10 they seem to have four faces
  3. Revelation 4 records a different face for each creature

Special Topic: Cherubim

entries.title: Ezekiel 41:22 "the altar of wood"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
41:22 "the altar of wood" There are two possibilities for this piece of furniture because it is called both an altar (BDB 258) and a table (BDB 1020):

  1. the table of showbread (cf. Exod. 25:23-30; Lev. 24:5-9; 1 Kgs. 6:20-22; 11 Chr. 3:lff)
  2. the altar of incense which stood before the inner veil (cf. Exod. 30:1-10; 37:25-29).

Special Topic: Showbread of the Presence

Special Topic: Altar of Incense

Copyright © 2014 Bible Lessons International

entries.title: Ezekiel 42:1 "he brought me"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
42:1 "he brought me" See note at Ezek. 41:1.

NASB, NRSV, NJB, JPSOA  "outer court"
TEV  "outer courtyard"
RSV  "inner court"

The Hebrew OT Text Project of the UBS, p. 160, gives "outer" an A rating (very high probability).

42:4
NASB, NRSV, REB  "a way of one hundred cubits"
NKJV  "at a distance of one cubit"

The MT has "one cubit," but the Septuagint and Peshitta have "one hundred cubits. The Expositors Bible Commentary (p. 967) says that "an inner walk" (BDB 237) of Ezek. 42:4 can be understood as a step (1x10 cubits). There are many ambiguous and rare terms and phrases in this section that remain unknown.

Special Topic: Cubit.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

  1. First paragraph
  2. Second paragraph
  3. Third paragraph, etc.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Ezekiel 42:13 "the priests who are near to the Lord"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
42:13 "the priests who are near to the Lord" This refers to Zadok's line which exclusively offered sacrifices (cf. Ezek. 40:46). These priests were allowed to eat part of most sacrifices (cf. Lev. 2:3; 5:13; 6:16,26,29; 7:6,10; 10:12-14). The sacrifices are described in Leviticus 1-7.

Special Topic: Sacrifices in Mesopotamia and Israel, IV.

entries.title: Ezekiel 42:14
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
42:14 The priests' garments (cf. Exod. 39:1-43) that they wore when ministering at the altar must be left in the "holy" place. This corresponds to Aaron's instruction in Lev. 16:23.

Special Topic: Tabernacle (chart)

entries.title: Ezekiel 42:16 "the measuring reed five hundred reeds by the measuring reed"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
42:16 "the measuring reed five hundred reeds by the measuring reed" The problem occurs in the length of a "measuring reed." Earlier in the literary unit (cf. Ezek. 40:5) it was over ten feet, but here it seems to refer to one cubit (i.e. 21 inches). The MT scholars recognized the problem.

Qere (to be read), five hundred reeds

Ketiv (written), five cubits, reeds

This same confusion is repeated in Ezek. 42:17, 18, and 19.

If one assumes that a reed is over 10' the area was about 500 acres (The Jewish Study Bible, p. 1125), if 21 inches, the area is about 14 acres. If the larger measurement is used it denotes the symbolic nature because of its size.

entries.title: Ezekiel 42:20 "to divide between the holy and profane"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
42:20 "to divide between the holy and profane" This is another example of architectural design to accentuate holiness. The wall was too low to provide protection; therefore, some commentators see it as a wall of holiness (similar to the dividing walls of Herod's temple).

 

Copyright © 2014 Bible Lessons International

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

  1. First paragraph
  2. Second paragraph
  3. Third paragraph, etc.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Ezekiel 43:2 "the glory of the God of Israel was coming from the way of the east"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
43:2 "the glory of the God of Israel was coming from the way of the east" We must remember that the glory, or the presence of YHWH, had left, moving east to be with the exiles in Babylon (cf. Ezek. 10:18-22; 11:22-24). Now He is returning to His temple. It is a way of affirming that the ancient covenant had been re-established (cf. Ps. 24:7-10).

▣ "His voice was like the sound of many waters" See notes at Ezek. 1:24 and Rev. 1:15; 14:2; 19:6.

▣ "the earth shone with His glory" The VERB (BDB 21, KB 24, Hiphil PERFECT) is used of the Shekinah Cloud of Glory during the wilderness wandering period (cf. Exod. 13:21; 14:20). This is part of the Aaronic blessing of Num. 6:25. It involved God's face (i.e. intimate presence) to shine in/on those whom He fully accepted.

Special Topic: Glory

Special Topic: Shekinah

entries.title: Ezekiel 43:3
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
43:3 This vision of the manifested glory of YHWH is the same as in the vision that Ezekiel saw in chapters 1 and 10 (i.e. the portable throne chariot of YHWH).

NASB, NRSV, REB, NET  "when He came"
NKJV, NJB  "when I came"
TEV  "when God came"

The MT has "when I came" (בבאי), but some Hebrew manuscripts (six) and the Vulgate have "when he came" (בבאו). There is much confusion in Ezekiel related to the PRONOUNS "I," "you"; "He" and "they."

The UBS Text Project, p. 169, gives the MT a "C" rating (considerable doubt).

▣ "I fell on my face" See notes at Ezek. 1:28 and 3:23.

entries.title: Ezekiel 43:5 "the Spirit lifted me up and brought me"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
43:5 "the Spirit lifted me up and brought me" See notes at Ezek. 3:12 and 40:1.

Special Topic: Spirit in the Bible

▣ "the glory of the Lord filled the house" This was like the Shekinah cloud that came down on Mount Sinai (cf. Exodus 19:16,18,20), the Tabernacle (cf. Exodus 40:34,35), and Solomon's temple (cf. 1 Kgs. 8:10,11; 2 Chr. 5:14; 7:1-2). This is another way of showing that YHWH was present and the covenant was reestablished.

Special Topic: Shekinah

entries.title: Ezekiel 43:6 "I heard one speaking to me from the house"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
43:6 "I heard one speaking to me from the house" From the next three verses we know it was YHWH Himself who had just returned from Babylon. This seems to imply that Ezekiel thought this message was for the post-exilic community. Surely YHWH does not stay in Babylon.

▣ "while a man was standing beside me" This refers to one of the angel guides (cf. Ezek. 40:3-4).

Special Topic: Apocalyptic Literature

▣ "Son of man" See full note at Ezek. 2:1.

entries.title: Ezekiel 43:7 "the place of My throne"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
43:7 "the place of My throne" Normally YHWH's throne is in heaven, but since the vision of chapters 1 and 10 (YHWH's portable Throne Chariot, cf. Ezek. 1:26; 10:1), the new temple is both His throne (cf. Jer. 3:17; 14:21; 17:12) and His footstool (i.e. the space between the Cherubim on the Ark, cf. 1 Chr. 28:2; Ps. 132; 7: Isa. 66:1; Lam. 2:1). Obviously this is imagery for power and majesty and not meant to be turned into YHWH, the eternal Spirit, actually sitting on a chair/throne! Even Ps. 45:6 probably refers to the coming Davidic descendant (i.e. Messiah, cf. 2 Samuel 7; 1 Chronicles 17), not God (see Hard Sayings of the Bible, pp. 270-271).

Special Topic: Cherubim

Special Topic: Ark of the Covenant

Special Topic: God Described As Human

▣ "the place of the soles of My feet" Although YHWH lived in heaven, His feet were between the Cherubim (i.e. Jerusalem, Mt. Moriah, cf. Exod. 25:22; Isa. 37:16) above the Ark of the Covenant in the holy of holies (cf. 1 Chr. 28:2; Ps. 99:5; 132:7; Isa. 60:13). This dedication service of the new temple is very similar to Solomon's in 1 Kings 8 (cf. Isa. 66:1).

▣ "where I will dwell among the sons of Israel" The VERB (BDB 1014, KB 1496, Qal IMPERFECT) is used so often in Deuteronomy of the place God will cause His name to dwell (cf. Deut. 12:11; 14:23; 16:2,6,11; 26:2). This promise is also found in Ezek. 37:26-27. It goes back to Exod. 25:8 (YHWH gave them a detailed pattern of the tabernacle, also Exod. 25:9; 29:45-46).

This same covenant language is continued when the coming Messiah is called Emmanuel (i.e. God with us) in Isa. 7:14 (cf. Matt. 1:23). This is another way of showing that the covenant has been reestablished (cf. Ezek. 16:60-63; 37:24-28). YHWH is with His people.

Special Topic: Eden

▣ "forever" See Special Topic: Forever ('olam).

▣ "Israel will not defile My holy name" This is a recurrent issue in Ezekiel. YHWH wants His name revealed to the nations, not profaned among them (cf. Ezek. 20:9,14,22,39; 36:21,22; 39:7; 43:7,8)! Israel was meant to be a kingdom of priests, but they turned into a kingdom of idolaters! This will change; a new day is coming! There will be no distinction between Jew and Gentile anymore (cf. Eph. 2:11-3:13). Joel 2:28 has been realized (cf. Acts 2:14-21).

Special Topic: YHWH's Eternal Redemptive Plan

Special Topic: "The Name" of YHWH (OT)

▣ "the corpses" This term (BDB 803, KB 910) has several possible meanings.

  1. the bodies of dead kings in their tombs/monuments in the vicinity of the temple (cf. Lev. 26:30)
  2. the offering of dead bodies to Molech (same consonants as "king"; see Special Topic: Molech)
  3. the place and practice of ancestral idolatry (cf. Ezek. 43:8; 8:3,16)

The parallelism suggests #3.

NASB  "when they die"
NKJV  "on their high places"
NRSV, JPSOA  "at their death"
TEV, NJB, Peshitta  "by burying the corpses of their dead
  kings"
REB  "with the monuments raised to dead
  kings"
LXX  "the murders of their princes in the
  midst of them"

The only difference between the two options is the vowel points of the MT scholars. The Hebrew consonants are the same. The question is, "Does the context refer to idolatry (cf. Ezek. 5:11; 23:36-45) or the monuments (stele) of dead sinful kings?" The The IVP Bible Background Commentary (OT), p. 726, suggests:

"These lifeless idols" are probably not corpses but refer to a pagan cult of the dead, similar to that of Lev. 26:30. Ezekiel probably had in mind a veneration of the spirits of Israel's royal ancestors, much like a cult of the royal dead at Ugarit. Whether the kings were considered deified at either place is not clear."

Special Topic: Masoretic Text

entries.title: Ezekiel 43:8 "their threshold by My threshold"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
43:8 "their threshold by My threshold" The IVP Bible Background Commentary (OT), p. 726, has a good explanitory note:

"The statement here in verse 8 corresponds with the description of the Solomonic temple in 1 Kings 6-7. The original temple was built as one element of the entire Solomonic palace complex. Only a wall separated the temple and palace, and they bordered "threshold to threshold, and doorpost to doorpost."

▣ "abominations" See Special Topic: Abomination (OT)

▣ "So I have consumed them in My anger" See Special Topic: God Described As Human (anthropomorphism).

entries.title: Ezekiel 43:9-11
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
43:9-11 There is a series of commands.

  1. put away harlotry, Ezek. 43:9, BDB 934, KB 1221, Piel IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense
  2. describe/declare, Ezek. 43:10, BDB 616, KB 665, Hiphil IMPERATIVE
  3. be ashamed of iniquities, Ezek. 43:10, BDB 483, KB 480, Niphal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense
  4. make known to them, Ezek. 43:11, BDB 393, KB 390, Hiphil IMPERATIVE
  5. write, Ezek. 43:11, BDB 507, KB 503, Qal IMPERATIVE
  6. observe, Ezek. 43:11, BDB 1036, KB 1581, Qal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense

entries.title: Ezekiel 43:9 "Now let them"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
43:9 "Now let them" Ezek. 43:9, 11 show the conditional nature of Ezekiel's covenant, as most covenants in the OT were conditional on mankind's appropriate response to God in repentance, faith, obedience, and perseverance.

Special Topic: Covenant

▣ "and I will dwell among them forever" See note at Ezek. 43:7.

entries.title: Ezekiel 43:10
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
43:10 This elaborate plan of the new temple was meant to

  1. remind them of the Exodus (a detailed pattern from YHWH of a place of worship and its procedures, cf. Exodus 25-31; Special Topic: Repentance [OT])
  2. cause them to repent (cf. Ezek. 6:9; 16:61,63; 20:43; 36:31; 43:11)
  3. give them an opportunity for obedience (i.e. "and do them," Ezek. 43:11; Special Topic: Keep)
NASB  "let them measure the plan"
NKJV, NRSV  "let them measure the pattern"
TEV  "let them study the plan"
NJB  "(let them draw up the plan of it)"
JPSOA  "let them measure its design"
LXX, RSV, NEB  "and its appearance and plan"

The MT is reflected in the NKJV, NRSV. The UBS Text Project, p. 171, supports the MT over the LXX, but only with a "C" rating (considerable doubt).

entries.title: Ezekiel 43:11
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
43:11 Notice the parallelism between

  1. design, BDB 849, KB 1017, only in this chapter, possibly drawing, plan, or form
  2. statutes, BDB 349, cf. Ezek. 43:18
  3. laws, BDB 435, cf. Ezek. 43:12(twice)

YHWH is giving them a new temple (i.e. to build) and new procedures (i.e. to act on) to test their obedience. They failed the tabernacle test; they failed Solomon's temple test; they will fail Zerubbabel's and Herod's tests also! Only after the new covenant of chapter 36 and the restoration of chapter 37 can Israel be obedient.

Special Topic: Terms for God's Revelation

entries.title: Ezekiel 43:13 "cubit"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
43:13 "cubit" See Special Topic: Cubit

NASB, NKJV, NRSV, JPSOA, LXX, NET  "height"
REB  "rim"
NJB, Peshitta  "edge"
JPSOA footnote, NET footnote  "bulge"

The MT has "back" (BDB 146; it suggests "anything that is convex").

  1. back, rim ‒ גב
  2. height ‒ גבה (KB 170)

The UBS Text Project, p. 173, gives the MT a "C" rating (considerable doubt).

This term relates to the rim of the altar.

entries.title: Ezekiel 43:15 "and from the altar hearth shall extend upwards four horns"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
43:15 "and from the altar hearth shall extend upwards four horns" There are numerous references to the four horns (i.e. like cow horns) of the sacrificial altar in the OT (cf. Exod. 27:2; 29:12; 30:10; 1 Kgs. 1:50; 2:28). Even the incense altar had four horns. This was the most holy part of the sacrificial altar on which a small portion of the blood was smeared (cf. Exod. 29:12; Lev. 4:7,18,25; 9:9; Ezek. 43:20) before the rest was poured out at the base of the altar of sacrifice.

Special Topic: Altar of Sacrifice

Special Topic: Altar of Incense

43:16
NASB, NKJV, NRSV, NEt  "altar hearth"
TEV  "the top of the altar"
REB, JPSOA, NJB  "hearth"
LXX, Peshitta  "the altar"

The MT has BDB 72, KB 87 I, which occurs only here in vv. 15,16. KB suggests a related form which denotes an altar for burnt sacrifices.

entries.title: Ezekiel 43:18
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
43:18 This clearly states that the altar was for the purpose of atonement (i.e. Lev. 1:5,11; 3:2,8,13), not a memorial (cf. Ezek. 45:15, 17, 20). This is superseded by the NT book of Hebrews (esp. Heb. 9-10), which sees Jesus as the last sacrifice needed to atone for mankind's sin.

Special Topic: The Superiority of the New Covenant Over the Mosaic Covenant

entries.title: Ezekiel 43:19
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
43:19 Originally, only the family of Aaron could act as priests serving the altar, but in the post-exilic period there was not enough of this family to serve so other Levitical families begn to share the task.

Special Topic: Levitical Priests

entries.title: Ezekiel 43:20 "cleanse it"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 43:20 "cleanse it" This VERB (BDB 306, KB 305, Piel PERFECT with waw) is repeated in Ezek. 43:22 (twice) and the Piel INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT in Ezek. 43:23. The Piel denotes cleansing by means of a blood sacrifice (cf. Lev. 8:15; Ezek. 45:18) as does the next VERB "make atonement" (BDB 497, KB 493, Piel PERFECT with waw, cf. Ezek. 43:26; 45:20). The altar must be inaugurated with a blood sacrifice (cf. Lev. 16:18). Ezekiel was very familiar with Levitical rituals.

entries.title: Ezekiel 43:24 "salt"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
43:24 "salt" Usually salt was put with the grain offerings (cf. Lev. 2:13) and here with blood offerings. Because of Ezek. 6:9 it possibly was put on all offerings. It was a symbol of the Israelite's covenant with YHWH (cf. Num. 18:19; 2 Chr. 13:5).

Special Topic: Salt

entries.title: Ezekiel 43:25 "for seven days"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
43:25 "for seven days" This purification and dedication procedure parallels Exod. 29:35-37; Lev. 8:33-36. Holy things had to have a special initiation and also rigid procedures for maintaining their holiness. The Mosaic legislation (and also that of Ezekiel) was keen on maintaining a strict separation between the holy and the mundane, the clean and the unclean. This ritual separation reflected their theology of the world and life, the physical and spiritual.

▣ "goat" Goats were not used in the Mosaic system for dedication offerings.

entries.title: Ezekiel 43:26 "so shall they consecrate it"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 43:26 "so shall they consecrate it" This is literally "fill the hands" (BDB 569, KB 583, Piel PERFECT with waw; cf. Exod. 29:24).

entries.title: Ezekiel 43:27 "peace offering"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
43:27 "peace offering" This was the fellowship meal where God symbolically ate with the offerer (Leviticus 3). It was eaten in the temple setting and is a foreshadowing of the Lord's Supper.

Special Topic: Peace Offering

▣ "I will accept you, declares the Lord God" This was the purpose of Ezekiel's sacrificial cultus (i.e. reunite sinful national Israel with their holy God). Ezekiel sees it in terms of ancient sacrificial ritual (i.e. Leviticus 1-7). Remember, he was a trained priest.

The VERB (BDB 953, KB 1280, Qal PERFECT) is also used in Ezek. 20:40,41 of an accepted sacrifice. Because YHWH was with His people, purity, holiness, ceremonial cleanness must be maintained!

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

  1. When were these chapters fulfilled?
  2. What is the purpose of the end-time sacrificial system?
  3. Describe the Cherubim.
  4. What is the purpose of an end-time temple?

entries.title: Ezekiel 44:1-3
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
44:1-3 This text is often used as a prophecy relating to modern Jerusalem, Israel. The modern city's wall has a sealed eastern gate, but these are not the walls of Jerusalem that were built by Solomon, Nehemiah, or even Herod. These modern walls were built by an Islamic ruler in the ninth century A.D. Jerusalem was destroyed by Titus in A.D. 70.

Ezekiel's temple is symbolic of YHWH's return to Palestine and His fulfillment of the covenant promises of the Mosaic covenant. Notice in context that this passage refers to YHWH Himself, who has already returned! He left the temple from this place (cf. chapters 8-10) and He once-and-for-all returned to this place (cf. Ezek. 44:4; 43:4-5).

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

  1. First paragraph
  2. Second paragraph
  3. Third paragraph, etc.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Ezekiel 44:3 "the prince"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
44:3 "the prince" This is a Messianic reference (see full note at Ezek. 46:2, cf. Ezek. 34:24; 37:24-25).

Special Topic: OT Titles for the Special Coming One

▣ "eat bread before the Lord" This is imagery for worship and covenant (cf. Gen. 31:54; Exod. 24:9-11). To eat with someone was a sign of friendship and fellowship. It was one way to seal a covenant. This fellowship meal is institutionalized in the Peace Offering and the meal that follows (cf. Leviticus 3 and 7).

Also note that there is no hint that the prince is divine. The NT deity of the Messiah was a surprise because it seems to conflict with monotheism. Only the NT clearly reveals this surprising truth (i.e. John 1:1-14; Phil. 2:6-11; Col. 1:15-18; Heb. 1:2-3; Rev. 1).

Special Topic: Monotheism

Special Topic: Worship

Special Topic: The Deity of Christ from the OT

Special Topic: The Trinity

entries.title: Ezekiel 44:4 "the glory of the Lord"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
44:4 "the glory of the Lord" This phrase refers to the personal presence of YHWH (cf. Ezek. 1:28; 3:23; 43:4-5; Exod. 24:16).

Special Topic: Glory (kabod. OT)

▣ "filled the house" This is reminiscent of

  1. the tabernacle (cf. Exod. 40:34-35)
  2. Solomon's temple (cf. 1 Kgs. 8:11; 2 Chr. 5:14; 7:1-3)

It was a visible way of showing YHWH's acceptance and presence. Ezekiel saw YHWH's glory fill the temple in his vision of chapter 10 (cf. Ezek. 10:4), as it would at YHWH's return (cf. Ezek. 43:5).

▣ "I fell on my face" Ezekiel (as all humans) is staggered by the holy, glorious presence of God (i.e. Ezek. 1:28; 3:23; 43:3; Gen. 17:3; Lev. 9:24; Dan. 8:17; 10:9,10,15; Rev. 1:17).

entries.title: Ezekiel 44:5
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
44:5 This verse is very similar to Ezek. 40:4, with three commands.

  1. mark well (lit. "set your heart on") – BDB 962, KB 1321, Qal IMPERATIVE
  2. see – BDB 906, KB 1321, Qal IMPERATIVE
  3. hear – BDB 1033, KB 1570, Qal IMPERATIVE

Ezekiel is to be careful what he sees so he can describe this future temple accurately for a restored, obedient Israel, especially the new temple's entrances and exits.

44:6
NASB  "the rebellious ones"
NKJV, NET  "the rebellious"
NRSV, Peshitta, JPSOA  "the rebellious house"
TEV  "those rebellious people"
NJB, NEB  "the rebels"
LXX  "the embittering house" or "the
  provoking house"

The MT has two parallel phrases.

  1. to the rebellious
  2. to the house of Israel

The LXX adds the word "house" to the MT's first phrase. The UBS Text Project, p. 175, gives the MT (option #1) a "B" rating (some doubt).

This NOUN (BDB 598) refers to Judah (cf. Ezek. 2:5-8; 3:9,26,27; 12:2 [twice], 3,9,25; 17:12; 24:3). They are called rebellious because they violated YHWH's statutes about the temple, especially in connection to non-Israelites' involvement in temple activities. This refers specifically to political alliances made with foreign powers (i.e. Egypt, Babylon, etc.). This involved the acknowledgement of their gods.

▣ "abominations" See Special Topic: Abomination.

entries.title: Ezekiel 44:7 "uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
44:7 "uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh" In context this refers to non-Israelites. It speaks of a rebellious heart, as well as an unbelieving (i.e. non-covenant) person. It could refer to

  1. political alliances with foreign nations (i.e. possibly Jer. 9:25-26)
  2. welcoming foreign ambassadors by showing them the temple (i.e. 2 Kgs. 20:12-15)
  3. foreign servants in the tabernacle (cf. Josh. 9:23,27)
  4. the foreign guards in the temple (cf. 1 Kgs. 11:4-16)

but the exact reference is uncertain. Ezekiel witnessed some of the abominations which occurred in Ezekiel 8-10.

The same expression, "uncircumcised of heart," can be used of rebellious Israelites (cf. Lev. 26:41; Deut. 10:16; 30:6; Jer. 4:4; 9:25-26).

Circumcision was a covenant sign (cf. Gen. 17:9-14) and a covenant attitude of obedience and humility. The priests had violated this covenantal trust (cf. Ezek. 44:9-14).

Special Topic: Circumcision

▣ "profane" This term's (BDB 320, KB 319 I) meaning is uncertain, but the same three consonant roots in Arabic meant "to loosen" or "untie," which came to mean "free from obligations." Here it refers to ceremonially defiling sacred places (cf. Ezek. 7:21,22[twice]; 23:39; 24:21; Lev. 21:12,23). The temple was YHWH's house and the place of His dwelling. To disregard it was to disregard Him (cf. Ezek. 23:36-45, esp. Ezek. 44:39).

44:8b
NASB, NRSV, JPSOA, NET  "for you"
Peshitta  "for yourselves"

The end of verse 8 is uncertain.

  1. MT, "for you" ‒ לכם
  2. "therefore" ‒ לכן

The UBS Text Project, p. 176, gives option #1 a "C" rating (considerable doubt).

entries.title: Ezekiel 44:10
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
44:10 Some Levites were excluded because of their idolatry (cf. Ezek. 44:12; chapters 8-10). Also Ezekiel goes back to the days of Solomon when he excluded the priestly line of Abiathar from ministering in the temple. Ezekiel extends this ban (cf. Ezek. 44:15).

The other members of the tribe of Levi were to be temple servants with the responsibility of

  1. being gate keepers, Ezek. 44:11
  2. accepting the sacrifices of the people, Ezek. 44:11
  3. slaughtering and butchering the sacrifices brought by the people, Ezek. 44:11
  4. not approaching YHWH's altar or holy things, Ezek. 44:13
  5. keeping charge of the temple (implying the daily activities of cleaning, preparation, and maintenance), Ezek. 44:14

entries.title: Ezekiel 44:12 "I have sworn against them"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 44:12 "I have sworn against them" This is literally "lifted up My hand." See note at Ezek. 20:5.

entries.title: Ezekiel 44:13 "abominations"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 44:13 "abominations" See Special Topic: Abomination (OT)

entries.title: Ezekiel 44:15 "sons of Zadok"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
44:15 "sons of Zadok" This designation goes back to David's day. As king he had two high priests (cf. 2 Sam. 8:17; 19:11; 20:25).

  1. Zadok, son of Ahitub
  2. Ahimelech, son of Abiathar

However, the line of Abiathar was involved in the attempted coup of David's son Adonijah and was removed from office by Solomon (cf. 1 Kgs. 2:35).

Remember, Ezekiel was of the line of Zadok, while Jeremiah was of the line of Abiathar.

▣ "fat and blood" These two items refer to the entire sacrificial system. They were the parts of the animals put on the altar of sacrifice.

  1. The fat of the entrails was burnt
  2. The blood was
    1. placed on the horns of the altar
    2. poured out at the base

entries.title: Ezekiel 44:15-27
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
44:15-27 Here is a list of what the faithful Zadokian priests can and cannot do.

  Accepted Actions Forbidden Actions
1.  wear linen garments  could not wear wool while ministering
2.  leave garments in the holy place  do not wear holy garments into the outer courts
3.  only trim their hair  no shaved heads nor long hair
4.   no wine while on duty in the inner court 
5.   marry virgins from Israel or the widow of a priest not to marry a widow or divorced woman 
6.  teach laws related to ceremonial purity (as a priest this was very important to Ezekiel, Lev. 10:10-11; 14:57; Ezek. 22:26)  
7.  judge according to God's revealed law  
8.  keep all laws themselves  
9.   not touch a dead person except in rare, special cases of compassionate necessity and then be excluded from service until a period of cleansing

This list was a literary way of asserting that the Mosaic covenant was reestablished!

entries.title: Ezekiel 44:18 "turbans"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
44:18 "turbans" This term (BDB 802) refers to the headgear of all priests (cf. Exod. 28:40; 39:28), not the special miter of the High Priest.

▣ "linen undergarments" The Israelite priests were to be modestly clothed (i.e. Exod. 20:26), which was in contradistinction to the ritual nudity of Mesopotamian religions (NIDOTTE, vol. 2, p. 891). Israel was to be distinct from the surrounding polytheistic religions of the Ancient Near East.

▣ "sweat" From a Mosaic perspective, any bodily fluids made one ceremonially unclean. Ezekiel is very concerned with ceremonial purity. As a trained priest his vision of a future symbolic temple and its staff and procedures must conform to the details of the Mosaic legislation.

entries.title: Ezekiel 44:20 "they shall not shave their heads"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
44:20 "they shall not shave their heads" This is a Hebrew grammatical form which intensifies an action (i.e. IMPERFECT VERB and INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE of the same stem – BDB 493, KB 490). Here it means not just "clip," but do not shave the hair of the head. This term is found only here in the OT. This forbidden action is related to Lev. 21:5; Deut. 14:1, which denoted pagan rituals and/or practices. Much of the Levitical legislation can be understood as

  1. limiting contact with Canaanite culture
  2. a way of differentiating between the common and the holy.

entries.title: Ezekiel 44:21
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
44:21 This prohibition goes back to Lev. 10. The death of Aaron's two sons.

Special Topic: Wine and Strong Drink

entries.title: Ezekiel 44:28 "I am their inheritance"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
44:28 "I am their inheritance" The MT has only one negative in this verse (i.e. LXX, Peshitta, NKJV, NRSV, NET) but some English translations follow the Vulgate, which has two negatives (i.e. RSV, NEB, REB, NJB). The UBS Text Project, p. 177, gives the MT an "A" rating (very high probability).

The priests and Levites did not receive a part of the original land allotment (cf. Joshua 12-19), only special cities (cf. Joshua 20-21). They were to serve YHWH and trust Him for their provisions. He was their inheritance (cf. Num. 18:20; Deut. 10:9; 18:1,2; Josh. 13:14,33; 18:7).

Special Topic: Believers' Inheritance

Special Topic: Cities of Refuge

entries.title: Ezekiel 44:29
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
44:29 The regulations are first stated in Lev. 5:14-6:7; 7:1-7.

SPECIAL TOPIC: Sacrificial Systems of the ANE

entries.title: Ezekiel 44:30 "the first of all"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 44:30 "the first of all" This offering is described in Num. 18:12; 2 Chr. 31:4-6; Neh. 10:35-37. It was a tangible way of thanking God for the bountiful produce of the land. It symbolized His ownership of the land and His control of its fertility.

entries.title: Ezekiel 45:1 "when you divide by lot the land"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
45:1 "when you divide by lot the land" The VERB (BDB 656, KB 709, Hiphil INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT) basically means "to fall," but in the Hiphil refers to casting lots to know the Lord's will on a matter. The concept (i.e. mechanism) originated with the Urim and Thummim of the High Priest (cf. Exod. 28:30; Num. 27:21). This method was to be used to divide the Promised Land (i.e. Canaan) among the twelve tribes (excluding Levi) as described in Num. 26:53-56; 33:54; 34:2,13; 36:2-3 and originally done in Joshua 13-22 (esp. 14:1-2). Ezekiel is drawing a mental image from the past to illustrate a new beginning!

Special Topic: Urim and Thummim

▣ "an allotment to the Lord" The phrase is literally "set apart an offering" (BDB 926, KB 1202, Hiphil IMPERFECT). This refers to the temple area.

This offering/allotment is described in Ezek. 45:1-5.

  1. length, 25,000 cubits or rods/reeds (cf. Ezek. 42:15-20)
  2. width, 10,000 cubits (LXX, 20,000) or rods/reeds, which means it includes the priestly and Levitical areas
  3. containing a square 500 cubits by 500 cubits or rods/reeds for the holy place
  4. square surrounded by an open space of 50 cubits or rods/reeds
  5. contains YHWH's sanctuary and priests' housing
  6. area for the Levites (25,000 cubits by 10,000 cubits or rods/reeds)

A cubit would be about 21 inches, a rod/reed about 10 feet.

Special Topic: Cubit

NASB, NRSV, NJB, REB, LXX  "20,000"
NKJV, JPSOA, Peshitta  "10,000"

The MT has "10,000." The UBS Text Project, p. 178, suggests that the text of the LXX be followed but gives it only a "C" rating (considerable doubt).

45:5
NASB, NRSV, RSV, NEB, LXX  "cities"
NKJV, JPSOA  "chambers"
TEV, NJB  "towns"
Peshitta  "houses"
REB  "places in which they live"

The MT has "chambers" (לשכת, BDB 545), which is so common in this section of Ezekiel (cf. Ezek. 40:17 [twice], 38,44,45,46; 41:10; 42:1,4,7 [twice],8,11), but the Septuagint has "cities," reflecting the Hebrew word (לשבת). The B (beth) and K (kaph) consonants are formed in a similar way and are often confused in handwritten texts. The UBS Text Project, p. 178, gives "cities" a "C" rating (considerable doubt).

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

  1. First paragraph
  2. Second paragraph
  3. Third paragraph, etc.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Ezekiel 45:6 "the city"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 45:6 "the city" This area (5,000 by 25,000 cubits) is further described in Ezek. 48:15-18,30-35. It is a holy area for all the house of Israel, similar to the courts of Herod's temple.

entries.title: Ezekiel 45:7-8 "The prince shall have land"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
45:7-8 "The prince shall have land" The allotment for the royal leader is described in Ezek. 45:7-8, which is adjacent to the holy common area for the people.

The purpose of the land is twofold.

  1. symbolizes closeness to YHWH
  2. symbolizes he is a servant of the people (i.e. outside the common area)

It is also a way of providing status and authority without oppressing the people (cf. Ezek. 45:9; 22:27; 46:18).

This "prince" (BDB 672) is an administrator fulfilling Isa. 9:6-7 and Micah 5:2-5. However, the "princes" (cf. Ezek. 45:8,9) are governmental leaders who must be admonished to live and act appropriately. Ezekiel takes seriously the corruption of the leadership which occurred regularly in the past. This very point shows that this does not directly refer to an "ideal Messianic" period, but future Israeli history. The results of the fall potentially continue and must be guarded against. See full note on "prince" at Ezek. 46:2.

entries.title: Ezekiel 45:9-10
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
45:9-10 These verses list what the governmental leaders should and should not do.

  1. put away violence (BDB 329) and oppression (BDB 994) – BDB 693, KB 747, Hiphil IMPERATIVE PLURAL
  2. practice justice (BDB 1048) and righteousness (BDB 842) – BDB 793, KB 889, Qal IMPERATIVE (terms often paired, cf. Ezek. 18:5,19,21,27; 33:14,16,19)
  3. stop your expropriations (BDB 177, literally, "lift your evictions") – BDB 926, KB 1202, Hiphil IMPERATIVE
  4. have just balances, ephah and baths – BDB 224, KB 243, Qal JUSSIVE

entries.title: Ezekiel 45:11-12,14
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 45:11-12,14 See Special Topic: Ancient Near Eastern Weights and Measures (metrology).

entries.title: Ezekiel 45:13-16
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
45:13-16 These verses describe what an Israelite worshiper should provide (either in kind or as a tax).

  1. a sixth of an ephah (dry measure) from a homer of wheat
  2. a sixth of an ephah from a homer of barley (cf. Num. 5:15)
  3. a bath (liquid measure) of oil
  4. one sheep

which will make up

  1. a grain offering (Leviticus 2)
  2. a burnt offering (Leviticus 1)
  3. a peace offering (Leviticus 3)

Special Topic: ANE Weights and Volumes

entries.title: Ezekiel 45:17
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
45:17 The prince (i.e. government) shall provide the offerings.

  1. the burnt offering
  2. the grain offering
  3. the drink offering

for the feasts of

  1. new moons
  2. sabbaths
  3. appointed feasts

to make atonement (cf. Ezek. 45:15)

  1. the sin offering
  2. the grain offering
  3. the burnt offering
  4. the peace offering (often used to inaugurate a temple, cf. Lev. 9:4,18,22; 1 Kgs. 8:63-64; 2 Chr. 30:22; 31:2; Ezek. 43:27)

Special Topic: Feasts of Israel

Special Topic: Atonement

entries.title: Ezekiel 45:18-25
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
45:18-25 The lists of feasts (the year begins in the spring):

  Verse(s) Month Day Parallel Texts
1. Ezek. 45:18-19 1st month 1st day Num. 28:11-15
2. Ezek. 45:20 1st month 9th day Leviticus 16
3. Ezek. 45:21-24 1st month 14th day Lev. 23:5; Num. 28:16-25
4. Ezek. 45:21-24 1st month 15th-21st days Lev. 23:6
5. Ezek. 45:25 7th month 15th-21st days Lev. 23:33-37; Numbers 29; Deut. 16:13-15

Even though #2 has elements of the Day of Atonement, probably Ezek. 45:18-20 reflect the New Year Feast, while Ezek. 45:21-24 reflect Passover/Unleavened Bread and Ezek. 45:25 reflects the Feast of Booths/Tabernacles.

The last of this chapter and the next is the section that disagrees so much with the Mosaic regulation. The question is why. Ezekiel was a priest. He knew the law of Moses. I think that the differences and exaggerated land dimensions are a way to denote its symbolic nature (it is similar to John listing the tribes incorrectly in Revelation 7). Only literalists demand a future temple!

Special Topic: Feasts of Israel

entries.title: Ezekiel 46:1 "the gate of the inner court facing east"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
46:1 "the gate of the inner court facing east" Remember the outer eastern gate was permanently sealed (cf. Ezek. 44:2) because this is the gate by which YHWH left the temple (cf. Ezekiel 10) and returned (cf. Ezekiel 43).

▣ "the new moon" This monthly feast is first mentioned in Num. 10:10 and explained in Num. 28:11-15. It is referred to in Ps. 81:3-5 and Ezek. 45:18; 46:3,6. Since the tabernacle was set up on the first day of the month (cf. Exod. 40:2,17), it is possible that it is connected to this event.

The Jews used a lunar calendar.

Special Topic: ANE Calendars

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Ezekiel 46:2 "his burnt offerings and his peace offerings"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
46:2 "his burnt offerings and his peace offerings" Also note, verse 12 lists several other offerings.

Special Topic: Burnt Offering

Special Topic: Peace Offering

Special Topic: Sacrificial Systems of the Ancient Near East

▣ "he shall worship" This is an unusual form of a common religious concept of "worship" or "bow down" (BDB 1005, KB 295 II, Histaphel PERFECT with waw).

The basic stem seems to be חוה (KB 295 II), which in Ugaritic means "to prostrate oneself in worship" or שחה, "to bow down" (BDB 1005). It occurs three times in this paragraph (cf. Ezek. 46:2,3,9).

The prince has a special place at the gateway of the inner court where he can see the sacrificing being made, but cannot enter the sacred precincts of the priests.

Special Topic: Worship

▣ "the gate shall not be shut" This is imagery of access and availability (cf. Isa. 60:11; Rev. 21:25). YHWH would receive the prince and the people in regular worship at all times.

▣ "the prince" This future Davidic leader ("prince," BDB 672) is mentioned several times in Ezekiel.

  1. YHWH will establish him as shepherd over a united covenant people, Ezek. 34:20-24
  2. YHWH will restore the covenant people to their land and restore their Davidic prince. He will make an everlasting covenant of peace with an obedient Israel, Ezek. 37:24-28
  3. he will eat/worship before YHWH in the new temple, Ezek. 44:2-3; 46:1-12
  4. he shall receive a large special land allotment (i.e. great wealth) on both sides of the temple area to keep him from oppressing the people, Ezek. 45:7-8; 48:21-22
  5. the people will give offerings to the prince so that he can provide sacrifices on special days, Ezek. 45:13-25
  6. regulations about inheritance gifts given by the prince, Ezek. 46:16-18

entries.title: Ezekiel 46:4 "without blemish"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
46:4 "without blemish" This term (BDB 1071) denotes an animal that is healthy and without obvious defect. In other words, it is a prime example (typical) of its breed in color, shape, and size (i.e. Exod. 12:5; Lev. 3:1).

Special Topic: Blameless, Innocent, Guiltless, Without Reproach

entries.title: Ezekiel 46:4-7
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
46:4-7 The prince shall offer

  1. the sabbath
    1. six lambs
    2. one ram
    3. one ephah of grain (with ram)
    4. as much as able of grain (with the lambs)
    5. a hin of oil
  2. new moon
    1. a young bull
    2. six lambs
    3. a ram
    4. one ephah of grain (with bull)
    5. one ephah of grain (with ram)
    6. as much as able of grain (with lambs)
    7. a hin of oil

entries.title: Ezekiel 46:5 "ephah. . .hin"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
46:5 "ephah. . .hin" See Special Topic: ANE Weights and Volumes (metrology).

46:7
NASB  "as much as he is able"
NKJV, TEV  "as much as he wants to give"
NRSV  "as much as he wishes"
NJB  "what he pleases"
LXX  "according as his hand can furnish"
Peshitta, JPSOA, REB  "as much as he can afford"

The literal phrase is "as much as his hand can reach." The amount of sacrifices depended on two things.

  1. the free-will offerings of the people
  2. the wealth and/or ability and/or desire of the monarch

entries.title: Ezekiel 46:9
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 46:9 There were great crowds of people at the temple during the feast days. The procedure of verse 9 was to help with the congestion.

entries.title: Ezekiel 46:10
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
46:10 The prince has a special place to observe the sacrifices on the "special" days (i.e. appointed feasts), but on other days he was not allowed even this special place, but must enter and exit with other covenant people.

46:13
NASB, NKJV, REB  "you"
NRSV, NJB, LXX, Peshitta, Vulgate  "he"

The MT has "you," but ancient translations (and some Hebrew MSS) understood it as a reference to "the prince" (same in Ezek. 46:14).

▣ "morning by morning" This refers to the "continual" (i.e. post-exilic designation), which was a lamb offered every morning and evening at the temple (cf. Exod. 29:38-42; Num. 28:3-4; 2 Kgs. 16:15). This continued in the time of Jesus.

entries.title: Ezekiel 46:14 "a perpetual ordinance"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
46:14 "a perpetual ordinance" The Hebrew term "forever" (עולמ, BDB 761) is used in several senses as the Special Topic shows and must be interpreted in each context.

Special Topic: Forever ('olam and aiōnios)

entries.title: Ezekiel 46:17 "the year of liberty"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
46:17 "the year of liberty" This refers to the "year of Jubilee" (cf. Lev. 25:8-17, esp. Ezek. 46:10), in which the land returns to its original tribal owners because the land was a gift from YHWH (cf. Joshua 13-23).

Special Topic: Feasts of Israel, II. C.

entries.title: Ezekiel 46:18
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
46:18 This verse links to Ezek. 45:8, where the prince is given a large section of land to keep him from taking common land from the people.

This shows that "the prince" was understood as a person still affected by Genesis 3. This would not fit a NT understanding of "Messiah" (this is also true of Isa. 42:1 vs. 42:18-19). Oppression was often associated with the kingship (cf. Ezek. 18:7,12,16).

entries.title: Ezekiel 46:19-20
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
46:19-20 This refers to the place where the priests prepared

  1. items to be offered
  2. items for them to eat

This food was holy and had to be prepared and eaten in a special holy place (cf. Ezek. 35:11-13)

entries.title: Ezekiel 46:20
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 46:20 See the same emphasis in Ezek. 44:19.

entries.title: Ezekiel 46:22 "corners. . .enclosed"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
46:22 "corners. . .enclosed" Both of these words are uncertain.

  1. "corners" ‒ the VERB (BDB 893) is found only here in the OT. Many OT scholars assume it is a Hophal PARTICIPLE. The NOUN is found in Ezek. 26:24; 36:29; 46:21 (twice). It could refer to a corner post. Many of Ezekiel's architectural terms are rare and uncertain.
  2. "enclosed" ‒ BDB 883 (קטר) could also mean "vaulted" or "covered" (NEB, REB). JPSOA has "uncovered" or "unroofed," following the Mishnah (Middoth 2.5). The Septuagint assumes a different stem (קטנות), "smaller" (BDB 881-882), and is followed by Peshitta, NRSV, TEV, and NJB or possibly "the same size" (NEB, JPSOA footnote. REB).

 

Copyright © 2014 Bible Lessons International

entries.title: Ezekiel 47:1 "water was flowing"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
47:1 "water was flowing" For desert people water was a sign of God's blessing and presence (i.e. Joel 3:18). The eschatological sense is present in Zech. 13:1 and 14:8. It is used by John in Rev. 22:1,17. The covenant promises of Deuteronomy 27-30 have become a reality!

This is imagery (cf. Ps. 46:4; 65:9) and not meant to be taken literally. It conveys

  1. original creation
  2. Eden (see Special Topic: Eden)
  3. covenant promises

Special Topic: Waters

entries.title: Ezekiel 47:3 "the man"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
47:3 "the man" This is the interpreting angel of Ezek. 40:3. This measuring angel is also mentioned by John in Revelation 21.

Special Topic: Apocalyptic Literature

entries.title: Ezekiel 47:7 "many trees on the one side and the other"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 47:7 "many trees on the one side and the other" This is imagery for fertility (cf. Ezek. 47:12). This imagery is also used by John in Revelation 22.

entries.title: Ezekiel 47:8
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 47:8 Many commentators have asserted that this verse refers to a miraculous change of saltwater to fresh water, but it seems to me that it refers to the abundance of waters that fill up the Arabah depression and overflow it.

entries.title: Ezekiel 47:13
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 47:13 This is the beginning of the reallocation of the land (i.e. Joshua 12-23).

entries.title: Ezekiel 47:14 "each one equally"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
47:14 "each one equally" In Joshua the land was divided according to the size of the individual tribes.

▣ "for I swore to give it to your forefathers" This reflects the promises to the Patriarchs beginning in Genesis 12 and 15.

Special Topic: Covenant Promises to the Patriarchs

entries.title: Ezekiel 47:15-20
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 47:15-20 The southern boundaries are close to Joshua' boundaries (cf. Num. 34:1-12) and the kingdoms of David and Solomon, but the northern part is expanded northward and eastward as far as Hamath and including most of Syria.

entries.title: Ezekiel 47:22 "aliens"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
47:22 "aliens" This is the one section of the book that seems to be inclusive instead of exclusive. This is similar to Isa. 56:3-8 and follows the pattern of Lev. 24:22 and Num. 15:29.

  1. First paragraph
  2. Second paragraph
  3. Third paragraph, etc.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

  1. Judah to the north and Benjamin to the south are closest to the central sanctuary. The "prince" has the land to the east and west of it.

  2. These tribal divisions are unrelated to the divisions found in Joshua 12-23.

  3. The children of Jacob's wives' servants are farthest from the sanctuary.

  4. Ezekiel describes the gates of the city of Jerusalem and how they relate to specific tribes. John, in Revelation 21, draws on this imagery. See my latest exegetical verse-by-verse commentary on Revelation (2024).

  5. The imagery denotes a complete new covenant start. Jacob's descendants are to begin again!

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Ezekiel 48:35 "The Lord is there"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
48:35 "The Lord is there" This reflects the covenant promise of YHWH's personal presence with His people. The same concept is expressed by the name "Emmanuel" (God is with us).

The exile is over! YHWH has returned!
